title.zh: 卷77 宋翻 辛雄 羊深 楊機 高崇
title.en: Volume 77: Song Fan, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yang Ji, Gao Chong
title.raw: 卷77 宋翻 辛雄 羊深 楊機 高崇 Volume 77: Song Fan, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yang Ji, Gao Chong

sentences.zh: 宋翻 辛雄 羊深 楊機 高崇

translations.literal: Song Fan, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yang Ji, and Gao Chong
translations.idiomatic: Song Fan, Xin Xiong, Yang Shen, Yang Ji, and Gao Chong

sentences.zh: 宋翻，字飛烏，廣平列人人也，吏部尚書弁族弟。

translations.literal: Song Fan, courtesy name Feiwu, was a native of Lie in Guangping and a cousin of Bian, Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Song Fan, whose courtesy name was Feiwu, came from Lie in Guangping and was a cousin of Bian, the Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 少有操尚，世人以剛斷許之。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed moral integrity; the world credited him with firm decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held himself to high standards, and contemporaries regarded him as resolute and decisive.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，起家奉朝請，本州治中、廣平王郎中令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he first entered office as a court gentleman, then served as provincial aide and director of retainers for the Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong first took the throne, Fan began his career as a court gentleman, then became provincial aide and director of retainers for the Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 尋拜河陰令。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 翻弟道璵，先為冀州京兆王愉法曹行參軍，愉反，逼道璵為官，翻與弟世景俱囚廷尉。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Daoyu had earlier served as acting aide in the law office for Prince Xu of Jingzhao in Jizhou; when Xu rebelled he forced Daoyu to take office, and Fan together with his brother Shijing were both imprisoned by the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Daoyu had previously been acting aide in the law office of Prince Xu of Jingzhao in Jizhou. When Xu rebelled he compelled Daoyu to serve; Fan and his brother Shijing were both detained by the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 道璵後棄愉歸罪京師，猶坐身死，翻、世景除名。

translations.literal: Daoyu later abandoned Xu and returned to the capital to accept punishment, yet was still sentenced to death; Fan and Shijing were struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu later deserted Xu and came back to the capital to submit to judgment, but was still condemned to death; Fan and Shijing were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜翻治書侍御史、洛陽令、中散大夫、相州大中正，猶領治書。

translations.literal: After a long interval Fan was appointed investigating censor, magistrate of Luoyang, Palace Attendant, and chief arbiter of Xiangzhou, while still holding the post of investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Fan was made investigating censor, magistrate of Luoyang, Palace Attendant, and chief arbiter of Xiangzhou, and continued to serve as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 又遷左將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to General of the Left and governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to General of the Left and governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍遣將先據荊山，規將寇竊。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent generals who first seized Jingshan, intending to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yan dispatched generals who first occupied Jingshan, planning an incursion.

sentences.zh: 屬壽春淪陷，賊遂乘勢徑趨項城。

translations.literal: When Shouchun fell, the enemy took advantage of the momentum and pressed straight toward Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun was lost, the rebels rode the tide of victory and marched directly on Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 翻遣將成僧達潛軍討襲，頻戰破之，自是州境帖然。

translations.literal: Fan sent the general Cheng Sengda with a hidden force to strike them, repeatedly defeating them in battle, and from then on the province was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Fan sent General Cheng Sengda with troops in concealment to attack them, won repeated victories, and thereafter the province was at peace.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，除司徒左長史、撫軍將軍、河南尹。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was appointed chief steward of the left in the Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the Army, and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Xiaozhuang he was made chief steward of the left in the Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the Army, and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，翻為河陰令，順陽公主家奴為劫，攝而不送，翻將兵圍主宅，執主壻馮穆，步驅向縣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan was magistrate of Heyin, a household slave of the Princess of Shunyang committed robbery; she detained him and would not hand him over. Fan led troops to surround the princess's residence, seized her son-in-law Feng Mu, and drove him on foot toward the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan had been magistrate of Heyin, a slave in the household of the Princess of Shunyang committed robbery; she held him and refused to surrender him. Fan surrounded the princess's mansion with soldiers, seized her son-in-law Feng Mu, and marched him on foot to the county yamen.

sentences.zh: 時正炎暑，立之日中，流汗霑地。

translations.literal: It was the height of summer heat; he made him stand in the midday sun until sweat soaked the ground.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer; he made him stand in the noonday sun until sweat pooled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有大枷，時人號曰「彌尾青」，及翻為縣主，吏請焚之。

translations.literal: The county had long possessed a great cangue that people nicknamed "Mawei Qing"; when Fan became magistrate the clerks asked to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long kept a great cangue that people called "Mawei Qing"; when Fan took office the clerks asked to burn it.

sentences.zh: 翻曰：「且置南牆下，以待豪家。」

translations.literal: Fan said, "For now set it beneath the south wall to await great families."
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Leave it for now under the south wall, to await the great houses."

sentences.zh: 未幾，有內監楊小駒詣縣請事，辭色不遜，命取尾青以鎮之。

translations.literal: Before long the inner attendant Yang Xiaoju came to the county on business with insolent words and manner; Fan ordered the "tail-green" taken to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the eunuch supervisor Yang Xiaoju came to the county on business with rude speech and bearing; Fan ordered the cangue brought to hold him.

sentences.zh: 既免，入訴於世宗。

translations.literal: Once released, he went in to complain to Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: After he was released he went to lodge a complaint with Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 世宗大怒，敕河南尹推治其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered the governor of Henan to investigate and punish the offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered the governor of Henan to investigate and punish the crime.

sentences.zh: 翻具自陳狀。

translations.literal: Fan set forth the full facts in his own statement.
translations.idiomatic: Fan presented a full account in his own words.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿故違朝法，豈不欲作威以買名？」

translations.literal: An edict said, "You deliberately violated court law—did you not wish to make a display of power to buy a reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "You knowingly violated the law of the court. Did you not mean to throw your weight about and purchase a name for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 翻對：「造者非臣，買名者亦宜非臣。

translations.literal: Fan replied, "The one who made it was not your servant, and the one who would buy a name ought not to be your servant either.
translations.idiomatic: Fan answered, "Your servant did not make it, and your servant is not one who would buy a name.

sentences.zh: 所以留者，非敢施於百姓，欲待兇暴之徒如小駒者耳。」

translations.literal: The reason I kept it was that I did not dare apply it to common people but wished to await violent fellows like Xiaoju."
translations.idiomatic: I kept it because I did not dare use it on ordinary people, but meant to keep it for brutal men like Xiaoju."

sentences.zh: 於是威振京師。

translations.literal: From then on his authority shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his awe-inspiring reputation spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 及為洛陽，迄於為尹，畏憚權勢，更相承接，故當世之名大致減損。

translations.literal: When he served in Luoyang and down to his tenure as governor, he feared and respected power and constantly deferred to it, so his contemporary fame was largely diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Once he served in Luoyang and through his time as governor, he feared the powerful and kept yielding to them, and so his standing in his own day was largely reduced.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he died in his post.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、衞將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, General of the Guard, and governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, General of the Guard, and governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，重贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書左僕射、雍州刺史，諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he was again posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, equal rank with the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu first ascended the throne, Fan was again posthumously made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 子思遠，卒於司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son Siyuan died while serving as aide in the office of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Siyuan died in the post of aide in the office of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 翻弟毓，字道和，敦篤有志行。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Daohe, was sincere and possessed resolve and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Yu, whose courtesy name was Daohe, was earnest and steadfast in purpose and conduct.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: He held the ranks of General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Service.

sentences.zh: 子世軌，齊文襄王大將軍府祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Shigui was libationer in the great general's staff of Qi's Prince Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shigui served as libationer in the great general's staff of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 毓弟世景，在良吏傳。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Shijing is treated in the biography of good officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Shijing appears in the biography of good officials.

sentences.zh: 世景弟叔集，亦有學行。

translations.literal: Shijing's younger brother Shuji also possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing's younger brother Shuji likewise had learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 征東裴衍之討葛榮也，表為員外散騎侍郎，引同戎役。

translations.literal: When Pei Yan marched east to suppress Ge Rong, he memorialized Shuji as supernumerary gentleman attendant at the palace gate and took him along on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yan campaigned east against Ge Rong, he recommended Shuji as supernumerary gentleman attendant at the palace gate and brought him on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 及衍敗，同時遇害。

translations.literal: When Yan was defeated, Shuji perished at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was defeated, Shuji was killed along with him.

sentences.zh: 叔集弟道璵，少而敏儁。

translations.literal: Shuji's younger brother Daoyu was clever and outstanding from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Shuji's younger brother Daoyu was clever and brilliant from youth.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，以才學被召，與祕書丞孫惠蔚典校羣書，考正同異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was summoned for talent and learning, and together with Secretariat Director Sun Huiwei collated the books and corrected discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he was called up for his scholarship and, with Secretariat Director Sun Huiwei, supervised the collation of the books and corrected errors.

sentences.zh: 自太學博士轉京兆王愉法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: From Erudite of the Imperial Academy he was transferred to acting aide in the law office for Prince Xu of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from Erudite of the Imperial Academy to acting aide in the law office of Prince Xu of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 臨死，作詩及挽歌詞，寄之親朋，以見怨痛。

translations.literal: Facing death he composed poems and dirges and sent them to kin and friends to show his grief and pain.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of death he wrote poems and dirges and sent them to relatives and friends to express his anguish.

sentences.zh: 道璵又曾贈著作佐郎張始均詩，其末章云：「子深懷璧憂，余有當門病。」

translations.literal: Daoyu had also once presented a poem to Zhang Shijun, assistant editor in the History Office; its closing lines read, "Zi bears the worry of a jade in his bosom; I have the ailment of a tree before the gate."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu had also once given a poem to Zhang Shijun, assistant editor in the History Office, whose final stanza ran, "You carry the worry of a jade in your breast; I have the sickness of a tree before the gate."

sentences.zh: 道璵既不免難，始均亦遇世禍，時咸怪之。

translations.literal: After Daoyu could not escape disaster, Shijun also met with worldly calamity, and at the time all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyu could not escape his fate, Shijun also suffered calamity in the world, and contemporaries all found it strange.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄毓以第三子子叔繼。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his elder brother Yu made his third son Zishu his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons; his elder brother Yu had his third son Zishu succeed him.

sentences.zh: 辛雄，字世賓，隴西狄道人。

translations.literal: Xin Xiong, courtesy name Shibin, was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong, whose courtesy name was Shibin, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父暢，字幼達，大將軍諮議參軍、汝南鄉郡二郡太守，太和中，本郡中正。

translations.literal: His father Chang, courtesy name Youda, was staff adviser to the great general and governor of two commanderies, Runan and Xiang; in the Taihe era he was chief arbiter of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang, courtesy name Youda, had been staff adviser to the great general and governor of the commanderies of Runan and Xiang; in the Taihe period he was chief arbiter of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 雄有孝性，頗涉書史，好刑名，廉謹雅素，不妄交友，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Xiong was filial by nature, broadly read in histories, fond of penal law, frugal and careful, refined and plain, not making friends lightly, and not letting joy or anger show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was filial by nature, well versed in historical writings, devoted to penal law, frugal and scrupulous, refined and unadorned, careful in friendship, and never betraying emotion on his face.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the robe he became a court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering office he became a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父於郡遇患，雄自免歸，晨夜扶抱。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill in his commandery, Xiong resigned of his own accord and returned, supporting and embracing him morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill while serving in his commandery, Xiong asked to be relieved and went home, attending him day and night.

sentences.zh: 及父喪居憂，殆不可識，為世所稱。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning until he was scarcely recognizable, and the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he grieved until he was scarcely recognizable, and the world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除給事中，十年不遷職，乃以病免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed gentleman attendant at the palace gate; for ten years he received no promotion and then resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhengshi era he was made gentleman attendant at the palace gate; for ten years he was not promoted and then left office citing illness.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌為司空，辟戶曹參軍，攝田曹事。

translations.literal: When Prince Qinghe Yi became Minister of Works, he recruited Xiong as aide in the household bureau and put him in charge of the fields bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qinghe Yi became Minister of Works, he engaged Xiong as aide in the household bureau and had him oversee the fields bureau.

sentences.zh: 懌遷司徒，仍隨授戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Yi became Minister of Education, Xiong was again appointed aide in the household bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became Minister of Education, Xiong was again made aide in the household bureau.

sentences.zh: 並當煩劇，諍訟填委。

translations.literal: Both posts were taxing and contentious suits piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Both duties were onerous and lawsuits overflowed the desk.

sentences.zh: 雄用心平直，加以閑明政事，經其斷割，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Xiong's mind was fair and direct, and added to his familiarity with government affairs; cases that passed through his judgment left none displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong applied himself with impartiality, and together with his mastery of administration, every case he decided won approval.

sentences.zh: 懌重之，每謂人曰：「必也無訟乎，辛雄其有焉。」

translations.literal: Yi valued him and often told others, "If there must be no litigation, perhaps Xin Xiong can achieve it."
translations.idiomatic: Yi held him in esteem and often said to others, "If there could truly be no lawsuits, perhaps Xin Xiong could bring that about."

sentences.zh: 由是名顯。

translations.literal: From this his name became known.
translations.idiomatic: By this his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 懌遷太尉，又為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Yi became Grand Commandant, Xiong again served as recorder in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became Grand Commandant, Xiong again served as recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，除尚書駕部郎中，轉三公郎。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was appointed director in the chariot office of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to gentleman of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui period he was made director in the chariot office of the Department of State Affairs and then transferred to gentleman of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 其年，沙汰郎官，唯雄與羊深等八人見留，餘悉罷遣，更授李琰等。

translations.literal: That year the gentlemen were culled; only Xiong and Yang Shen among eight were retained, the rest all dismissed and replaced by Li Yan and others.
translations.idiomatic: That year the corps of gentlemen was winnowed; only Xiong, Yang Shen, and six others were kept, while the rest were all dismissed and Li Yan and others were appointed in their place.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史中尉、東平王元匡復欲輿棺諫諍，尚書令、任城王澄劾匡大不敬，詔恕死為民。

translations.literal: Earlier, the censor-in-chief, Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang, again wished to carry a coffin and remonstrate; the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, impeached Kuang for great disrespect, and an edict spared his life but reduced him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the censor-in-chief, Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang, had again wished to present remonstrance with a coffin; the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, impeached Kuang for grave disrespect, and an edict spared his life but stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 雄奏理匡曰：「竊惟白衣元匡，歷奉三朝，每蒙寵遇。

translations.literal: Xiong memorialized in Kuang's defense, saying, "I venture to consider the commoner Yuan Kuang, who has served three reigns and each time received favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong submitted a memorial arguing for Kuang: "I respectfully consider the commoner Yuan Kuang, who has served three reigns and repeatedly received imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 謇諤之性，簡自帝心；

translations.literal: His forthright and outspoken nature was singled out by the emperor's own heart;
translations.idiomatic: His blunt, remonstrating character was known to the emperor himself;

sentences.zh: 鷹鸇之志，形於在昔。

translations.literal: his hawk-and-falcon resolve was manifest in days past.
translations.idiomatic: his fierce, loyal spirit had long been plain to see.

sentences.zh: 故高祖錫之以匡名，陛下任之以彈糾。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Gaozu bestowed on him the name Kuang, and Your Majesty entrusted him with impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Gaozu gave him the name Kuang, and Your Majesty charged him with impeachment.

sentences.zh: 至若茹皓昇輦，匡斥宜下之言；

translations.literal: When Ru Hao ascended the carriage, Kuang rebuked him with words that such a man ought to step down;
translations.idiomatic: When Ru Hao rode in the imperial carriage, Kuang spoke words demanding that he descend;

sentences.zh: 高肇當政，匡陳擅權之表。

translations.literal: when Gao Zhao held power, Kuang submitted a memorial on usurped authority.
translations.idiomatic: when Gao Zhao dominated the government, Kuang filed a memorial on his monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 剛毅忠款，羣臣莫及；

translations.literal: His firmness, loyalty, and sincerity none among the ministers could match;
translations.idiomatic: In firmness, loyalty, and sincerity no minister could equal him;

sentences.zh: 骨鯁之跡，朝野共知。

translations.literal: his uncompromising conduct was known alike in court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: his unyielding conduct was known throughout court and realm.

sentences.zh: 當高肇之時，匡造棺致諫，主聖臣直，卒以無咎。

translations.literal: In Gao Zhao's time Kuang made a coffin and offered remonstrance; the ruler was sage and the minister upright, and in the end he suffered no blame.
translations.idiomatic: In Gao Zhao's day Kuang prepared a coffin and remonstrated; ruler and minister were both upright, and in the end he went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 假欲重造，先帝已容之於前，陛下亦宜寬之於後，況其元列由緒與罪按不同也。

translations.literal: Even if he should make one again, the late emperor already tolerated it before, and Your Majesty should also show leniency afterward, especially as the original grounds and the present charge are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he were to do so again, the late emperor had already indulged it once, and Your Majesty should likewise be indulgent hereafter, especially since the original grounds and the present accusation differ.

sentences.zh: 脫終貶黜，不在朝廷，恐杜忠臣之口，塞諫者之心，乖琴瑟之至和，違鹽梅之相濟。

translations.literal: If in the end he is demoted and no longer in court, I fear it will stop loyal ministers' mouths and block remonstrators' hearts, departing from the perfect harmony of lute and zither and violating the mutual seasoning of salt and plum.
translations.idiomatic: Should he finally be banished from court, I fear loyal mouths will be stopped and remonstrators' hearts sealed, breaking the perfect concord of lute and zither and forsaking the mutual seasoning of salt and plum.

sentences.zh: 祁奚云，叔向之賢，可及十世，而匡不免其身，實可嗟惜。」

translations.literal: Qi Xi said that the worth of Shuxiang could reach ten generations, yet Kuang cannot preserve his own person—this is truly lamentable."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xi said that Shuxiang's worth might extend ten generations, yet Kuang cannot save his own person—a thing truly to be mourned."

sentences.zh: 未幾，匡除龍驤將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Kuang was appointed General of Dragon Cavalry and governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kuang was made General of Dragon Cavalry and governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 右僕射元欽謂左僕射蕭寶夤曰：「至如辛郎中才用，省中諸人莫出其右。」

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director Yuan Qin said to the Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin, "As for Director Xin's talent and ability, none in the department surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Qin said to Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin, "When it comes to Director Xin's talent, no one in the department ranks above him."

sentences.zh: 寶夤曰：「吾聞游僕射云：『得如雄者四五人共治省事，足矣。』

translations.literal: Baoyin said, "I have heard Vice Director You say, 'With four or five men like Xiong to run the department's business together, it would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin replied, "I have heard Vice Director You say that with four or five men like Xiong to manage the department's affairs together, it would suffice.

sentences.zh: 今日之賞，何其晚哉！」

translations.literal: Today's reward—how late it comes!"
translations.idiomatic: Today's recognition—how late in coming!"

sentences.zh: 初，廷尉少卿袁翻以犯罪之人，經恩競訴，枉直難明，遂奏曾染風聞者，不問曲直，推為獄成，悉不斷理。

translations.literal: Earlier, the vice director of the Court of Justice Yuan Fan, because convicted persons after an amnesty competed in appeals so that right and wrong were hard to discern, memorialized that anyone once tainted by rumor, regardless of guilt or innocence, should be treated as a closed case and none further judged.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Director of the Court of Justice Yuan Fan, finding that after amnesties convicted persons flooded the courts with appeals so that guilt and innocence were hard to tell apart, memorialized that anyone who had once been named in rumor, whether guilty or not, should be treated as a finished case and no longer adjudicated.

sentences.zh: 詔令門下、尚書、廷尉議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Chancellery, the Department of State Affairs, and the Court of Justice to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Chancellery, the Department of State Affairs, and the Court of Justice to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 雄議曰：

translations.literal: Xiong's opinion said:
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's opinion read:

sentences.zh: 春秋之義：不幸而失，寧僭不濫。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals: if one must err, better to exceed than to be excessive in leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when judgment must fail, it is better to exceed than to be excessive in leniency.

sentences.zh: 僭則失罪人，濫乃害善人。

translations.literal: Exceeding loses the guilty; leniency harms the good.
translations.idiomatic: Exceeding punishes the innocent guilty; leniency injures the innocent good.

sentences.zh: 今議者不忍罪姦吏，使出入縱情，令君子小人薰蕕不別，豈所謂賞善罰惡，殷勤隱恤者也。

translations.literal: Now the debaters cannot bear to punish corrupt officials, letting them come and go at will, so that gentlemen and petty men are not distinguished as musk-grass from stench-weed—is this what is called rewarding good and punishing evil with earnest, hidden care?
translations.idiomatic: The proponents cannot bear to punish corrupt officials, allowing them to act at will so that gentlemen and petty men are not separated like musk from stench—can this be called rewarding good and punishing evil with conscientious care?

sentences.zh: 仰尋周公不減流言之愆，俯惟釋之不加驚馬之辟，所以小大用情，貴在得所。

translations.literal: Looking up, the Duke of Zhou did not lessen the offense of spreading rumors; looking down, [Zhang] Shi'zhi did not add a penalty for startling the horses—thus great and small are treated according to feeling, and what matters is hitting the mark.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou did not reduce the fault of spreading rumors; Zhang Shizhi did not add a penalty for startling the emperor's horses—great and small are judged by circumstance, and what counts is striking the right measure.

sentences.zh: 失之千里，差在毫釐。

translations.literal: To miss by a thousand li is to differ by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: A miss of a thousand li begins in a hairsbreadth.

sentences.zh: 雄久執按牘，數見疑訟，職掌三千，願言者六。

translations.literal: Xiong long held case files and often saw doubtful suits; in charge of three thousand statutes, six matters call for speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had long handled dossiers and often saw doubtful litigation; charged with three thousand statutes, six points deserve to be stated.

sentences.zh: 一曰：御史所糾，有注其逃走者。

translations.literal: First: in impeachments by the censorate, some are noted as having fled.
translations.idiomatic: First: in censorial impeachments, some persons are recorded as having fled.

sentences.zh: 及其出訴，或為公使，本曹給過所有指，如不推檢，文按灼然者，雪之。

translations.literal: When they later appeal, some are on public mission and the original bureau has issued passes for all stops indicated; if this is not investigated and the documentary record is clearly established, clear them.
translations.idiomatic: When they later appeal, some are on official mission and the original office has issued passes for every stop listed; if this is not checked and the documents plainly show it, they should be cleared.

sentences.zh: 二曰：御史赦前注獲見贓，不辨行賕主名，檢無賂以置直之主，宜應洗復。

translations.literal: Second: the censorate before an amnesty notes seizure of visible booty but does not identify who gave the bribe; if investigation finds no bribe and the person charged is upright, restoration is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Second: before an amnesty the censorate records seized visible loot but does not name who paid the bribe; if inquiry finds no bribe and the accused is upright, he should be restored.

sentences.zh: 三曰：經拷不引，傍無三證，比以獄按既成，因即除削。

translations.literal: Third: after torture they do not confess and there are not three witnesses at the side; lately, because the prison record is deemed complete, they are at once struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Third: after interrogation under torture they do not confess and there are no three supporting witnesses; recently, because the prison file is treated as complete, they are immediately struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 或有據令奏復者，與奪不同，未獲為通例。

translations.literal: Some have memorialized restoration on the basis of statute, yet outcomes differ and no uniform rule has been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Some have appealed for restoration under statute, yet decisions differ and no common rule has been settled.

sentences.zh: 又須定何如得為證人。

translations.literal: It is also necessary to fix what counts as a witness.
translations.idiomatic: It is also necessary to define who may serve as a witness.

sentences.zh: 若必須三人對見受財，然後成證，則於理太寬。

translations.literal: If three persons must face one another and see the bribe received before proof is complete, the standard is too lenient.
translations.idiomatic: If proof required three persons to witness the bribe together, the rule would be too lenient.

sentences.zh: 若傳聞即為證，則於理太急。

translations.literal: If hearsay alone counts as proof, the standard is too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: If hearsay alone counted as proof, the rule would be too harsh.

sentences.zh: 今請以行賕後三人俱見，物及證狀顯著，準以為驗。

translations.literal: Now I ask that after the bribe all three be present together, with goods and evidence clearly shown, and that be taken as verification.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that after the bribe all three witnesses be present together, with goods and evidence clearly shown, and that this be taken as sufficient proof.

sentences.zh: 四曰：赦前斷事，或引律乖錯，使除復失衷，雖按成經赦，宜追從律。

translations.literal: Fourth: judgments before an amnesty that cited the wrong statute, making restoration unjust, though the case was closed by amnesty, should be corrected to follow the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: pre-amnesty judgments that misapplied the statute, making restoration unjust, though closed by amnesty, should be revised to follow the law.

sentences.zh: 五曰：經赦除名之後，或邀駕訴枉，被旨重究；

translations.literal: Fifth: after being struck from the rolls by amnesty, some intercept the imperial carriage to plead injustice and receive an order for renewed investigation;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: after removal from the rolls by amnesty, some waylay the imperial carriage to plead injustice and receive an order for reinvestigation;

sentences.zh: 或訴省稱冤，為奏更檢。

translations.literal: some appeal to the department claiming wrong and obtain a memorial for further review.
translations.idiomatic: some appeal to the department claiming injustice and obtain a memorial for further examination.

sentences.zh: 事付有司，未被研判，遂遇恩宥。

translations.literal: The matter is handed to the responsible office but not yet judged, and then an amnesty is encountered.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is assigned to the responsible office but not yet decided, and then an amnesty intervenes.

sentences.zh: 如此之徒，謂不得異於常格，依前按為定。

translations.literal: Persons of this sort, I hold, must not differ from the usual rule and should be settled according to the prior record.
translations.idiomatic: Such persons, I hold, should not be treated differently from the ordinary rule and should be decided according to the prior record.

sentences.zh: 若不合拷究，已復之流，請不追奪。

translations.literal: If they do not fit interrogation under torture and investigation, those already restored to office — please do not pursue confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not subject to torture and full investigation, those already restored to their posts should not have their property seized again.

sentences.zh: 六曰：或受辭下檢反覆，使鞫獄證占分明，理合清雪，未及告按，忽逢恩赦。

translations.literal: Sixth: Sometimes one receives testimony and is placed under repeated investigation, causing the interrogation, evidence, and divination to become clear and reason to warrant exoneration — yet before the case could be reported and adjudicated, suddenly an amnesty is encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth point: Sometimes a person gives testimony and is subjected to repeated scrutiny until the trial evidence and divination are clear and exoneration is warranted — but before the case can be formally reported, an amnesty suddenly intervenes.

sentences.zh: 若從證占而雪，則違正格；

translations.literal: If one clears based on evidence and divination, then one violates the proper statute;
translations.idiomatic: If exoneration follows from the evidence and divination, that violates the proper regulations;

sentences.zh: 如除其名，罪濫潔士。

translations.literal: If one removes their name, guilt is wrongly extended to besmirch upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: If their name is struck from the record, the charge is wrongly applied to sully worthy men.

sentences.zh: 以為罪須按成，雪以占定，若拷未畢格及要證一人不集者，不得為占定。

translations.literal: They held that guilt must be verified to completion and clearing fixed by divination; if torture is not finished per statute, or if required witnesses have not all been assembled, divination-based clearing must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that guilt must be fully established before exoneration can be fixed by divination — and that if torture has not been completed according to statute, or if even one required witness is missing, divination-based clearing must not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 古人雖患察獄之不精，未聞知冤而不理。

translations.literal: The ancients, though they worried about imprecise investigation of cases, never heard of knowing of injustice and yet not addressing it.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients feared sloppy trials, but never of learning that someone was wronged and doing nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 今之所陳，實士師之深疑，朝夕之急務，願垂察焉。

translations.literal: What is now presented is truly a matter of deep doubt for judicial officers, an urgent task morning and night — I beg you to give it your attention.
translations.idiomatic: What I now submit is a grave concern for those who judge cases and an urgent matter that admits no delay — I beg Your Majesty to consider it.

sentences.zh: 詔從雄議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Xiong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted Xiong's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 自後每有疑議，雄與公卿駁難，事多見從，於是公能之名甚盛。

translations.literal: After this, whenever there were disputed issues, Xiong debated with the senior officials, and his views were often adopted; thus his reputation for public competence grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever a disputed question arose, Xiong argued with the chief ministers, and his views were usually accepted — so his fame as a man of public ability spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 又為祿養論，稱仲尼陳五孝，自天子至庶人無致仕之文。

translations.literal: He also wrote a treatise on salary and provision for parents, stating that Confucius set forth the Five Filial Duties, and from the Son of Heaven down to commoners there is no text on retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on stipends for supporting parents, arguing that Confucius laid out the Five Filial Duties yet nowhere, from Son of Heaven to commoner, is retirement from office mentioned.

sentences.zh: 禮記：「八十，一子不從政；

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: "At eighty, one son does not attend to government;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites states: "At eighty, one son is exempt from government service;

sentences.zh: 九十，家不從政。」

translations.literal: at ninety, the whole household does not attend to government."
translations.idiomatic: at ninety, the entire household is exempt from government service."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：「復除之。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "This means exemption from corvée and taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan annotates: "This refers to exemption from corvée and taxes."

sentences.zh: 然則，止復庶民，非公卿大夫士之謂。

translations.literal: Thus it refers only to exemption for common people, not to ministers, grand masters, and officers.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, this applies only to commoners — not to ministers, grand masters, or officers.

sentences.zh: 以為宜聽祿養，不約其年。

translations.literal: He held that one should allow salary provision for parents without limiting it by age.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that stipends for supporting parents should be permitted without age restrictions.

sentences.zh: 書奏，肅宗納之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and Emperor Suzong accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Suzong approved it.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去任。

translations.literal: He left his post due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 卒哭，右僕射元欽奏雄起復為郎。

translations.literal: After the final mourning rites, Right Vice Director Yuan Qin memorialized that Xiong should be recalled to serve as a court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, Right Vice Director Yuan Qin recommended that Xiong be recalled from mourning to serve again as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 俄兼司州別駕，加前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Administrator of Si Province and was promoted to General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed concurrently as Administrator of Si Province and promoted to General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 時諸方賊盛，而南寇侵境，山蠻作逆，肅宗欲親討，以荊州為先，詔雄為行臺左丞，與前軍臨淮王彧東趣葉城，別將裴衍西通鵶路。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were rampant in all regions; southern invaders encroached on the borders and mountain barbarians rebelled. Emperor Suzong wished to lead a campaign in person, with Jing Province as the first priority. Xiong was appointed Left Director of the Mobile Secretariat, and together with the Forward Army under Prince of Huainai Yu he marched east toward Yecheng, while the separate commander Pei Yan was to open the route west through the Ya Road.
translations.idiomatic: At the time rebels were powerful everywhere, southern enemies were raiding the frontier, and mountain tribes had risen in revolt. Emperor Suzong intended to lead a personal campaign, beginning with Jing Province. Xiong was made Left Director of the Mobile Secretariat and, with Prince of Huainai Yu's vanguard, marched east toward Yecheng, while the separate commander Pei Yan was to advance west and open the Ya Road.

sentences.zh: 衍稽留未進，彧師已次汝濱。

translations.literal: Pei Yan delayed and did not advance; Yu's army had already encamped on the banks of the Ru River.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan lingered without advancing, while Yu's forces had already reached the Ru River.

sentences.zh: 北溝求救，[1]彧以處分道別，不欲應之。

translations.literal: Beigou sought aid; Yu, considering that their posts were on separate routes, did not wish to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Beigou sought aid, but Yu, believing their assignments were on different routes, did not want to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「今裴衍未至，王士眾已集，蠻左唐突，撓亂近畿，梁汝之間，民不安業，若不時撲滅，更為深害。

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Now Pei Yan has not yet arrived, but Your Highness's troops are already assembled. The barbarians on the left are rashly pressing forward, disturbing the vicinity of the capital. Between Liang and Ru the people cannot live in peace. If we do not crush them promptly, the harm will grow deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong said: "Pei Yan has not yet arrived, but Your Highness's troops are already gathered. The barbarian forces are pressing recklessly, disrupting the region near the capital. Between Liang and Ru the people cannot work in peace. If we do not destroy them at once, the damage will become far worse.

sentences.zh: 王秉麾閫外，唯利是從，見可而進，何必守道，苟安社稷，理可專裁。

translations.literal: Your Highness holds command outside the passes; one follows what is advantageous, advances when one sees opportunity — why must one hold to rigid procedure? If it will secure the state, reason permits independent decision.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness commands beyond the capital and should pursue whatever serves the interest — advance when the moment is right; why cling to fixed rules? If it will safeguard the realm, you may decide on your own authority.

sentences.zh: 所謂臣率義而行，不待命者也。」

translations.literal: This is what is called a minister acting according to duty without awaiting orders."
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant when a subject acts on principle without waiting for orders."

sentences.zh: 彧恐後有得失之責，要雄符下。

translations.literal: Yu, fearing later blame for gain or loss, demanded that Xiong issue a written order.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, afraid of being held accountable afterward for success or failure, insisted that Xiong issue a written authorization.

sentences.zh: 雄以駕將親伐，蠻夷必懷震動，乘彼離心，無往不破，遂符彧軍，令速赴擊。

translations.literal: Xiong reasoned that since the Emperor's carriage was about to lead a campaign in person, the barbarians would surely be shaken; exploiting their disunity, they would be invincible wherever they went. He therefore issued orders to Yu's army to hasten to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong argued that with the Emperor about to campaign in person, the barbarians would surely be terrified; seizing their disunity, no enemy could stand before them. He therefore authorized Yu's army to strike at once.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，果自走散。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard this, they indeed fled and dispersed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard of it, they indeed broke and scattered of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 在軍上疏曰：「凡人所以臨堅陳而忘身，觸白刃而不憚者，一則求榮名，二則貪重賞，三則畏刑罰，四則避禍難。

translations.literal: While with the army he submitted a memorial saying: "The reason ordinary men face solid battle lines and forget themselves, meet naked blades and do not flinch, is first to seek glory and renown, second to crave rich rewards, third to fear punishment, fourth to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: While on campaign he submitted a memorial: "The reason common soldiers stand before entrenched enemy lines without regard for their lives, and meet naked blades without flinching, is first to win glory, second to gain rich rewards, third to fear punishment, and fourth to escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 非此數事，雖聖王不能勸其臣，慈父不能厲其子。

translations.literal: Apart from these several things, even a sage king cannot exhort his ministers, nor a loving father steel his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Without these incentives, not even a sage king can move his ministers, nor a loving father rouse his sons.

sentences.zh: 明主深知其情，故賞必行，罰必信，使親疏、貴賤、勇怯、賢愚，聞鍾鼓之聲，見旌旗之列，莫不奮激，競赴敵場，豈厭久生而樂早死也，利害懸於前，欲罷不能耳。

translations.literal: A clear-sighted ruler well knows this disposition, and therefore rewards are surely carried out and punishments surely enforced, so that whether near or far, noble or base, brave or timid, worthy or foolish, all who hear the sound of bells and drums and see the ranks of banners are roused and strive together to reach the field of battle — it is not that they loathe long life and delight in early death; gain and harm hang before them, and though they wish to stop, they cannot.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler understands this perfectly, and so makes rewards certain and punishments sure — so that whether close or distant in rank, high or low in birth, brave or timid, wise or dull, all who hear the drums and see the banners are stirred to rush toward the enemy. It is not that they hate life and love death; reward and danger stand before them, and they cannot hold back.

sentences.zh: 自秦隴逆節，將歷數年；

translations.literal: Since the rebellion in Qin and Long, it will soon be several years;
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellion broke out in Qin and Long, several years have nearly passed;

sentences.zh: 蠻左亂常，稍已多載。

translations.literal: the disorder of the barbarians on the left has already lasted many years.
translations.idiomatic: and the barbarian uprisings have already dragged on for many years.

sentences.zh: 凡在戎役，數十萬人，三方師眾，敗多勝少，跡其所由，不明賞罰故也。

translations.literal: All those in military service number in the hundreds of thousands; the armies on three fronts win little and lose much. Tracing the cause, it is because rewards and punishments are not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands serve in the armies, yet on all three fronts defeats outnumber victories. The reason is clear: rewards and punishments are not enforced.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲天下之早平，愍征夫之勤悴，乃降明詔，賞不移時。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes early peace under Heaven and pities the toil of the campaigners, and thus issued a clear edict that rewards would not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty desires swift peace under Heaven and pities the exhaustion of the soldiers, and so issued a clear edict promising prompt rewards.

sentences.zh: 然兵將之勳，歷稔不決；

translations.literal: Yet the merit of soldiers and generals goes unresolved for years;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the achievements of soldiers and commanders remain undecided for years;

sentences.zh: 亡軍之卒，晏然在家。

translations.literal: soldiers who lost their armies sit peacefully at home.
translations.idiomatic: while men who abandoned their units live quietly at home.

sentences.zh: 致令節士無所勸慕，庸人無所畏懾。

translations.literal: This causes men of integrity to have nothing to emulate, and mediocre men nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, men of principle have nothing to aspire to, and the mediocre have nothing to dread.

sentences.zh: 進而擊賊，死交而賞賒；

translations.literal: Advance and strike the enemy — one dies in battle yet reward is deferred;
translations.idiomatic: Advance to fight and one dies in combat while reward is delayed;

sentences.zh: 退而逃散，身全而無罪。

translations.literal: Retreat and flee — one's person is safe and one is without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat and flee and one's body is spared with no punishment.

sentences.zh: 此其所以望敵奔沮，不肯進力者矣。

translations.literal: This is why, upon sighting the enemy, they break and flee, unwilling to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: That is why soldiers waver at the sight of the enemy and refuse to fight with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 若重發明詔，更量賞罰，則軍威必張，賊難可弭。

translations.literal: If a clear edict is issued again and rewards and punishments are reassessed, then military prestige will surely expand and the bandit peril can be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reissues a clear edict and enforces rewards and punishments anew, military morale will rise and the rebel threat can be crushed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞必不得已，去食就信。

translations.literal: I have heard that when there is no alternative, one gives up food for trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when there is no other choice, one must sacrifice food for the sake of trust.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，信不可斯須廢也。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, trustworthiness cannot be set aside even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that trust cannot be abandoned even for an instant.

sentences.zh: 賞罰，陛下之所易，尚不能全而行之；

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments are what Your Majesty can easily apply, yet they still cannot be fully carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments lie entirely within Your Majesty's power, yet even these cannot be fully enforced;

sentences.zh: 攻敵，士之所難，欲其必死，寧可得也？

translations.literal: Attacking the enemy is what soldiers find hard — to want them to die surely, how can that be attained?
translations.idiomatic: while attacking the enemy is what soldiers find hardest — how then can you expect them to fight to the death?

sentences.zh: 臣既庸弱，忝當戎使，職司所見，輒敢上聞。

translations.literal: I am mediocre and weak, yet I shamefully hold a military post; what my office observes, I dare report upward.
translations.idiomatic: I am a mediocre and unworthy man who holds a military post; what I have witnessed in the course of duty, I dare bring before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下審其可否。」

translations.literal: I only ask Your Majesty to examine whether this is feasible."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider whether this can be done."

sentences.zh: 會右丞闕，肅宗詔僕射、城陽王徽舉人，徽遙舉雄。

translations.literal: When the Right Director post was vacant, Emperor Suzong ordered the Vice Director, Prince of Chengyang Hui, to recommend a candidate; Hui recommended Xiong from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Right Director fell vacant, Emperor Suzong ordered Vice Director Prince of Chengyang Hui to nominate someone; from a distance Hui recommended Xiong.

sentences.zh: 仍除輔國將軍、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Xiong was appointed General Who Assists the State and Right Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was appointed General Who Assists the State and Right Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋轉吏部郎中，遷平東將軍、光祿大夫，郎中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, retaining his directorship.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became Director in the Ministry of Personnel and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, while retaining his directorship.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「帝王之道，莫尚於安民，安民之本，莫加於禮律。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "The way of emperors and kings — nothing surpasses securing the people; the root of securing the people — nothing exceeds rites and law.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "In the way of emperors and kings, nothing is higher than bringing peace to the people; and the foundation of bringing peace to the people is nothing other than rites and law.

sentences.zh: 禮律既設，擇賢而行之，天下雍熙，無非任賢之功也。

translations.literal: Once rites and law are established and the worthy are selected to implement them, the realm flourishes in harmony — all of it is the achievement of employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Once rites and law are in place and the worthy are chosen to carry them out, the realm flourishes in harmony — and that is entirely the work of appointing capable men.

sentences.zh: 故虞舜之盛，穆穆標美；

translations.literal: Thus the splendor of Yu Shun was marked by dignified majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the glory of Emperor Shun was celebrated for its solemn dignity;

sentences.zh: 文王受命，濟濟以康。

translations.literal: when King Wen received the Mandate, the multitudes thrived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: when King Wen received the Mandate, the host of officials served in ordered prosperity.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝，天縱大聖，開復典謨，選三代之異禮，採二漢之典法。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu the Filial and Cultured, heaven-endowed with great sagacity, reopened canonical institutions, selected the diverse rites of the Three Dynasties, and adopted the classical laws of the two Han.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu the Filial and Cultured, endowed by Heaven with supreme wisdom, restored the canonical institutions, drew on the varied rites of the Three Dynasties, and adopted the statutes of the two Han dynasties.

sentences.zh: 端拱而四方安，刑措而兆民治。

translations.literal: He sat with folded hands and the four quarters were secure; punishments were set aside and the myriad people were governed.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with hands folded in his sleeves and the four quarters were at peace; punishments fell into disuse and the myriad people were well governed.

sentences.zh: 世宗重光繼軌，每念聿修，官人有道，萬里清謐。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong continued the former track in renewed radiance, ever mindful of maintaining governance; officials had their way and ten thousand li were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong carried forward that legacy in renewed brilliance, ever intent on good governance; officials performed their duties and peace extended ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 陛下劬勞日昃，躬親庶政，求瘼恤民，無時暫憩，而黔首紛然，兵車不息。

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils from sun to sundown, personally overseeing all affairs, seeking out distress and caring for the people without a moment's rest — yet the common folk are in turmoil and war chariots do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty labors from dawn to dusk, personally attending to every matter, seeking out the people's hardships and showing them compassion without a moment's pause — yet the common people remain in disorder and the chariots of war never stop.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚見，可得而言。

translations.literal: In my humble view, this can be explained.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble opinion, the reason can be stated plainly.

sentences.zh: 自神龜末來，專以停年為選。

translations.literal: Since the end of the Shengui era, selection has relied solely on years-of-service ranking.
translations.idiomatic: Since the end of the Shengui era, appointments have been made solely on the basis of seniority.

sentences.zh: 士無善惡，歲久先敍；

translations.literal: Gentlemen without regard to good or bad — the long-serving are promoted first;
translations.idiomatic: Without regard to merit, those who have served longest are promoted first;

sentences.zh: 職無劇易，名到授官。

translations.literal: posts without regard to difficulty or ease — when one's name comes up, one receives office.
translations.idiomatic: without regard to whether a post is demanding or easy — when one's turn arrives, one is given office.

sentences.zh: 執按之吏，以差次日月為功能；

translations.literal: Investigators take the tally of dates and months as their merit;
translations.idiomatic: Investigating officials measure their achievement by the calendar of cases processed;

sentences.zh: 銓衡之人，以簡用老舊為平直。

translations.literal: Those who weigh appointments take simplicity in using the old and established as fairness.
translations.idiomatic: and those who assess candidates treat the routine promotion of the aged and familiar as impartial judgment.

sentences.zh: 且庸劣之人，莫不貪鄙。

translations.literal: Moreover, mediocre and inferior men are without exception greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, mediocre and unworthy men are invariably greedy and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 委斗筲以共治之重，託碩鼠以百里之命，皆貨賄是求，肆心縱意。

translations.literal: Entrusting the great weight of joint governance to men of petty capacity, and the command of a hundred-li district to those like great rats — all seek bribes and give free rein to their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting the weighty business of governance to men of petty capacity, and the fate of a hundred-li district to creatures like bloated rats — all of them seek bribes and indulge their every whim.

sentences.zh: 禁制雖煩，不勝其欲。

translations.literal: Though prohibitions are numerous, they cannot overcome their greed.
translations.idiomatic: However many regulations are imposed, they cannot restrain their appetites.

sentences.zh: 致令徭役不均，發調違謬，箕斂盈門，囚執滿道。

translations.literal: This causes corvée to fall unevenly, levies and requisitions to be wrongly dispatched, exploitive collections to fill every doorway, and prisoners to crowd the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The result is unequal corvée, wrongful levies and requisitions, extortionate collections at every door, and prisoners filling the roads.

sentences.zh: 二聖明詔，寢而不遵；

translations.literal: The clear edicts of the two sage emperors lie dormant and are not followed;
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened edicts of the two previous emperors lie unheeded;

sentences.zh: 畫一之法，懸而不用。

translations.literal: Uniform laws hang unused.
translations.idiomatic: and uniform laws are proclaimed but never applied.

sentences.zh: 自此夷夏之民相將為亂。

translations.literal: From this the barbarian and Han peoples have successively risen in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: From this, barbarians and Han subjects alike have one after another taken up arms.

sentences.zh: 豈有餘憾哉？

translations.literal: Is there any other cause for regret?
translations.idiomatic: What further cause for unrest could there be?

sentences.zh: 蓋由官授不得其人，百姓不堪其命故也。

translations.literal: It is because offices are granted to unfit men and the common people cannot bear their commands.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that offices are given to the wrong men, and the people cannot endure their rule.

sentences.zh: 當今天下黔黎，久經寇賊，父死兄亡，子弟淪陷，流離艱危，十室而九，白骨不收，孤煢靡恤，財殫力盡，無以卒歲。

translations.literal: Today the black-haired people under Heaven have long suffered bandits and rebels — fathers dead, brothers lost, sons and younger brothers fallen into captivity; scattered and in peril, nine households out of ten; white bones unburied, the orphaned and solitary untended; wealth exhausted and strength spent, with no means to finish the year.
translations.idiomatic: Today the common people throughout the realm have long endured raids and rebellion — fathers dead, brothers lost, sons and younger brothers taken captive; scattered and destitute, nine out of ten households ruined; white bones left unburied, orphans and widows uncared for; resources exhausted, with no means to survive the year.

sentences.zh: 宜及此時，早加慰撫。

translations.literal: One should take this moment to offer comfort and relief early.
translations.idiomatic: This is the time to offer comfort and relief without delay.

sentences.zh: 蓋助陛下治天下者，惟在守令，最須簡置，以康國道。

translations.literal: Those who help Your Majesty govern the realm are none other than prefects and magistrates; they must be carefully appointed to secure the way of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those who assist Your Majesty in governing the realm are the prefects and magistrates above all; they must be carefully chosen if the state is to prosper.

sentences.zh: 但郡縣選舉，由來共輕，貴遊儁才，莫肯居此。

translations.literal: Yet selection for commanderies and counties has long been collectively despised; noble travelers and outstanding talents will none of them take such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet appointments to commanderies and counties have long been held in contempt, and men of noble birth and outstanding talent refuse to accept them.

sentences.zh: 宜改其弊，以定官方。

translations.literal: One should reform this abuse to fix the official order.
translations.idiomatic: This abuse must be corrected to restore the proper order of officialdom.

sentences.zh: 請上等郡縣為第一清，中等為第二清，下等為第三清。

translations.literal: I request that superior commanderies and counties be ranked First Pure, middling ones Second Pure, and inferior ones Third Pure.
translations.idiomatic: I propose ranking superior commanderies and counties as First Pure, middling ones as Second Pure, and inferior ones as Third Pure.

sentences.zh: 選補之法，妙盡才望，如不可並，後地先才。

translations.literal: In the method of selection and appointment, fully weigh talent and reputation; where both cannot be combined, rank the post behind and talent first.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting candidates, talent and reputation should be weighed with the utmost care; where the two cannot be reconciled, talent should take precedence over the rank of the post.

sentences.zh: 不得拘以停年，竟無銓革。

translations.literal: Do not bind appointments to years-of-service ranking, never permitting selection reform.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments must not be constrained by seniority alone, leaving no room for merit-based selection.

sentences.zh: 三載黜陟，有稱者補在京名官，如前代故事，不歷郡縣不得為內職。

translations.literal: After three years' assessment and promotion, those with good repute should be appointed to prestigious capital offices; as in former precedents, one who has not served in commanderies and counties may not hold inner-court posts.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of assessment, those with distinguished records should be promoted to prestigious posts in the capital; following earlier precedent, no one who has not served in a commandery or county should hold an inner-court office.

sentences.zh: 則人思自勉，上下同心，枉屈可申，強暴自息，刑政日平，民俗奉化矣。

translations.literal: Then people will strive to improve themselves; high and low will be of one mind; wrongs can be redressed; the violent will subside on their own; punishments and governance will daily grow even; and custom and law will be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Then men will strive to better themselves, high and low will act in concert, injustices will be redressed, the violent will restrain themselves, law and order will improve day by day, and the people will return to proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 復何憂於不治，何恤於逆徒也。

translations.literal: What worry would remain for failure to govern? What fear for rebels?
translations.idiomatic: What anxiety would remain about misgovernment? What need to dread rebels?

sentences.zh: 竊見今之守令，清慎奉治，則政平訟理，有非其才，則綱維荒穢。

translations.literal: I have observed that today's prefects and magistrates — if pure and careful in governance, then affairs are even and lawsuits are settled; if not suited to the role, then the fabric of rule is neglected and fouled.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that when today's prefects and magistrates are upright and diligent, government is fair and disputes are resolved — but when they lack ability, the whole administrative order falls into chaos.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下暫留天心，校其利害，則臣言可驗，不待終朝。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to pause the imperial mind and compare the benefits and harms; then my words will be verified without waiting until the end of the morning.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to pause and weigh the advantages and disadvantages — and my words will be proved true before the morning is out.

sentences.zh: 昔杜畿寬惠，河東無警；

translations.literal: In the past, Du Ji was lenient and generous, and Hedong knew no alarm;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Du Ji governed with generosity, and Hedong remained untroubled;

sentences.zh: 蘇則分糧，金城克復。

translations.literal: Su Ze distributed grain, and Jincheng was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ze distributed grain, and Jincheng was retaken.

sentences.zh: 略觀今古，風俗遷訛，罔不任賢以相化革，朝任夕治，功可立待。

translations.literal: Broadly viewing past and present, as customs shift and go awry, there is none that does not employ the worthy to transform and reform — appoint in the morning and govern by evening; achievements can be awaited at once.
translations.idiomatic: Looking broadly at past and present, whenever customs have decayed, no state has failed to appoint the worthy to reform them — appoint a man in the morning and order is restored by evening; results can be immediate.

sentences.zh: 若遵常習故，不明選典，欲以靜民，便恐無日。」

translations.literal: If one follows routine and old habit, not clarifying the law of selection, and hopes to quiet the people — I fear there may never be such a day."
translations.idiomatic: If we cling to old habits and ignore the principles of selection, hoping thereby to calm the people — I fear that day will never come."

sentences.zh: 書奏，會肅宗崩。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; just then Emperor Suzong passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted just as Emperor Suzong died.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭寶夤在雍州起逆，城人侯眾德等討逐之，多蒙爵賞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiao Baoyin raised rebellion in Yong Province, the townspeople Hou Zhongde and others pursued and drove him out, and many received ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xiao Baoyin rebelled in Yong Province, the townspeople Hou Zhongde and others pursued and expelled him, and many were ennobled and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，詔雄兼尚書，為關西賞勳大使。

translations.literal: During Wutai, Xiong was ordered to serve concurrently as Director of the Secretariat and as Grand Commissioner for Awards of Merit in the Western Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wutai era, Xiong was appointed concurrently as Director of the Secretariat and Grand Commissioner for Awarding Merit in the Western Passes.

sentences.zh: 未行之間，會尒朱榮入洛，及河陰之難，人情未安，雄潛竄不出。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang; at the disaster at the River Yin, popular sentiment was unsettled, and Xiong went into hiding and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang; after the massacre at the River Yin, public feeling was unstable, and Xiong went into hiding and did not appear.

sentences.zh: 莊帝欲以雄為尚書，門下奏曰：「辛雄不出，存亡未分。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang wished to appoint Xiong as Director of the Secretariat; the Chancellery memorialized: "Xin Xiong does not come forth — whether he lives or perishes is still uncertain."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang wished to appoint Xiong Director of the Secretariat; the Chancellery submitted: "Xin Xiong has not emerged — whether he is alive or dead remains unknown."

sentences.zh: 莊帝曰：「寧失亡而用之，不可失存而不用也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang said: "Better to appoint him and risk that he is dead than to fail to appoint him though he still lives."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said: "Better to appoint him and risk that he is gone than to leave him unappointed while he still lives."

sentences.zh: 遂除度支尚書，加安南將軍。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Director of the Bureau of Revenue and promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was then appointed Director of the Bureau of Revenue and promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛也，北中郎將楊侃從駕北出，莊帝以侃為度支尚書。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, the General of the Northern Gentlemen Yang Kan followed the imperial carriage north; Emperor Zhuang appointed Kan as Director of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, General of the Northern Gentlemen Yang Kan accompanied the Emperor north; Emperor Zhuang appointed Kan Director of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿反洛，復召雄上。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, Xiong was again summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned to Luoyang, Xiong was summoned back to court.

sentences.zh: 雄面辭曰：「臣不能死事，俛眉從賊，乃是朝廷罪人，縱陛下不賜誅罰，而北來尚書勳高義重，臣宜避賢路。」

translations.literal: Xiong faced the Emperor and declined, saying: "Your servant failed to die in service and bowed his brows to follow the rebels — I am a criminal of the court. Even if Your Majesty does not grant punishment, the Director who came from the north has lofty merit and weighty righteousness; your servant ought to yield the path to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong faced the Emperor and declined: "I failed to die in your service and instead bowed my head to the rebels — I am a criminal of the court. Even if Your Majesty spares me, the Director who came from the north has greater merit and standing; I ought to yield the office to a better man.

sentences.zh: 莊帝曰：「卿且還本司，朕當別有處分。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang said: "You shall for now return to your original office; I shall deal with this separately.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said: "Return for now to your original post; I will decide your case separately.

sentences.zh: 遂解侃尚書。

translations.literal: He thereupon removed Kan from the Directorship of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He then removed Kan from the Directorship of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔雄以本官兼侍中、關西慰勞大使。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered Xiong, in his existing office, to serve concurrently as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Envoy to Console and Comfort the Western Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, an edict appointed Xiong, in his existing post, concurrently as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Envoy to Console the Western Passes.

sentences.zh: 將發，請事五條。

translations.literal: Before departing, he submitted five requests regarding affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, he submitted five policy requests.

sentences.zh: 一言逋懸租調，宜悉不徵。

translations.literal: First: on overdue and suspended rents and levies, none should be collected.
translations.idiomatic: First: outstanding and suspended rents and taxes should not be collected at all.

sentences.zh: 二言簡罷非時徭役，以紓民命。

translations.literal: Second: simplify and abolish corvée labor imposed at improper seasons, to ease the burden on the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Second: cut untimely corvée labor to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 三言課調之際，使豐儉有殊，令州郡量檢，不得均一。

translations.literal: Third: when assessing levies, rich and poor should be treated differently; let the provinces and commanderies measure and inspect, and do not apply a uniform rate.
translations.idiomatic: Third: when assessing levies, rich and poor should be treated differently; provinces and commanderies should inspect locally rather than apply a flat rate.

sentences.zh: 四言兵起歷年，死亡者眾，或父或子，辛酸未歇，見存耆老，請假板職，悅生者之意，慰死者之魂。

translations.literal: Fourth: warfare has gone on for years and the dead are many — sometimes fathers, sometimes sons; grief has not ceased. For the elderly who survive, grant provisional honorary offices to please the living and comfort the spirits of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: war has raged for years and countless men have died, fathers and sons alike; grief still lingers. For the elderly who remain, grant provisional honors to delight the living and comfort the dead.

sentences.zh: 五言喪亂既久，禮儀罕習，如有閨門和穆、孝悌卓然者，宜表其門閭。

translations.literal: Fifth: disorder and ruin have lasted long and ritual propriety is rarely practiced. Where households are harmonious within and filial piety and brotherly duty stand out, their gates should be publicly honored.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: after long chaos, ritual custom has faded. Where families are harmonious and filial piety is exemplary, their households should be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 仍啟曰：「臣聞王者愛民之道有六，一曰利之，二曰成之，三曰生之，四曰與之，五曰樂之，六曰喜之。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Your servant has heard that the way a king loves his people has six parts: first, to benefit them; second, to complete them; third, to give them life; fourth, to give to them; fifth, to give them joy; sixth, to give them delight.
translations.idiomatic: He further wrote: "I have heard that the way a king cherishes his people has six aspects: to benefit them, to complete them, to nurture them, to share with them, to give them joy, and to give them delight.

sentences.zh: 使民不失其時，則成之也；

translations.literal: Not letting the people miss their seasons — that is completing them;
translations.idiomatic: Not letting the people miss their seasons — that completes them;

sentences.zh: 省刑罰，則生之也；

translations.literal: reducing punishments — that is giving them life;
translations.idiomatic: reducing punishments — that nurtures them;

sentences.zh: 薄賦斂，則與之也；

translations.literal: lightening taxes and levies — that is giving to them;
translations.idiomatic: lightening taxes and levies — that shares with them;

sentences.zh: 無多徭役，則樂之也；

translations.literal: not imposing much corvée labor — that is giving them joy;
translations.idiomatic: not imposing heavy corvée — that gives them joy;

sentences.zh: 吏靜不苛，則喜之也。

translations.literal: officials quiet and not harsh — that is giving them delight.
translations.idiomatic: officials restrained and not harsh — that gives them delight.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下道邁前王，功超往代，敷春風而鼓俗，旌至德以調民。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's Way surpasses former kings and your achievements exceed past ages; you spread the spring wind to rouse custom and display supreme virtue to harmonize the people.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's Way surpasses the kings of old and your achievements exceed those of former ages; you spread a spring wind through custom and hold up supreme virtue to harmonize the people.

sentences.zh: 生之養之，正當茲日；

translations.literal: To nurture life and sustain the people — the time is precisely now;
translations.idiomatic: To nurture and sustain the people — the moment is now;

sentences.zh: 悅近來遠，亦是今時。

translations.literal: to delight those near and reach those far — this too is the task of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: to delight those near and win over those far — that too is the work of our time.

sentences.zh: 臣既忝將命，宣揚聖澤，前件六事，謂所宜行。

translations.literal: Your servant, having the misfortune to bear this commission, will proclaim the sage grace; the six matters aforesaid are what ought to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Having been entrusted with this mission, I will proclaim your sage grace; the six matters above are what ought to be enacted.

sentences.zh: 若不除煩收疾，[2]惠孤恤寡，便是徒乘官驛，虛號王人，往還有費於郵亭，皇恩無逮於民俗。

translations.literal: If one does not remove burdens and pardon the afflicted, favor orphans and pity widows, then one merely rides the official post relays under an empty title as the sovereign's envoy — going and returning costs the post stations, and the imperial grace does not reach the people's customs.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not lift burdens, pardon the afflicted, and care for orphans and widows, then I would merely ride the post relays under an empty title as the sovereign's envoy — wasting the stations on the road while your grace never reaches the people.

sentences.zh: 謹率愚管，敢以陳聞，乞垂覽許。」

translations.literal: Respectfully, with my humble understanding, I venture to submit this for hearing; I beg that you look down and grant approval.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully, with my humble counsel, I submit this for your review and ask that you approve it.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從之，因詔民年七十者授縣，八十者授郡，九十加四品將軍，百歲從三品將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang assented, and accordingly issued an edict: men of seventy were granted county rank, those of eighty commandery rank, those of ninety the additional title of Fourth-Rank General, and centenarians the title of Third-Rank General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang agreed and issued an edict: men of seventy received county rank, those of eighty commandery rank, those of ninety the additional title of Fourth-Rank General, and centenarians the title of Third-Rank General.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷鎮南將軍、都官尚書、行河南尹。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to General Who Guards the South, Director of the Bureau of Justice, and Acting Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to General Who Guards the South, Director of the Bureau of Justice, and Acting Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 普泰時，為鎮軍將軍、殿中尚書，又加衞將軍、右光祿大夫、秦州大中正。

translations.literal: During Putai, he served as General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and was further given the titles of General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right, and Chief Rectifier of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai he served as General Who Guards the Army and Director of the Palace Secretariat, and was further given the titles of General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right, and Chief Rectifier of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，又除殿中尚書、兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, he was again appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he was again appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，仍尚書。

translations.literal: Soon after he was removed as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, while retaining his post as Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left, while remaining Director.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年三月，又兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yongxi, he again served concurrently as Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Yongxi he again served concurrently as Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 於時近習專恣，請託不已，雄懼其讒慝，不能確然守正，論者頗譏之。

translations.literal: At that time close favorites acted with arbitrary power and requests and entreaties never ceased. Xiong feared their slander and malice and could not firmly uphold what was right; commentators largely mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor's close favorites acted with impunity and favor-seeking never ceased. Xiong feared their slander and could not hold firmly to principle; commentators largely scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 出帝南狩，雄兼左僕射留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu went south on the imperial tour, Xiong served concurrently as Left Vice Director and remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu fled south, Xiong served concurrently as Left Vice Director and remained to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongxi, he served concurrently as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongxi he served concurrently as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 帝入關右，齊獻武王至洛，於永寧寺集朝士，責讓雄及尚書崔孝芬、劉欽、楊機等曰：「為臣奉主，扶危救亂，若處不諫諍，出不陪隨，緩則耽寵，急便竄避，臣節安在？」

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered the lands west of the passes, the Prince of Qi, Gao Huan, arrived at Luoyang. At Yongning Temple he assembled the court officials and rebuked Xiong and the Directors Cui Xiaofen, Liu Qin, Yang Ji, and others, saying: "Serving a lord as ministers, you should support him in peril and rescue disorder. If at ease you do not remonstrate, and in departure you do not accompany him — in calm you cling to favor, in urgency you flee and hide — where is your ministerial integrity?
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor entered the west, Gao Huan arrived at Luoyang. At Yongning Temple he assembled the court and rebuked Xiong and the Directors Cui Xiaofen, Liu Qin, Yang Ji, and others: "As ministers you should support your lord in peril and rescue the realm from chaos. At ease you did not remonstrate; in flight you did not follow — clinging to favor in calm times, fleeing in crisis — where was your integrity as ministers?

sentences.zh: 諸人默然不能對。

translations.literal: The men were silent and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The men fell silent and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 雄對曰：「當主上信狎近臣，雄等不與謀議。

translations.literal: Xiong replied: "When the sovereign trusted and was intimate with his close ministers, Xiong and the rest were not included in deliberations.
