translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied: "When the sovereign trusted and favored his close attendants, we were not included in deliberations.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿西邁，若即奔隨，便恐跡同佞黨；

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went west, if we had at once rushed to follow, we feared our tracks would be the same as the flatterers' faction;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went west, if we had rushed to follow at once, we feared we would seem no different from the flatterers' faction;

sentences.zh: 留待大王，便以不從蒙責。

translations.literal: by remaining to await Your Highness, we have instead been burdened with blame for not following.
translations.idiomatic: by staying behind to await Your Highness, we have instead been blamed for not following.

sentences.zh: 雄等進退如此，不能自委溝壑，實為慚負。」

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating as we did, unable to throw ourselves into a ditch, we are truly ashamed and at fault.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between advance and retreat as we were, unable even to throw ourselves into a ditch, we are truly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 王復責曰：「卿等備位納言，當以身報國，不能盡忠，依附諂佞，未聞卿等諫諍一言，使國家之事忽至於此，罪欲何歸也！」

translations.literal: The Prince again rebuked them: "You held the posts of speaking officials and ought to have repaid the state with your persons. You could not exhaust your loyalty and clung to flatterers — yet never did one hear a word of remonstrance from you, until the affairs of the state suddenly came to this. To whom shall the guilt be assigned!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince rebuked them again: "You held the posts of speaking officials and ought to have given your lives for the state. You failed in loyalty and attached yourselves to flatterers — yet not one word of remonstrance was heard from you until the realm came to this pass. Who is to bear the guilt?"

sentences.zh: 乃誅之，時年五十。

translations.literal: They were then executed; he was fifty years old.
translations.idiomatic: They were then executed; he was fifty years old.

sentences.zh: 沒其家口。

translations.literal: His household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 二子士璨、士貞，逃入關中。

translations.literal: His two sons, Shican and Shizhen, fled into the lands within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Shican and Shizhen, fled into the west.

sentences.zh: 雄從父兄纂，字伯將。

translations.literal: Xiong's older male cousin by a paternal uncle, Zuan, styled Bojiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's older male cousin Zuan, styled Bojiang.

sentences.zh: 學涉文史，溫良雅正。

translations.literal: He studied broadly in literature and history and was gentle, good, refined, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned in literature and history, gentle and upright in character.

sentences.zh: 初為兗州安東府主簿。

translations.literal: He first served as Recorder of the Eastern Pacification Office of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Recorder of the Eastern Pacification Office of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 與祕書丞同郡李伯尚有舊，伯尚與咸陽王禧同逆，逃竄投纂。

translations.literal: He had an old acquaintance in the Secretariat Director Li Boshang of the same commandery; Boshang joined the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, in rebellion, fled, and sought refuge with Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Li Boshang, a Secretariat Director from the same commandery; Boshang joined the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, in rebellion, fled, and sought refuge with Zuan.

sentences.zh: 事覺，坐免官。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, he was dismissed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter came to light, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 稍轉太尉騎兵參軍，每為府主清河王懌所賞。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Cavalry Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and was often praised by his superior, the Prince of Qinghe, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to Cavalry Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and was often praised by his superior, Prince Yi of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 及欲定考，懌曰：「辛騎兵有學有才，宜為上第。」

translations.literal: When the annual merit review was to be settled, Yi said: "Adjutant Xin has learning and talent and ought to receive the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the annual merit review was due, Yi said: "Adjutant Xin has learning and talent and deserves the top grade.

sentences.zh: 轉越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Colonel of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尚書令李崇北伐蠕蠕，引為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the Director of the Secretariat Li Chong marched north against the Rouran, he was brought in as Recording Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Director Li Chong marched north against the Rouran, Zuan was brought in as Recording Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧北征，以纂隨崇有稱，啟為長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Huaiyang, Yu, campaigned north, because Zuan had distinguished himself under Chong, Yu memorialized to appoint him Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Huaiyang campaigned north, because Zuan had distinguished himself under Chong, Yu recommended him as Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 及廣陽王淵北伐，又引為長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guangyang, Yuan, campaigned north, he too was brought in as Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuan of Guangyang campaigned north, he was again brought in as Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 尋拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 雅為彧所稱歎，屢在朝廷薦舉之。

translations.literal: Yu consistently praised and admired him and repeatedly recommended him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu consistently praised him and repeatedly recommended him at court.

sentences.zh: 尋除持節、平東將軍、中郎將，賜絹五十匹，金裝刀一口。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and General of the Gentlemen, and was granted fifty bolts of silk and one gold-mounted blade.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and General of the Gentlemen, and was granted fifty bolts of silk and one gold-mounted blade.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，元顥乘勝，卒至城下，尒朱世隆狼狽退還，城內空虛，遂為顥擒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan, Yuan Hao pressed his advantage and suddenly arrived beneath the walls; Erzhu Shilong withdrew in disarray, the city was empty within, and Zuan was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan, Yuan Hao pressed his advantage and suddenly appeared beneath the walls; Erzhu Shilong withdrew in disarray, the city was empty within, and Hao captured Zuan.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝還宮，纂謝不守之罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Zuan apologized for failing to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Zuan apologized for failing to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「於時朕亦北巡。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At that time I too was touring the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "At that time I too was touring the north.

sentences.zh: 東軍不守，[3]豈卿之過。」

translations.literal: The eastern army failed to hold — how could that be your fault?"
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army failed to hold — how could that be your fault?"

sentences.zh: 還鎮虎牢，俄轉中軍將軍、滎陽太守。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Hulao and soon was transferred to General of the Central Army and Governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison Hulao and soon was transferred to General of the Central Army and Governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 民有姜洛生、康乞得者，舊是太守鄭仲明左右，豪猾偷竊，境內為患。

translations.literal: Among the people were Jiang Luosheng and Kang Qide, formerly attendants of the former governor Zheng Zhongming — violent ruffians who stole and plundered and were a scourge within the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people were Jiang Luosheng and Kang Qide, formerly attendants of the former governor Zheng Zhongming — violent thieves who plagued the territory.

sentences.zh: 纂伺捕擒獲，梟於郡市，百姓忻然。

translations.literal: Zuan watched for them, captured them, and displayed their heads in the commandery market; the people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan tracked them down, captured them, and displayed their heads in the commandery market; the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，除左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.

sentences.zh: 纂僑寓洛陽，乃為河南邑中正。

translations.literal: Zuan was a sojourner in Luoyang and therefore served as Chief Rectifier of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, a sojourner in Luoyang, served as Chief Rectifier of Henan.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，除使持節、河內太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王赴洛，兵集城下，纂出城謁王曰：「纂受詔於此，本有禦防。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan went to Luoyang and his troops gathered beneath the walls, Zuan went out to meet the Prince and said: "Zuan received his orders here and originally had the duty of defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched on Luoyang and his troops gathered beneath the walls, Zuan went out to meet him and said: "I received my orders here and originally had the duty to defend this place.

sentences.zh: 大王忠貞王室，扶奬顛危，纂敢不匍匐。」

translations.literal: Your Highness is loyal and true to the royal house and supports the realm in its overturn — how could Zuan not prostrate himself before you?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is loyal to the throne and supports the realm in its peril — how could I not submit to you?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「吾志去姦佞，以康國道，河內此言，深得王臣之節。」

translations.literal: The Prince said: "My aim is to remove treacherous flatterers and bring peace to the state. These words from Henei deeply accord with the integrity of a royal minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said: "My aim is to remove treacherous flatterers and restore the realm. These words from Henei show true ministerial integrity.

sentences.zh: 因命前侍中司馬子如曰：「吾行途疲弊，宜代吾執河內手也。」

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the former Attendant-in-Ordinary Sima Ziru: "I am weary from the road; you should hold Henei in my stead.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the former Attendant-in-Ordinary Sima Ziru: "I am weary from the road; you shall hold Henei in my stead.

sentences.zh: 便入洛。

translations.literal: He then entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，行西荊州事、兼尚書、南道行臺，尋正刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was charged with the affairs of Western Jing Province and served concurrently as Director and Southern Route Mobile Office; soon after he was made regular Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was charged with the affairs of Western Jing Province and served concurrently as Director and head of the Southern Route Mobile Office; soon after he was made regular Governor.

sentences.zh: 時蠻酋樊五能破析陽郡，應宇文黑獺。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian chieftain Fan Wuneng broke Xiyang Commandery and responded to Yuwen Heitu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarian chieftain Fan Wuneng seized Xiyang Commandery and rallied to Yuwen Heitu.

sentences.zh: 纂議欲出軍討之，纂行臺郎中李廣諫曰：「析陽四面無民，唯一城之地耳。

translations.literal: Zuan proposed sending troops to attack him. Li Guang, a gentleman of Zuan's mobile office, remonstrated: "Xiyang has no people on all four sides — only a single walled place.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan proposed sending troops against him. Li Guang, a gentleman of Zuan's mobile office, remonstrated: "Xiyang has no population on all four sides — only a single walled place.

sentences.zh: 山路深險，表裏羣蠻。

translations.literal: The mountain roads are deep and perilous, and barbarians surround it on every side.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain roads are deep and perilous, and barbarians surround it on every side.

sentences.zh: 今若少遣軍，則力不能制賊；

translations.literal: If one sends too few troops now, their strength will not suffice to control the bandits;
translations.idiomatic: If we send too few troops, we will lack the strength to control the bandits;

sentences.zh: 多遣，則減徹防衞，根本虛弱。

translations.literal: if one sends many, then defensive garrisons are reduced and the root is weakened.
translations.idiomatic: if we send many, we weaken our garrisons and leave our base exposed.

sentences.zh: 脫不如意，便大挫威名。

translations.literal: If things do not go as wished, prestige will suffer a great blow.
translations.idiomatic: If things go badly, our prestige will suffer a great blow.

sentences.zh: 人情一去，州城難保。」

translations.literal: Once popular sentiment turns away, the provincial capital will be hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Once morale collapses, the provincial capital will be hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「豈得縱賊不討，令其為患日深！」

translations.literal: Zuan said: "How can we let the bandits go unpunished and allow the harm to deepen day by day!"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said: "How can we leave the bandits unpunished and let the harm grow day by day!"

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「今日之事，唯須萬全。

translations.literal: Guang said: "In today's affair, only total safety will do.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "In today's affair, only complete safety will do.

sentences.zh: 且慮在心腹，何暇疥癬。

translations.literal: Moreover, when trouble is in the vitals, who has leisure for a scab?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when danger lies at the heart, who has time for a scratch?

sentences.zh: 聞臺軍已破洪威，計不久應至。

translations.literal: I hear the imperial army has already broken Hongwei, and I reckon relief should arrive before long.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the imperial army has already broken Hongwei, and relief should arrive before long.

sentences.zh: 公但約勒屬城，使各修完壘壁，善撫百姓，以待救兵。

translations.literal: Your Excellency need only restrain the subordinate cities, have each repair and complete its walls, treat the people well, and await the relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency need only restrain the subordinate cities, have each repair its walls, treat the people well, and await relief.

sentences.zh: 雖失析陽，如棄雞肋。」

translations.literal: Even if Xiyang is lost, it is like discarding a chicken rib.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we lose Xiyang, it is like discarding a chicken rib.

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「卿言自是一途，我意以為不爾。」

translations.literal: Zuan said: "Your words are one course; my view is that it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said: "That is one course of action; I do not think it is right.

sentences.zh: 遂遣兵攻之，不克而敗，諸將因亡不返。

translations.literal: He then sent troops to attack but failed to take the place and was defeated; the generals thereupon fled and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops to attack but failed and was defeated; the generals fled and did not return.

sentences.zh: 城人又密招西賊，黑獺遣都督獨孤如願率軍潛至，突入州城，遂至廳閤。

translations.literal: The townspeople also secretly summoned the western rebels; Heitu sent the commander Dugu Ruyuan with troops who arrived in secret, burst into the provincial capital, and reached the hall pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople also secretly summoned the western rebels; Heitu sent the commander Dugu Ruyuan with troops who arrived in secret, burst into the provincial capital, and reached the hall pavilion.

sentences.zh: 纂左右惟五六人，短兵接戰，為賊所擒，遂害之。

translations.literal: At Zuan's side there were only five or six men; with short weapons they joined battle, were captured by the bandits, and were then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had only five or six men at his side; fighting at close quarters they were captured by the rebels and killed.

sentences.zh: 贈都督定殷二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司徒公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles of Supervisor of all military affairs in Ding and Yin provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Duke of the State of Tu, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Supervisor of all military affairs in Ding and Yin provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Tu, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子子炎，武定中，博陵太守。

translations.literal: His son Ziyan served in the Wuding era as Governor of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyan served in the Wuding era as Governor of Boling.

sentences.zh: 雄從祖曇護，以謹厚見稱。

translations.literal: Xiong's collateral ancestor Tanhu was praised for his prudence and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's collateral ancestor Tanhu was praised for his prudence and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 卒於并州州都。

translations.literal: He died in the post of Chief Rectifier of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Chief Rectifier of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 子熾，武定中，衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Chi, in the Wuding era, served as General of the Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chi, in the Wuding era, served as General of the Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right.

sentences.zh: 雄族祖琛，字僧貴。

translations.literal: Xiong's clan forebear Chen, styled Senggui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's clan forebear Chen, styled Senggui.

sentences.zh: 父敬宗，[4]延興中代郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Jingzong served in the Yanxing era as Governor of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzong served in the Yanxing era as Governor of Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 琛少孤，曾過友人，見其父母兄弟悉無恙，垂涕久之。

translations.literal: Chen was orphaned young. Once when visiting a friend, he saw that the friend's parents and brothers were all unharmed and wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Chen lost his father young. Once when visiting a friend, he saw the friend's parents and brothers all safe and well, and wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，滎陽郡丞。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and Assistant Administrator of Xingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first taking office he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and Assistant Administrator of Xingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太守元麗性頗使酒，琛每諫之。

translations.literal: The governor Yuan Li was rather given to wine, and Chen often remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: The governor Yuan Li was rather fond of drink, and Chen often remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 麗後醉，輒令閉閤，曰：「勿使丞入也。」

translations.literal: When Li was later drunk, he would always order the gate closed, saying, "Do not let the aide enter."
translations.idiomatic: When Li was drunk afterward, he would always have the gate shut and say, "Do not let the aide in."

sentences.zh: 高祖南征，麗從輿駕，詔琛曰：「委卿郡事，如太守也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu marched south, Li accompanied the imperial carriage, and an edict said to Chen, "I entrust the commandery affairs to you, as to a governor."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu marched south, Li followed the imperial train, and an edict told Chen, "I entrust the commandery to you, as though you were its governor."

sentences.zh: 景明中，為伏波將軍、濟州輔國府長史。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he served as General Who Quells Waves and Chief Clerk of the Jizhou Fuguo Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he was appointed General Who Quells Waves and Chief Clerk of the Jizhou Fuguo Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 轉奉車都尉，出為揚州征南府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Imperial Carriage Commandant and sent out as Chief Clerk of the Yangzhou Zhengnan Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bearer of the Imperial Carriage Commandant and dispatched as Chief Clerk of the Yangzhou Zhengnan Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 刺史李崇，多事產業，琛每諍折，崇不從，遂相糾舉，詔並不問。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Li Chong busied himself with property and enterprises; Chen often remonstrated and refuted him. Chong would not listen, and they eventually impeached each other; an edict ordered that neither be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor Li Chong occupied himself with property and business ventures; Chen repeatedly remonstrated and argued him down. Chong would not heed him, and they eventually impeached each other; an edict ordered that neither case be pursued.

sentences.zh: 後加龍驤將軍，帶南梁太守。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally appointed General of Dragon Might, concurrently serving as Governor of Nanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was additionally appointed General of Dragon Might, concurrently serving as Governor of Nanliang.

sentences.zh: 崇因置酒，謂琛曰：「長史後必為刺史，但不知得上佐何如人耳？」

translations.literal: Chong thereupon set out wine and said to Chen, "The chief clerk will surely become a provincial governor someday, but one does not know what sort of man his senior aide will be."
translations.idiomatic: Chong then set out wine and said to Chen, "The chief clerk will surely become a provincial governor one day, but who knows what sort of senior aide he will get?"

sentences.zh: 琛對曰：「若萬一叨忝，得一方正長史，朝夕聞過，是所願也。」

translations.literal: Chen replied, "If by some chance I am undeservedly promoted, to obtain an upright chief clerk and hear of my faults morning and evening — that is what I would wish."
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied, "If by some chance I am undeservedly promoted, to have an upright chief clerk who tells me of my faults morning and evening — that is what I would wish for."

sentences.zh: 崇有慚色。

translations.literal: Chong showed a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: Chong looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 琛寬雅有度量，涉獵經史，喜慍不形於色，當官奉法，在所有稱。

translations.literal: Chen was broad-minded and refined, possessed magnanimity, ranged through the classics and histories, did not let joy or anger show on his face, upheld the law in office, and wherever he served was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was generous and refined, possessed of magnanimity, ranged widely through the classics and histories, never let joy or anger show on his face, upheld the law in office, and was praised wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 長子悠，字元壽，早有器業。

translations.literal: His eldest son You, styled Yuanshou, early showed talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son You, styled Yuanshou, showed talent and promise from early on.

sentences.zh: 為侍御史，監揚州軍。

translations.literal: He served as Attending Censor, supervising Yangzhou forces.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attending Censor, supervising the Yangzhou army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，錄勳書，時崇猶為刺史，欲寄人名，悠不許。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, merit rolls were recorded; at the time Chong was still provincial governor and wished to insert other men's names — You would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, merit rolls were compiled; Chong was still provincial governor and wished to insert other men's names — You refused.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「我昔值其父，今復逢其子。」

translations.literal: Chong said, "In the past I encountered his father; now again I meet his son."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "In the past I dealt with his father; now I meet his son again."

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 悠弟俊，字叔義，有文才。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Jun, styled Shuyi, had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother Jun, styled Shuyi, possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 東益州征虜府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: External Army Attendant in the Dongyizhou Zhenglu Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as External Army Attendant in the Dongyizhou Zhenglu Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 府主魏子建為山南行臺，以為郎中，有軍國機斷。

translations.literal: When the headquarters chief Wei Zijian served as Mobile Commandant for the South of the Mountains, Jun was made Gentleman of the Palace and showed decisive judgment in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters chief Wei Zijian served as Mobile Commandant for the South of the Mountains, Jun was appointed Gentleman of the Palace and showed decisive judgment in military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 還京，於滎陽為人劫害。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, at Xingyang he was robbed and murdered on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital, he was robbed and killed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Dongqin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Dongqin Province.

sentences.zh: 俊弟術，武定末，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Shu, at the end of Wuding, served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Shu, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 術弟休，字季令。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Xiu, styled Jiling.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Xiu, styled Jiling.

sentences.zh: 休弟脩，字季緒。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Xiu, styled Jixu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiu, styled Jixu.

sentences.zh: 俱有學尚，亦早卒，時人傷惜之。

translations.literal: All had scholarly pursuits; they too died early, and men of the time mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: All pursued learning; they too died young, and people of the time mourned and regretted their loss.

sentences.zh: 琛族子珍之，少有氣力。

translations.literal: Chen's clansman Zhenzhi, from youth possessed physical vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's clansman Zhenzhi possessed physical vigor from youth.

sentences.zh: 太尉鎧曹行參軍，稍遷中堅將軍、司徒錄事參軍、廣州大中正。

translations.literal: Acting Army Attendant in the Grand Commandant's Armor Bureau, he was gradually promoted to General of the Central Garrison, Recorder in the Minister of Works' staff, and Chief Arbiter of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Army Attendant in the Grand Commandant's Armor Bureau, then was gradually promoted to General of the Central Garrison, Recorder in the Minister of Works' staff, and Chief Arbiter of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁憂去任。

translations.literal: He left his post upon observing mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He left his post to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 尋起為汝北太守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled and appointed Governor of Rubei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled and appointed Governor of Rubei.

sentences.zh: 永安中，司空諮議參軍、通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he served as Advisory Attendant in the Ministry of Works and Palace Attendant Directly at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he served as Advisory Attendant in the Ministry of Works and Palace Attendant Directly at the Gate.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，襄城太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was Governor of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was appointed Governor of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 天平初，洛州以南人情駭懼，敕為大使，持節慰諭廣洛二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, south of Luozhou the people's hearts were struck with fear; he was appointed commissioner, bearing credentials to reassure and instruct the two provinces of Guang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, the people south of Luozhou were seized with fear; he was appointed commissioner bearing credentials to reassure and instruct the two provinces of Guang and Luo.

sentences.zh: 三年，除征東將軍、行陽平郡事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed General Who Conquers the East and Acting Administrator of Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed General Who Conquers the East and Acting Administrator of Yangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡民路黑奴起逆，攻郡，為黑奴所執。

translations.literal: A commandery resident, Lu Heinu, rose in rebellion and attacked the commandery; Zhenzhi was captured by Heinu.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery resident named Lu Heinu rose in rebellion and attacked the commandery; Zhenzhi was captured by Heinu.

sentences.zh: 諸賊勸殺之，黑奴曰：「成敗未可知，何為先殺太守也？」

translations.literal: The various bandits urged killing him; Heinu said, "Success or failure cannot yet be known — why kill the governor first?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels urged that he be killed; Heinu said, "Victory or defeat is not yet certain — why kill the governor first?"

sentences.zh: 乃將珍之自隨，待遇以禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Zhenzhi along with him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he kept Zhenzhi with him and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 右衞將軍郭瓊討平黑奴，乃得免。

translations.literal: Right Guard General Guo Qiong suppressed and pacified Heinu, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Guo Qiong suppressed Heinu and restored order, and only then was Zhenzhi released.

sentences.zh: 興和中，為衞將軍、司徒司馬。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he served as General of the Guard and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era he served as General of the Guard and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 武定三年，除驃騎將軍、北海太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuding he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 還為儀同開府長史、兼光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Returning, he served as Chief Clerk of an Opener of Offices with the same privilege as the Three Excellencies, concurrently serving as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as Chief Clerk of an Opener of Offices with the same privilege as the Three Excellencies, concurrently serving as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔珍之持節為廣洛北荊揚雍襄六州慰勞大使、北荊鎮城、行廣州事，招納有稱。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict appointed Zhenzhi commissioner bearing credentials as Reassurance and Solace Envoy for the six provinces of Guang, Luo, Northern Jing, Yang, Yong, and Xiang, Walled City Commander of Northern Jing, and Acting Administrator of Guangzhou; his recruitment and pacification won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, an edict appointed Zhenzhi commissioner bearing credentials as Reassurance and Solace Envoy for the six provinces of Guang, Luo, Northern Jing, Yang, Yong, and Xiang, Walled City Commander of Northern Jing, and Acting Administrator of Guangzhou; his work in recruiting and pacifying won praise.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王遣書慰勉，賜以衣帛。

translations.literal: King Wenxiang of Qi sent a letter of comfort and encouragement and bestowed clothing and silk.
translations.idiomatic: King Wenxiang of Qi sent a letter of comfort and encouragement and bestowed robes and silk.

sentences.zh: 尋敕行平州，卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to administer Ping Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to administer Ping Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Luozhou, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Luozhou, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子懿，[5]武定末，開府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yi, at the end of Wuding, served as Army Attendant in the Opener of Offices' Armor Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Army Attendant in the Opener of Offices' Armor Bureau.

sentences.zh: 羊深，字文淵，太山平陽人，[6]梁州刺史祉第二子也。

translations.literal: Yang Shen, styled Wenyuan, was a native of Pingyang in Taishan — the second son of Zhi, Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen, styled Wenyuan, was a native of Pingyang in Taishan — the second son of Zhi, Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 早有風尚，學涉經史，好文章，兼長几案。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed moral refinement, studied and ranged through the classics and histories, loved literary composition, and was also skilled at desk duties.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed moral refinement, studied the classics and histories broadly, loved literary composition, and was also skilled at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 少與隴西李神儁同志相友。

translations.literal: In youth he shared the same aspirations and friendship with Li Shenjun of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he shared the same ideals and formed a close friendship with Li Shenjun of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 自司空府記室參軍轉輕車將軍、尚書騎兵郎。

translations.literal: From Recorder in the Ministry of Works he was transferred to General of Light Chariots and Gentleman in the Cavalry Section of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From Recorder in the Ministry of Works he was transferred to General of Light Chariots and Gentleman in the Cavalry Section of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋轉駕部，加右軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Transport Section and additionally appointed General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Transport Section and additionally appointed General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 于時沙汰郎官，務精才實，深以才堪見留。

translations.literal: At that time palace gentlemen were being winnowed, with emphasis on true talent and solid accomplishment; Shen was retained on account of his talents being adequate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the corps of palace gentlemen was being winnowed, with emphasis on genuine talent and solid accomplishment; Shen was kept on account of his abilities.

sentences.zh: 在公明斷，尚書僕射崔亮、吏部尚書甄琛咸敬重之。

translations.literal: In public affairs he was clear and decisive; Vice Director Cui Liang of the Ministry of Works and Minister of Personnel Zhen Chen both respected and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: In public affairs he was clear and decisive; Vice Director Cui Liang of the Ministry of Works and Minister of Personnel Zhen Chen both respected and esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗行釋奠之禮，講孝經，儕輩之中獨蒙引聽，時論美之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong conducted the ceremony of offering sacrifice at the school and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, among his peers Shen alone was invited to listen; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong conducted the school sacrifice and lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, Shen alone among his peers was invited to listen; contemporary opinion praised this.

sentences.zh: 正光末，北地人車金雀等帥羌胡反叛，高平賊宿勤明達寇豳夏諸州。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, Che Jinque of Beidi and others led the Qiang and barbarians in rebellion; the bandit Suqin Mingda of Gaoping raided the provinces of Bin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang, Che Jinque of Beidi and others led the Qiang and barbarians in rebellion; the bandit Suqin Mingda of Gaoping raided the provinces of Bin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 北海王顥為都督、行臺討之，以深為持節、通直散騎常侍、行臺左丞、軍司，仍領郎中。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao served as Commander and Mobile Commandant to suppress them; Shen was appointed Bearer of Credentials, Palace Attendant Directly at the Gate for Regular Cavalry, Left Adjutant of the Mobile Commandant, and Army Strategist, still concurrently holding the post of Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao served as Commander and Mobile Commandant to suppress them; Shen was appointed Bearer of Credentials, Palace Attendant Directly at the Gate for Regular Cavalry, Left Adjutant of the Mobile Commandant, and Army Strategist, while still holding the post of Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，還京。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Shen returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Shen returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷尚書左丞，加平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤反，攻圍華州。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin rebelled and besieged Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin rebelled and besieged Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 正平薛鳳賢等聚眾作逆，[7]敕深兼給事黃門侍郎，與大行臺僕射長孫稚共會潼關，規模進止。

translations.literal: Xue Fengxian of Zhengping and others gathered multitudes and rose in rebellion; an edict appointed Shen concurrently as Master of Ceremonies of the Yellow Gate Attendant, and together with the Vice Minister of the Great Mobile Commandant Zhangsun Zhi he assembled at Tong Pass to plan strategy and movements.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengxian of Zhengping and others gathered multitudes and rose in rebellion; an edict appointed Shen concurrently as Master of Ceremonies of the Yellow Gate Attendant, and together with the Vice Minister of the Great Mobile Commandant Zhangsun Zhi he assembled at Tong Pass to plan strategy and movements.

sentences.zh: 事平，以功賜爵新泰男。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, for his merit he was granted the title Noble of Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was pacified, he was granted the title Noble of Xintai for his merit.

sentences.zh: 靈太后曾幸邙山，集僧尼齋會，公卿盡在座。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once visited Mount Mang, gathering monks and nuns for a fasting assembly; the ministers and high officials were all in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once visited Mount Mang and gathered monks and nuns for a fasting assembly; the ministers and high officials were all present.

sentences.zh: 會事將終，太后引見深，欣然勞問之。

translations.literal: As the assembly was nearing its end, the empress dowager summoned Shen forward and graciously inquired after him with words of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: As the assembly was nearing its end, the empress dowager summoned Shen forward and graciously inquired after him with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 深謝曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，世荷榮遇，寇難未平，是臣憂責，而隆私忽被，犬馬知歸。」

translations.literal: Shen thanked her, saying, "Your subject has received the state's abundant grace and borne honor for generations; the bandits are not yet pacified — this is your subject's worry and responsibility. Yet suddenly such private favor has been bestowed; even horses and hounds know where to return."
translations.idiomatic: Shen thanked her, saying, "Your subject has received the state's abundant grace and borne honor for generations; the rebels are not yet pacified — that is your subject's worry and duty. Yet suddenly such private favor has been shown me; even horses and hounds know where to return home."

sentences.zh: 太后顧謂左右曰：「羊深真忠臣也。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager turned to those beside her and said, "Yang Shen is a true loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager turned to those beside her and said, "Yang Shen is a true loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 舉坐傾心。

translations.literal: The whole assembly was won over.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，徐方多事，以深為東道慰勞使，即為二徐行臺。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, Xu Province was troubled with many affairs; Shen was made Envoy to Comfort and Solace the Eastern Circuit and concurrently Mobile Commandant for the Two Xu Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang, Xu Province was troubled with many affairs; Shen was made Envoy to Comfort and Solace the Eastern Circuit and concurrently Mobile Commandant for the Two Xu Provinces.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐祚，除安東將軍、太府卿，又為二兗行臺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Shen was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury, and again served as Mobile Commandant for the Two Yan Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Shen was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury, and again served as Mobile Commandant for the Two Yan Provinces.

sentences.zh: 深處分軍國，損益隨機，亦有時譽。

translations.literal: Shen disposed of military and state affairs, adjusting gains and losses as circumstances required, and also won contemporary repute.
translations.idiomatic: Shen disposed of military and state affairs, adjusting gains and losses as circumstances required, and also won contemporary repute.

sentences.zh: 初，尒朱榮殺害朝士，深第七弟侃為太山太守，性粗武，遂率鄉人外託蕭衍。

translations.literal: Initially, when Erzhu Rong slaughtered court officials, Shen's seventh younger brother Kan was Governor of Taishan; coarse and martial by nature, he led his townsfolk and outwardly submitted to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Erzhu Rong slaughtered court officials, Shen's seventh younger brother Kan was Governor of Taishan; coarse and martial by nature, he led his townsfolk and outwardly submitted to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 深在彭城，忽得侃書，招深同逆。

translations.literal: Shen was at Pengcheng when suddenly he received Kan's letter inviting Shen to join him in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was at Pengcheng when he suddenly received Kan's letter inviting him to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 深慨然流涕，斬侃使人，并書表聞。

translations.literal: Shen, deeply moved, wept; he beheaded Kan's messenger and submitted a memorial reporting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Shen wept; he beheaded Kan's messenger and submitted a memorial reporting the matter.

sentences.zh: 莊帝乃下詔曰：「羊侃作逆，霧起瑕丘，擁集不逞，扇擾疆埸，傾宗之禍，侃乃自貽，累世之節，一朝毀汙。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang thereupon issued an edict saying, "Yang Kan has rebelled; mist rises at Xiaqiu, gathering the unruly, inciting and disturbing the frontier — the calamity of overturning the ancestral temple Kan has brought upon himself, the integrity of generations marred in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang thereupon issued an edict saying, "Yang Kan has rebelled; mist rises at Xiaqiu as the unruly gather, inciting and disturbing the frontier — the calamity of overturning the ancestral temple Kan has brought upon himself, the integrity of generations ruined in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 羊深血誠奉國，秉操罔貳，聞弟猖勃，自劾請罪。

translations.literal: Yang Shen serves the state with blood sincerity, holds his principles without duplicity; learning that his brother ran riot, he impeached himself and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen serves the state with blood sincerity and holds his principles without duplicity; learning that his brother ran riot, he impeached himself and requested punishment.

sentences.zh: 此之丹款，實戢于懷。

translations.literal: Such a loyal heart truly moves one in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Such loyal sincerity truly moves one in the heart.

sentences.zh: 且叔向復位，春秋稱美，深之慷慨，氣同古人。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Shu Xiang was restored to office the Spring and Autumn Annals praised the deed; Shen's ardor matches the ancients in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Shu Xiang was restored to office the Spring and Autumn Annals praised the deed; Shen's ardor matches the ancients in spirit.

sentences.zh: 忠烈遠彰，赤心已著。

translations.literal: His loyal valor shines far; his red heart is already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal valor shines far; his devoted heart is already manifest.

sentences.zh: 可令還朝，面受委敕。」

translations.literal: He may be ordered to return to court and receive appointment face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Let him return to court and receive appointment face to face."

sentences.zh: 乃歸京師，除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to the capital and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to the capital and was dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 久之，除撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以深兼黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shen was concurrently appointed Master of the Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shen was concurrently appointed Master of the Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 顥平，免官。

translations.literal: When Hao was pacified, Shen was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was pacified, Shen was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後拜大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master for Festivals.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Grand Master for Festivals.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，遷散騎常侍、衞將軍、右光祿大夫，監起居注。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right, and Supervisor of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right, and Supervisor of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 自天下多事，東西二省官員委積，前廢帝敕深與常侍盧道虔、元晏、元法壽選人補定，自奉朝請以上，各有沙汰。

translations.literal: From the time the empire was troubled with many affairs, officials in the eastern and western headquarters piled up in accumulated ranks; the Deposed Emperor ordered Shen together with Regular Attendants Lu Daogan, Yuan Yan, and Yuan Fashou to select men for appointment and fill vacancies, from Court Gentlemen for Attendance upward — each rank was winnowed.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the empire was troubled with many affairs, officials in the eastern and western headquarters piled up in accumulated ranks; the Deposed Emperor ordered Shen together with Regular Attendants Lu Daogan, Yuan Yan, and Yuan Fashou to select men for appointment and fill vacancies, from Court Gentlemen for Attendance upward — each rank was winnowed.

sentences.zh: 尋兼侍中，廢帝甚親待之。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant; the Deposed Emperor treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant; the Deposed Emperor treated him with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 是時膠序廢替，名教陵遲，深乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time the ritual schools were abandoned and in decay, and moral teaching was in decline; Shen thereupon submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the ritual schools were abandoned and in decay, and moral teaching was in decline; Shen thereupon submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞崇禮建學，列代之所修；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that exalting ritual and establishing schools is what every dynasty has cultivated;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that exalting ritual and establishing schools is what every dynasty has cultivated;

sentences.zh: 尊經重道，百王所不易。

translations.literal: honoring the classics and revering the Way is what no true king changes.
translations.idiomatic: honoring the classics and revering the Way is what no true king ever changes.

sentences.zh: 是以均塾洞啟，昭明之頌載揚；

translations.literal: Thus when the communal school of Zhou was broadly opened, the eulogy of Illustrious Brightness was raised;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the communal school of Zhou was broadly opened, the eulogy of Illustrious Brightness was raised;

sentences.zh: 膠序大闢，都穆之詠斯顯。

translations.literal: when the Jiao-Xu school was greatly established, the song of Du Mu appeared.
translations.idiomatic: when the Jiao-Xu school was greatly established, the song of Du Mu appeared.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大魏乘乾統物，欽若奉時，模唐軌虞，率由前訓。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Great Wei, riding Heaven's mandate to govern all things, reverently follows the seasons, models Tang and treads in Yu's tracks, and proceeds by the teachings of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Great Wei, riding Heaven's mandate to govern all things, reverently follows the seasons, models Tang and treads in Yu's tracks, and proceeds by the teachings of former ages.

sentences.zh: 重以高祖繼聖垂衣，儒風載蔚，得才之盛，如彼薪楢。

translations.literal: All the more when Emperor Gaozu succeeded the sage and governed through non-action, Confucian wind flourished abundantly, and the fullness of talent was like firewood piled high.
translations.idiomatic: All the more when Emperor Gaozu succeeded the sage and governed through non-action, Confucian wind flourished abundantly, and the gathering of talent was like firewood piled high.

sentences.zh: 固以追隆周而並驅，駕炎漢而獨邁。

translations.literal: Therefore it can pursue and match the Zhou in glory, and driving past the Han of fire, go alone beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it can pursue and match the glory of Zhou, and driving past the Han of fire, go alone beyond.

sentences.zh: 宣皇下武，式遵舊章，用能揄揚盛烈，聿修厥美。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu carried martial virtue downward and followed the old statutes, thereby able to spread the grand achievement and jointly repair its splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu carried martial virtue downward and followed the old statutes, thereby able to spread the grand achievement and jointly repair its splendor.

sentences.zh: 自茲已降，世極道消，風猷稍遠，澆薄方競，退讓寂寥，馳競靡節。

translations.literal: From then down, the age reached its limit and the Way declined; civilized teaching gradually receded, shallow customs competed in the open, yielding and yielding stood lonely, and headlong rivalry knew no restraint.
translations.idiomatic: From then down, the age reached its limit and the Way declined; civilized teaching gradually receded, shallow customs competed openly, yielding and forbearance stood lonely, and headlong rivalry knew no restraint.

sentences.zh: 進必吏能，升非學藝。

translations.literal: Advance depended on clerical ability; promotion came without scholarly craft.
translations.idiomatic: Advance depended on clerical ability; promotion came without scholarly craft.

sentences.zh: 是使刀筆小用，計日而期榮；

translations.literal: Thus petty scriveners with minor skills counted the days expecting glory;
translations.idiomatic: Thus petty scriveners with minor skills counted the days expecting glory;

sentences.zh: 專經大才，甘心於陋巷。

translations.literal: while great talents devoted to the classics were content to remain in humble lanes.
translations.idiomatic: while great talents devoted to the classics were content to remain in humble lanes.

sentences.zh: 然治之為本，所貴得賢，苟值其人，豈拘常檢。

translations.literal: Yet the root of good government lies in valuing the worthy; if one obtains the right man, why be bound by ordinary rules?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the root of good government lies in valuing the worthy; if one obtains the right man, why be bound by ordinary rules?

sentences.zh: 三代、兩漢，異世間出。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties and the two Han eras produced them in different ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties and the two Han eras produced them in different ages.

sentences.zh: 或釋褐中林，鬱登卿尹；

translations.literal: Some put on official robes in the midst of the forest and rose abundantly to ministerial rank;
translations.idiomatic: Some donned their first official robes in obscure woodland and rose straight to high ministerial office;

sentences.zh: 或投竿釣渚，徑升公相。

translations.literal: some cast rods fishing by sandbars and went straight to grand minister or chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: some cast fishing rods from river islets and ascended directly to the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 事炳丹青，義在往策。

translations.literal: Their deeds shine in vermilion and green; their righteousness rests in the annals of old.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds shine in the historical records; their righteousness lives on in the chronicles of former ages.

sentences.zh: 彼哉邈乎，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Those men, how remote! They cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Such men, how distant in time! They are beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 竊以今之所用，弗修前矩。

translations.literal: I venture to say that what is used today does not follow the standards of old.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that present practice no longer observes the standards of former ages.

sentences.zh: 至如當世通儒，冠時盛德，見徵不過四門，登庸不越九品。

translations.literal: As for the comprehensive scholars of the age, the foremost in virtue of the time — when summoned, they come no further than the Four Gates; when appointed, they rise no higher than the Nine Ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Take the great scholars of our own day, the foremost in virtue of the age: when summoned to office, they advance no further than the Four Gates; when promoted, they rise no higher than the Nine Ranks.

sentences.zh: 以此取士，求之濟治，譬猶却行以及前，之燕而向楚。

translations.literal: To select scholars in this way and seek well-ordered government is like walking backward to go forward, or heading to Yan while facing Chu.
translations.idiomatic: To choose men of talent in this fashion and expect good government is like walking backward to advance, or setting out for Yan while facing toward Chu.

sentences.zh: 積習之不可者，其所由來漸矣。

translations.literal: That accumulated custom cannot be undone — its origin has been gradual.
translations.idiomatic: That ingrained custom cannot easily be changed; it has taken shape little by little over time.

sentences.zh: 昔魯興泮宮，頌聲爰發；

translations.literal: In antiquity Lu established the Pan Palace, and eulogies then arose;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Lu established the Pan Palace, and songs of praise then arose;

sentences.zh: 鄭廢學校，國風以譏。

translations.literal: Zheng abolished the schools, and the state's winds used this to satirize.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng abolished its schools, and the state's songs turned this into satire.

sentences.zh: 將以納民軌物，莫始於經禮；

translations.literal: To bring the people within norm and to measure things aright — nothing begins before the canonical rites;
translations.idiomatic: To bring the people within proper bounds and set things in order — nothing begins before the canonical rites;

sentences.zh: 菁莪育才，義光於篇什。

translations.literal: nurturing talent with luxuriant growth, meaning shining in the odes.
translations.idiomatic: to nurture talent as in the Jing'e ode, its meaning shining in the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 自兵亂以來，垂將十載，干戈日陳，俎豆斯闕。

translations.literal: Since the military turmoil, nearly ten years have passed; weapons of war are daily displayed, and ritual vessels are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, nearly ten years have passed; arms are arrayed day after day, while ritual vessels stand empty.

sentences.zh: 四海荒涼，民物凋弊，名教頓虧，風流殆盡。

translations.literal: Within the four seas there is desolation; people and things are withered; the teaching of names has suddenly collapsed, and cultured refinement is nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm lies desolation; people and goods are wasted away; moral teaching has suddenly collapsed, and civilized refinement is all but gone.

sentences.zh: 世之陵夷，可為歎息。

translations.literal: The world's decline is worthy of lament.
translations.idiomatic: The world's decline is cause for deep lament.

sentences.zh: 陛下中興纂曆，理運惟新，方隅稍康，實惟文德。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has revived the dynasty and succeeded to the calendar; the governing mandate is newly renewed; the regions are somewhat at peace — truly through civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has revived the dynasty and taken up the imperial succession; Heaven's mandate is renewed; the borderlands are gradually at peace — truly through civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 但禮賢崇讓之科，沿世未備；

translations.literal: But the categories of honoring worthies and exalting yielding have not been complete through the generations;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the institutions for honoring the worthy and exalting forbearance have never been fully established across the ages;

sentences.zh: 還淳反樸之化，起言斯繆。

translations.literal: the transformation of returning to purity and simplicity — at the first word, this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: as for the transformation that would restore simplicity and plain virtue — to speak of it now is already mistaken.

sentences.zh: 夫先黃老而退六經，史遷終其成蠹；

translations.literal: To put Huang-Lao first and relegate the Six Classics — Sima Qian in the end became literature's bane;
translations.idiomatic: To put Huang-Lao first and push aside the Six Classics — Sima Qian in the end became a destroyer of proper learning;

sentences.zh: 貴玄虛而賤儒術，應氏所以亢言。

translations.literal: to value abstruse emptiness and despise Confucian learning — for this reason the Ying clan spoke so boldly.
translations.idiomatic: to prize mysterious emptiness and look down on Confucian learning — that is why the Ying clan spoke out so boldly.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，敢忘前載。

translations.literal: Though your subject is not clever, how dare he forget what past records teach.
translations.idiomatic: Though your subject lacks talent, how could he forget the lessons of former ages?

sentences.zh: 且魏武在戎，尚修學校；

translations.literal: Moreover, when Emperor Wu of Wei was at war, he still maintained schools;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even when Emperor Wu of Wei was campaigning in the field, he still maintained the schools;

sentences.zh: 宣尼確論，造次必儒。

translations.literal: Confucius's firm doctrine: even in haste, be Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's settled teaching was that even in haste one must hold to the rites.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜重修國學，廣延胄子，使函丈之教日聞，釋奠之禮不闕。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly believes that the National University should be rebuilt, imperial scions broadly enrolled, so that the teaching before the master's seat is heard daily and the libation sacrifice is never omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly believes the National University should be rebuilt and imperial scions broadly enrolled, so that instruction at the master's lectern is heard every day and the libation sacrifice is never omitted.

sentences.zh: 并詔天下郡國，興立儒教。

translations.literal: An edict should also go out to all commanderies and kingdoms to establish Confucian teaching.
translations.idiomatic: An edict should also go out to every commandery and kingdom to establish Confucian teaching.

sentences.zh: 考課之程，咸依舊典。

translations.literal: Examination procedures should all follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Examination procedures should all follow the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 苟經明行修，宜擢以不次。

translations.literal: If one is versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, he should be promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: If a man is versed in the classics and upright in conduct, he should be promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 抑斗筲喋喋之才，進大雅汪汪之德。

translations.literal: Suppress the petty chatter of bean-measure schemers; advance the broad virtue of great elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Hold back the petty chatter of small-minded schemers, and advance men of broad and generous virtue.

sentences.zh: 博收鴻生，以光顧問；

translations.literal: Broadly gather great scholars to glorify the advisory corps;
translations.idiomatic: Broadly gather eminent scholars to enrich the ranks of imperial advisers;

sentences.zh: 縶維奇異，共精得失。

translations.literal: tie up and preserve the extraordinary, jointly refining right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: bind and keep men of rare talent, and together refine what is right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 使區寰之內，競務仁義之風；

translations.literal: cause all within the realm to compete in the wind of benevolence and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: So that throughout the realm all strive after the spirit of benevolence and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 荒散之餘，漸知禮樂之用。

translations.literal: in the remnants of wasteland and dispersal, gradually to know the use of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: and in the scattered ruins left by chaos, gradually come again to know the use of ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 豈不美哉！

translations.literal: Would it not be beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Would that not be splendid!

sentences.zh: 臣誠闇短，敢慕前訓，用稽古義，上塵聽覽。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly dim and limited, but dares to admire former instruction, using it to examine ancient meaning and ascend to sully your hearing and sight.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is truly dull and limited, yet dares to follow the teachings of old, examine their meaning in light of antiquity, and lay this before your Majesty's hearing.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下垂就日之監，齊非煙之化，儻以臣言可採，乞特施行。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish that Your Majesty would extend the supervision of gazing at the sun, align with the transformation of no irregular portents; if my words may be adopted, I beg they be specially enacted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will extend the radiance of one who gazes upon the sun, and bring about a transformation pure as cloudless sky; if my words may be adopted, I beg that they be put into effect at once.

sentences.zh: 廢帝善之。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，拜中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign, he was appointed Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu first ascended the throne, Shen was appointed Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Glorious Great Master.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Glorious Great Master.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年六月，以深兼御史中尉、東道軍司。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongxi, Shen was additionally made Censor-in-Chief and Eastern Route Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yongxi 3, Shen was additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief and Eastern Route Army Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 及出帝入關，深與樊子鵠等同逆於兗州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu entered the pass, Shen together with Fan Zihu and others rebelled at Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu entered the pass, Shen joined Fan Zihu and others in rebellion at Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 子鵠署深為齊州刺史，於太山博縣商王村結壘，招引山齊之民。

translations.literal: Fan Zihu appointed Shen Governor of Qi Province; at Shangwang Village in Bo County on Mount Tai he built a fortress and recruited the Mountain Qi people.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zihu appointed Shen Governor of Qi Province; at Shangwang Village in Bo County on Mount Tai he built a fortress and rallied the Mountain Qi people.

sentences.zh: 天平二年正月，大軍討破之，於陳斬深。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianping, the grand army defeated them and executed Shen at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianping 2, the main army crushed them and executed Shen at Chen.

sentences.zh: 子肅，武定末，儀同開府東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Su, at the end of Wuding, served as Colonel-Director Opening-the-Fief, Eastern Pavilion Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Colonel-Director Opening-the-Fief, Eastern Pavilion Libationer.

sentences.zh: 楊機，字顯略，天水冀人。

translations.literal: Yang Ji, styled Xianlue, was a native of Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, styled Xianlue, was a native of Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖伏恩，郡功曹，赫連屈丐時將家奔洛陽，因以家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu'en served as Commandery Merit Officer; when Helian Qubugai ruled, he moved his family fleeing to Luoyang and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu'en served as Commandery Merit Officer; during the reign of Helian Qubugai he fled with his family to Luoyang and made it his home.

sentences.zh: 機少有志節，為士流所稱。

translations.literal: Ji from youth had resolve and integrity and was praised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji possessed resolve and integrity and was praised by men of standing.

sentences.zh: 河南尹李平、元暉並召署功曹，暉尤委以郡事。

translations.literal: Henan Intendant Li Ping and Yuan Hui both summoned him as Merit Officer; Hui especially entrusted him with commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Intendant Li Ping and Yuan Hui both summoned him to serve as Merit Officer; Hui especially entrusted him with commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 或謂暉曰：「弗躬弗親，庶人弗信，何得委事於機，高臥而已。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Hui, "If one is not personally diligent, the common people will not trust him — how can you entrust affairs to Ji and merely lie high?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Hui, "If one is not personally diligent, the common people will not trust him — how can you entrust affairs to Ji and simply recline at ease?"

sentences.zh: 暉曰：「吾聞君子勞於求士，逸於任賢。

translations.literal: Hui said, "I have heard that the gentleman toils at seeking talent but rests in employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "I have heard that the gentleman toils in seeking men of talent but rests once he has entrusted the worthy.

sentences.zh: 故前代有坐嘯之人，主諾之守。

translations.literal: Thus in former ages there were men who sat and whistled, and governors who merely assented.
translations.idiomatic: That is why in former ages there were men who sat and whistled while others governed, and prefects who merely assented to what their subordinates did.

sentences.zh: 吾既委得其才，何為不可？」

translations.literal: Since I have entrusted affairs to one who possesses the talent, why not?"
translations.idiomatic: Since I have entrusted affairs to a man who truly has the talent, why should I not?"

sentences.zh: 由是聲名更著。

translations.literal: Thereupon his reputation grew even greater.
translations.idiomatic: From this his reputation grew even greater.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: On leaving hemp he served as Attending Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first taking office he served as Attending Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 於時皇子國官，多非其人，詔選清直之士，機見舉為京兆王愉國中尉，愉甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: At the time many princes' state officials were not fit persons; an edict selected upright men — Ji was nominated as Attending Commandant of Prince Jingzhao Yu's state, and Yu greatly respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials in the princes' states were unfit for their posts; an edict called for upright men to be selected. Ji was nominated Attending Commandant in Prince Jingzhao Yu's state, and Yu greatly respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、伏波將軍、廷尉評。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Within, General Who Quells Waves, and Judge of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Within, General Who Quells Waves, and Judge of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，行河陰縣事。

translations.literal: During Yan chang he acted as magistrate of Heyin County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yan chang era he served as acting magistrate of Heyin County.

sentences.zh: 機當官正色，不避權勢，明達政事，斷獄以情，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: Ji held office with upright countenance, did not avoid powerful persons, was clear in government affairs, and judged cases according to circumstances — he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ji held office with an upright bearing, did not shrink from the powerful, understood government clearly, and judged cases according to the facts — he won great renown.

sentences.zh: 平東將軍、荊州刺史楊大眼啟為其府長史。

translations.literal: Pingdong General and Jingzhou Governor Yang Dayan recommended him as Chief Clerk of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Pingdong General and Jingzhou Governor Yang Dayan recommended him as Chief Clerk of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，為涇州平西府長史。

translations.literal: During Xiping he served as Chief Clerk of the Pingxi Headquarters in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era he served as Chief Clerk of the Pingxi Headquarters in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授河陰令，轉洛陽令，京輦伏其威風，希有干犯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Heyin, then transferred to magistrate of Luoyang; the capital submitted to his imposing manner, and transgressions were rare.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Heyin, then transferred to magistrate of Luoyang; the capital submitted to his imposing authority, and few dared to transgress.

sentences.zh: 凡訴訟者，一經其前，後皆識其名姓，并記事理，世咸異之。

translations.literal: All litigants, once they had appeared before him, afterward he recognized their names and surnames and remembered the facts of their cases — the world all marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Every litigant who once appeared before him — afterward he could recall their names and remember the facts of their cases; people everywhere marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮軍將軍、司州治中，轉別駕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Garrison Army General and Bureau Director of Sizhou, then transferred to Administrative Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Garrison Army General and Bureau Director of Sizhou, then transferred to Administrative Assistant.

sentences.zh: 荊州蠻叛，兼尚書左丞、南道行臺討之。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of Jingzhou rebelled, he was additionally appointed Left Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Southern Route Mobile Commandant to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Jingzhou rebelled, he was additionally appointed Left Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Southern Route Mobile Commandant to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 還，除中散大夫，復為別駕，州牧、高陽王雍事多委機。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Regular Attendant for Dispersal, again served as Administrative Assistant, and Provincial Governor Prince Gaoyang Yong entrusted many affairs to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Regular Attendant for Dispersal and again served as Administrative Assistant; Provincial Governor Prince Gaoyang Yong entrusted many affairs to Ji.

sentences.zh: 出除清河內史，轉左將軍、河北太守，並有能名。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Qinghe, then transferred to Left General and Governor of Hebei — in each post he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Qinghe, then transferred to Left General and Governor of Hebei — in every post he won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 建義初，拜平南將軍、光祿大夫、兼廷尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed Pingnan General, Glorious Great Master, and concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was appointed Pingnan General, Glorious Great Master, and concurrently Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 又除安南將軍、司州別駕。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Annan General and Administrative Assistant of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Annan General and Administrative Assistant of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行河南尹。

translations.literal: Before long he served as acting Henan Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served as acting Henan Intendant.

sentences.zh: 轉廷尉卿，徙衞尉卿，出除安西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice, moved to Minister of the Guards, and sent out as Annxi General and Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice, moved to Minister of the Guards, and sent out as Annxi General and Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he served as Guards General and Right Glorious Great Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he served as Guards General and Right Glorious Great Master.

sentences.zh: 尋除度支尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 機方直之心久而彌厲，奉公正己，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Ji's upright and straight heart grew fiercer with time; he held to fairness and rectified himself, and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's upright and uncompromising spirit grew fiercer with the years; he upheld fairness and kept himself in check, and was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 家貧無馬，多乘小犢車，時論許其清白。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no horses; he often rode in a small ox-cart, and public opinion praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and owned no horses; he often rode in a small ox-cart, and public opinion praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 與辛雄等並誅，年五十九。

translations.literal: He was executed together with Xin Xiong and others at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed together with Xin Xiong and others at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子毗羅，解褐開府參軍事，卒於鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: His son Piluo, on leaving hemp, served as Opening-the-Fief Army Attendant and died as General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Piluo, upon first taking office, served as Opening-the-Fief Army Attendant and died while holding the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 機兄順，字元信。

translations.literal: Ji's elder brother Shun, styled Yuanxin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's elder brother Shun, styled Yuanxin.

sentences.zh: 梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Governor of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 順子僧靜，武定中，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Shun's son Sengjing, during Wuding, served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's son Sengjing, during the Wuding era, served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 機兄子虬，少有公幹。

translations.literal: Ji's elder brother's son Qiu, from youth had public talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's nephew Qiu showed administrative talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 頻為司州記室戶曹從事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as Recorder and Households Clerk Attendant of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served as Recorder and Households Clerk Attendant in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 高崇，字積善，勃海蓨人。

translations.literal: Gao Chong, styled Jishan, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chong, styled Jishan, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 四世祖撫，晉永嘉中與兄顧避難奔於高麗。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Fu, in the Jin Yongjia era fled with his elder brother Gu to Goguryeo seeking refuge.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Fu, during the Jin Yongjia era, fled with his elder brother Gu to Goguryeo to escape the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 父潛，顯祖初歸國，賜爵開陽男，居遼東，詔以沮渠牧犍女賜潛為妻，封武威公主。

translations.literal: His father Qian, at the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign returned to the state, was enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiyang, and dwelt in Liaodong; an edict gave the daughter of Juqu Mujian to Qian as wife, enfeoffing her as Princess Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian returned to the realm at the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign, was enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiyang, and lived in Liaodong; an edict gave him the daughter of Juqu Mujian as his wife and enfeoffed her as Princess Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，加寧遠將軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Mounted Escort, additionally made General of Pacifying the Distance, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of Mounted Escort, additionally made General of Pacifying the Distance, and died.

sentences.zh: 崇少聰敏，以端謹見稱。

translations.literal: Chong from youth was clever and was praised for propriety and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chong was clever and was praised for his propriety and prudence.

sentences.zh: 徵為中散，稍遷尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant for Scattering and gradually promoted to Gentleman of Three Excellencies in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Attendant for Scattering and gradually promoted to Gentleman of Three Excellencies in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 家資富厚，僮僕千餘，而崇志尚儉素，車馬器服，充事而已。

translations.literal: His family's assets were rich and ample, with over a thousand servants, yet Chong's ambition favored plain simplicity; carriages, horses, utensils, and robes were only enough for his duties.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy, with more than a thousand servants, yet Chong aspired to plain simplicity; carriages, horses, utensils, and robes were only enough to meet his needs.

sentences.zh: 自修潔，與物無競。

translations.literal: He cultivated himself and kept clean, competing with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated himself and lived cleanly, striving against no one.

sentences.zh: 初崇舅氏坐事誅，公主痛本生絕胤，遂以崇繼牧犍後，改姓沮渠。

translations.literal: Initially Chong's maternal uncle was executed for a crime; the princess grieved that her birth clan had no heir, so Chong succeeded to Mujian's line and changed his surname to Juqu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chong's maternal uncle was executed for a crime; the princess grieved that her birth clan had no heir, so Chong was made heir to Mujian's line and changed his surname to Juqu.

sentences.zh: 景明中，啟復本姓，襲爵，遷領軍長史、伏波將軍、洛陽令。

translations.literal: During Jingming he memorialized to restore his original surname, inherited the enfeoffment, and was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Army of the Capital Garrison, General Who Quells Waves, and Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era he memorialized to restore his original surname, inherited the enfeoffment, and was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Army of the Capital Garrison, General Who Quells Waves, and Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為政清斷，吏民畏其威風，每有發摘，不避強禦，縣內肅然。

translations.literal: He governed with clarity and decisiveness; officials and people feared his imposing manner; whenever he exposed wrongdoing he did not avoid the powerful, and the county was internally orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and decisiveness; officials and commoners feared his authority; whenever he exposed wrongdoing he did not shrink from the powerful, and the county became thoroughly orderly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方有遷授，會病卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: The court was just about to transfer and promote him when he died of illness at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The court was just about to transfer and promote him when he died of illness at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈漁陽太守。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Governor of Yuyang.
