translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title Governor of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，復贈征虜將軍、滄州刺史，諡曰成。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was again posthumously awarded General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Cangzhou, with the posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 2 he was again posthumously awarded General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Cangzhou, with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 初崇謂友人曰：「仲尼四科，德行為首。

translations.literal: Initially Chong said to a friend, "Confucius's four categories — virtue and conduct come first.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chong said to a friend, "Confucius's four categories of men — virtue and conduct come first.

sentences.zh: 人能立身約己，不忘典訓，斯亦足矣。

translations.literal: If a man can establish himself and restrain himself, not forgetting canonical instruction, that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: If a man can stand on his own and keep himself in check, never forgetting the teachings of the classics, that is enough.

sentences.zh: 故吾諸子。」

translations.literal: Thus [I instruct] my sons."
translations.idiomatic: That is what I tell my sons."

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The passage is lost in the source.〉

translations.literal: [Corrupt marker].
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt scrape marker appears here in the source text.

sentences.zh: 子謙之，字道讓。

translations.literal: His son Qianzhi, styled Daorang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianzhi, styled Daorang.

sentences.zh: 少事後母李以孝聞，李亦撫育過於己生，人莫能辨其兄弟所出同異。

translations.literal: In youth he served his stepmother Lady Li and was famed for filial piety; Lady Li also reared him more tenderly than her own children, so that no one could tell which brothers were born of the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served his stepmother Lady Li and was renowned for filial piety; Lady Li in turn raised him even more tenderly than her own sons, so that no one could tell which brothers shared the same birth.

sentences.zh: 論者兩重之。

translations.literal: Commentators held both in equal esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised them both alike.

sentences.zh: 及長，屏絕人事，專意經史，天文算曆、圖緯之書，多所該涉，日誦數千言，好文章，留意老易。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he shut out worldly affairs and devoted himself to the classics and histories; he broadly mastered works on astronomy, calendrics, and prognostic charts, recited several thousand words daily, loved fine writing, and attended closely to the Laozi and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he withdrew from worldly affairs and devoted himself to the classics and histories; he mastered astronomy, calendrics, and prognostic texts, recited several thousand characters each day, loved good writing, and studied the Laozi and the Book of Changes with care.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，釋褐奉朝請，加宣威將軍，轉奉車都尉、廷尉丞。

translations.literal: He inherited the enfeoffment, left common cloth for Attendance at Court, was additionally made General Who Displays Might, and was transferred to Commandant of the Chariots and Assistant in the Court of Imperial Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title, entered office as Attendance at Court, was additionally appointed General Who Displays Might, and was transferred to Commandant of the Chariots and Assistant in the Court of Imperial Justice.

sentences.zh: 正光中，尚書左丞元孚慰勞蠕蠕，反被拘留。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, Left Assistant in the Department of State Affairs Yuan Fu went to console the Rouran and was in turn detained.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era, Left Assistant in the Department of State Affairs Yuan Fu was sent to console the Rouran, but was detained instead.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕大掠而還，置孚歸國。

translations.literal: When the Rouran finished their great plunder and returned, they released Fu to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran finished their great raid and withdrew, they released Fu to return home.

sentences.zh: 事下廷尉，卿及監以下謂孚無坐，惟謙之以孚辱命，□以流罪。

translations.literal: The matter went to the Court of Imperial Justice; the Chief Minister and all below including the Supervisors held that Fu bore no guilt; only Qianzhi, on the ground that Fu had disgraced his mission, sentenced him to exile. [One character missing in source; 處 supplied from parallel passage in Book of Wei 20.]
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Court of Imperial Justice. The Chief Minister and all officials below him, including the Supervisors, held that Fu was not guilty; only Qianzhi argued that Fu had disgraced his mission and should be sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 尚書同卿執，詔可謙之奏。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs sided with the Chief Minister's view, but an edict approved Qianzhi's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs agreed with the Chief Minister, but an edict approved Qianzhi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，行河陰縣令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, he served as Acting Magistrate of Heyin County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiaochang era, he served as Acting Magistrate of Heyin County.

sentences.zh: 先是，有人囊盛瓦礫，指作錢物，詐市人馬，因逃去。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had bagged rubble and gravel, passed it off as money or goods, and fraudulently bought horses and men from the market before fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, a man had filled sacks with rubble, passed them off as money or valuables, fraudulently bought horses and men in the market, and then escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔令追捕，必得以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered pursuit; the culprits had to be found and reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the criminals be pursued and that the matter be reported once they were caught.

sentences.zh: 謙之乃偽枷一囚立於馬市，宣言是前詐市馬賊，今欲刑之。

translations.literal: Qianzhi then falsely put a cangue on one prisoner and stood him in the horse market, proclaiming that this was the earlier horse-market swindler and that he was now to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi then had a prisoner falsely placed in the cangue and set up in the horse market, announcing that this was the earlier swindler who had cheated the market and was now to be executed.

sentences.zh: 密遣腹心察市中私議者。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent trusted men to observe those whispering private comments in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he sent trusted agents to listen to private talk in the market.

sentences.zh: 有二人相見忻然曰：「無復憂矣。」

translations.literal: Two men met and said with delight, "No more worry."
translations.idiomatic: Two men met and said with relief, "No more need to worry."

sentences.zh: 執送按問，具伏盜馬，徒黨悉獲。

translations.literal: They were seized, interrogated, and fully confessed to horse theft; all their accomplices were captured.
translations.idiomatic: They were seized and questioned, confessed fully to horse theft, and all their accomplices were captured.

sentences.zh: 并出前後盜竊之處，資貨甚多，遠年失物之家，各來得其本物。

translations.literal: They also revealed places of earlier thefts; the goods were very numerous, and households that had lost things years before each came and recovered their original property.
translations.idiomatic: They also revealed the sites of earlier thefts; the stolen goods were very numerous, and families that had lost property years before each came and recovered what was theirs.

sentences.zh: 具以狀奏。

translations.literal: He submitted a full report of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a full report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋詔除寧遠將軍，正河陰令。

translations.literal: Soon an edict removed him as General Who Pacifies the Distance and confirmed him as Magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance and confirmed him as Magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 在縣二年，損益治體，多為故事。

translations.literal: During his two years in the county, he improved and refined the structure of governance, and much became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During his two years in the county, he improved the structure of local governance, and much of what he did became precedent.

sentences.zh: 弟道穆為御史，在公亦有能名，世美其父子兄弟並著當官之稱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Daomu was an Investigating Censor; in office he too had a reputation for ability, and the age praised father and sons and brothers alike for their distinction in office.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Daomu served as Investigating Censor and likewise earned a reputation for competence; contemporaries praised the whole family for their distinction in office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，二縣令得面陳得失，時佞幸之輩惡其有所發聞，遂共奏罷。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the two county magistrates could state gains and losses face to face; at the time flatterers and favorites hated that anything might be exposed, so together they memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the two county magistrates could report problems and successes directly to the throne; the flatterers and favorites of the day hated anything that might be exposed, and together they memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 謙之乃上疏曰：「臣以無庸，謬宰神邑，實思奉法不撓，稱是官方，酬朝廷無貲之恩，盡人臣守器之節。

translations.literal: Qianzhi then submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject, being without talent, has wrongly been made magistrate of the divine capital; I truly mean to uphold the law without bending, to fit the measure of official duty, to repay the court's boundless grace, and to fulfill a minister's duty of guarding his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi then submitted a memorial saying, "I am without merit, yet have been wrongly placed as magistrate of the sacred capital. I truly mean to uphold the law without yielding, to measure up to the standards of office, to repay the court's boundless grace, and to fulfill a minister's duty of guarding his charge.

sentences.zh: 但豪家支屬，戚里親媾，縲紲所及，舉目多是，皆有盜憎之色，咸起怨上之心。

translations.literal: But the collateral branches of powerful families, relatives by marriage among the imperial kin — wherever bonds and fetters reach, nearly all one sees are such people; all wear the look of thieves under threat, and all harbor resentment against their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: But the collateral branches of great clans and the marriage kin of the imperial family — wherever my arrests reach, nearly everyone involved is of that sort. They all wear the look of thieves under threat, and all harbor resentment against their superiors.

sentences.zh: 縣令輕弱，何能克濟。

translations.literal: A county magistrate is weak and slight — how can he overcome and succeed?
translations.idiomatic: A county magistrate is weak and powerless — how can he prevail?

sentences.zh: 先帝昔發明詔，得使面陳所懷。

translations.literal: The former emperor once issued a bright edict allowing one to state one's thoughts face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor once issued a clear edict allowing magistrates to state their views directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣崇之為洛陽令，常得入奏是非，所以朝貴斂手，無敢干政。

translations.literal: My deceased father, the former minister Chong, when he was Magistrate of Luoyang, was often able to enter and report right and wrong; for this reason the court nobles held their hands and none dared interfere in government.
translations.idiomatic: My late father, the former minister Chong, when he was Magistrate of Luoyang, was often able to enter court and report what was right and wrong; because of this the great officials of the capital held back and none dared meddle in government.

sentences.zh: 近日以來，此制遂寢，致使神宰威輕，下情不達。

translations.literal: In recent days this system has lain dormant, causing the divine ruler's authority to grow light and lower sentiments not to reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times this system has fallen into disuse, so that the emperor's authority has weakened and the concerns of the people no longer reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 今二聖遠遵堯舜，憲章高祖。

translations.literal: Now the Two Sages far follow Yao and Shun and take the Grand Ancestor's institutions as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Two Sages look far back to Yao and Shun and take the Grand Ancestor's institutions as their model.

sentences.zh: 愚臣望策其駑蹇，少立功名。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject hopes to spur his lame nag and establish a little merit.
translations.idiomatic: Your unworthy subject hopes to spur his feeble efforts and achieve even a little merit.

sentences.zh: 乞新舊典，更明往制。

translations.literal: I beg that old and new statutes be examined anew and the former system made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that old and new regulations be reviewed and the former system restored in plain terms.

sentences.zh: 庶姦豪知禁，頗自屏心。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps powerful wrongdoers will know prohibition and somewhat restrain their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps the powerful and lawless will know their limits and restrain themselves somewhat."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此啟深會朕意，付外量聞。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "This memorial deeply accords with Our intent; deliver it outside for deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "This memorial goes deeply to Our intent; refer it outward for deliberation and report."

sentences.zh: 謙之又上疏曰：

translations.literal: Qianzhi again submitted a memorial saying,
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi submitted another memorial, saying,

sentences.zh: 臣聞夏德中微，少康成克復之主；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when the virtue of Xia waned in its middle age, Shaokang became a ruler who achieved restoration;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the virtue of Xia waned in its middle age, Shaokang became a ruler who restored the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 周道將廢，宣王立中興之功。

translations.literal: when the Way of Zhou was about to fall, King Xuan established the achievement of revival.
translations.idiomatic: when the Way of Zhou was nearing collapse, King Xuan achieved the work of revival.

sentences.zh: 則知國無常安，世無恒弊，唯在明主所以變之有方，化之有道耳。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that a state has no constant peace and an age no everlasting decline — all depends on whether the enlightened ruler has means to change affairs and a Way to transform them.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that no state enjoys permanent peace and no age suffers eternal decline — all depends on whether the enlightened ruler knows how to change affairs and has a Way to transform them.

sentences.zh: 自正光已來，邊城屢擾，命將出師，相繼於路，軍費戎資，委輸不絕。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenguang era, the border fortresses have been repeatedly disturbed; orders to generals to take the field have followed one after another on the roads, and military expenses and war supplies have been delivered without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguang era the border fortresses have been repeatedly harassed; orders sending generals to the field have followed one after another, and military expenses and war supplies have flowed without cease.

sentences.zh: 至如弓格賞募，咸有出身；

translations.literal: For example, in bow-drawing recruitment rewards, all gained entry to office;
translations.idiomatic: For example, those rewarded for passing the bow-drawing recruitment test all gained entry to office;

sentences.zh: 槊刺斬首，又蒙階級。

translations.literal: for spear thrusts and beheadings in battle, one again received rank advancement.
translations.idiomatic: those who scored spear thrusts and beheadings in battle again received promotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 故四方壯士，願征者多，各各為己，公私兩利。

translations.literal: Therefore brave men from the four quarters who wished to campaign were many; each acted for himself, and public and private both profited.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore brave men from every quarter who wished to serve in the campaigns were many; each pursued his own gain, and both state and individual benefited.

sentences.zh: 若使軍帥必得其人，賞勳不失其實，則何賊不平，何征不捷也！

translations.literal: If army commanders were always the right men and rewards for merit never missed their true measure, then what enemy would not be pacified, what campaign would not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: If army commanders were always the right men and rewards for merit always matched real achievement, then what enemy could not be subdued, what campaign could fail!

sentences.zh: 諸守帥或非其才，多遣親者妄稱入募，別倩他人引弓格，虛受征官。

translations.literal: Many garrison commanders were not equal to their posts; they often sent relatives who falsely claimed enrollment in recruitment, then hired others to draw the bow in the test and falsely received conscript officer rank.
translations.idiomatic: Many garrison commanders were unfit for their posts; they often sent relatives who falsely claimed to have enrolled for recruitment, then hired others to draw the bow in the test and received conscript officer rank without merit.

sentences.zh: 身不赴陳，惟遣奴客充數而已，對寇臨敵，曾不彎弓。

translations.literal: They themselves did not go to the battle line but only sent slave retainers to fill the quota; facing the enemy they never bent a bow.
translations.idiomatic: They themselves never went to the front but only sent slave retainers to fill the rolls; when facing the enemy they never so much as bent a bow.

sentences.zh: 則是王爵虛加，征夫多闕，賊虜何可殄除，忠貞何以勸誡也？

translations.literal: Then royal ranks were falsely bestowed, conscript soldiers were largely absent — how could bandits and invaders be exterminated, and how could loyalty and integrity be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Thus royal ranks were handed out for nothing, and the ranks of conscript soldiers stood largely empty — how could bandits and invaders be destroyed, and how could loyalty and integrity be rewarded?

sentences.zh: 且近習、侍臣、戚屬、朝士，請託官曹，擅作威福。

translations.literal: Moreover, close attendants, palace attendants, imperial kin, and court officials request favors from government offices and arbitrarily wield authority.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, close attendants, palace attendants, imperial kin, and court officials solicit favors from government offices and wield power arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 如有清貞奉法不為回者，咸共譖毀，橫受罪罰。

translations.literal: If any were pure, upright, upheld the law, and would not bend, all together slandered and destroyed them, and they suffered punishment without cause.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone was upright, upheld the law, and refused to bend, they all joined in slandering him and he suffered punishment without cause.

sentences.zh: 在朝顧望，誰肯申聞？

translations.literal: Looking about at court, who would dare report it?
translations.idiomatic: Looking about at court, who would dare speak out?

sentences.zh: 蔽上擁下，虧風壞政。

translations.literal: They conceal matters from above and block those below, damaging custom and ruining government.
translations.idiomatic: They hide the truth from superiors and block those below, damaging public morals and ruining good government.

sentences.zh: 使讒諂甘心，忠讜息義。

translations.literal: Thus slander and flattery find willing hearts, while loyal remonstrance loses its force.
translations.idiomatic: Thus slander and flattery flourish, while loyal remonstrance falls silent.

sentences.zh: 況且頻年以來，多有徵發，民不堪命，動致流離，苟保妻子，競逃王役，不復顧其桑井，憚比刑書。

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent years levies and conscription have been frequent; the people cannot bear the burden and readily flee; to preserve wife and children they compete to escape imperial service, no longer caring for their homesteads, fearing only matching the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent years levies and conscription have been frequent; the people cannot bear the burden and readily take flight. To preserve their wives and children they compete to evade imperial service, no longer caring for their homesteads, fearing only the penalties of the law.

sentences.zh: [8]正由還有必困之理，歸無自安之路。

translations.literal: [8] It is precisely because return still holds the certainty of hardship, while home offers no path to peace.
translations.idiomatic: It is precisely because those who return still face certain hardship, while those at home have no secure path to peace.

sentences.zh: 若聽歸其本業，徭役微甄，則還者必眾，墾田增闢，數年之後，大獲課民。

translations.literal: If they were allowed to return to their original occupations and corvée and levies were lightly assessed, then those returning would surely be many; reclaimed fields would expand, and after several years revenue from the people would greatly increase.
translations.idiomatic: If they were allowed to return to their original occupations and corvée and taxes were lightly assessed, returnees would surely be numerous; reclaimed land would expand, and within a few years tax revenue would greatly increase.

sentences.zh: 今不務以理還之，但欲嚴符切勒，恐數年之後，走者更多，安業無幾。

translations.literal: Now, instead of striving to bring them back by reason, you only wish to enforce strict orders and tight commands — I fear that after several years there will be more fugitives and few who keep to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Now, instead of trying to win them back through reasonable policy, the court only seeks to enforce strict orders and tight commands — I fear that after several years there will be more fugitives and fewer who remain at their occupations.

sentences.zh: 故有國有家者，不患民不我歸，唯患政之不立，不恃敵不我攻，唯恃吾不可侮。

translations.literal: Therefore he who has a state or a family does not worry that the people will not return to him, but worries that his government will not be established; he does not rely on the enemy not attacking him, but relies on his own being not to be insulted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ruler of a state or a family does not worry that the people will not come back to him, but worries that his government will not stand firm; he does not rely on enemies refraining from attack, but relies on making himself not to be despised.

sentences.zh: 此乃千載共遵，百王一致。

translations.literal: This is what a thousand ages jointly observe and a hundred kings hold as one.
translations.idiomatic: This is what every age has observed and every sage king has held as one.

sentences.zh: 且琴瑟不韻，知音改弦更張；

translations.literal: Moreover, when qin and se are out of tune, the knowing ear changes the strings and restrings them;
translations.idiomatic: When the qin and se are out of tune, the knowing musician changes the strings and restrings the instrument;

sentences.zh: 騑驂未調，善御執轡成組。

translations.literal: when the paired horses are not in step, the skilled driver takes the reins and sets them right.
translations.idiomatic: when the paired horses are not in step, the skilled driver takes the reins and sets them to rights.

sentences.zh: 諺云：「迷而知反，得道不遠。」

translations.literal: A proverb says, "When lost, to turn back — the Way is not far."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "When you are lost, to turn back — the Way is not far."

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以諭大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it can instruct what is great.
translations.idiomatic: Though this saying is small, it can instruct what is great.

sentences.zh: 陛下一日萬機，事難周覽，元、凱結舌，莫肯明言。

translations.literal: Your Majesty handles ten thousand affairs in a day; matters are hard to survey completely; Yuan and Kai hold their tongues and none will speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty handles ten thousand affairs each day, and it is hard to see everything; even men of wisdom hold their tongues and will not speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 臣雖庸短，世受榮祿，竊慕前賢匪躬之義，不避斧鉞之誅，以希一言之益。

translations.literal: Your subject, though mediocre and limited, has for generations received honor and salary; I privately admire the former worthies' principle of not sparing oneself, and do not avoid execution by axe and halberd, hoping for the benefit of a single word.
translations.idiomatic: I am mediocre and of little account, yet I have received honor and salary for generations; I privately admire the former worthies' principle of not sparing oneself, and do not shrink from death by axe and halberd in hope of offering even one word of benefit.

sentences.zh: 伏願少垂覽察，略加推採，使朝章重舉，軍威更振，海內起惟新之歌，天下見復禹之績，則臣奏之後，笑入下泉。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty would slightly extend examination and inquiry, and somewhat push and select, so that court statutes are again raised up, military prestige is renewed, renewal rises within the seas, and the realm sees achievements like those of Yu's restoration — then after my memorial I may laugh as I enter the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will look into these matters and act upon them, so that court institutions are restored, military prestige renewed, songs of renewal rise across the realm, and the world sees achievements like those of Yu's restoration — then after this memorial I may go down smiling to the grave.

sentences.zh: 靈太后得其疏，以責左右近侍。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling received his memorial and reproached the close attendants at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling received his memorial and rebuked the close attendants around her.

sentences.zh: 諸寵要者由是疾之，乃啟太后云：「謙之有學藝，宜在國學，以訓胄子。」

translations.literal: Those who enjoyed favor and power therefore resented him, and memorialized the Empress Dowager saying, "Qianzhi has learning and skill; he should be in the Imperial Academy to instruct the crown princes."
translations.idiomatic: Those who held favor and power therefore resented him and memorialized the Empress Dowager, saying, "Qianzhi has learning and talent; he should serve in the Imperial Academy to instruct the imperial students."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，除國子博士。

translations.literal: An edict followed this; he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved; he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 謙之與袁翻、常景、酈道元、溫子昇之徒，咸申款舊。

translations.literal: Qianzhi with Yuan Fan, Chang Jing, Li Daoyuan, Wen Zisheng, and the like all renewed old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi renewed old friendships with Yuan Fan, Chang Jing, Li Daoyuan, Wen Zisheng, and others of that circle.

sentences.zh: 好於贍恤，言諾無虧。

translations.literal: He was fond of providing for and caring for others; in word and promise he never fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to provide for and care for others; in word and promise he never failed.

sentences.zh: 居家僮隸，對其兒不撻其父母，生三子便免其一，世無髠黥奴婢，常稱俱禀人體，如何殘害。

translations.literal: At home, his male and female servants — before his children he would not beat their parents; when a servant bore three sons he exempted one from service; in his household there were no shaved or tattooed slave women, for he often said that all alike receive the human body — how could one mutilate it?
translations.idiomatic: At home, before his children he would not have male and female servants beaten for their parents' sake; when a servant bore three sons he exempted one from service; in his household there were no shaved or tattooed slave women, for he often said that all alike receive the human body — how could one mutilate it?

sentences.zh: 以父舅氏沮渠蒙遜曾據涼土，國書漏闕，謙之乃修涼書十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Because his father's maternal clan, Juqu Mengxun, had once held Liang territory and the state annals were incomplete, Qianzhi compiled a History of Liang in ten scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Because his maternal grandfather's clan, Juqu Mengxun, had once held Liang territory and the official histories were incomplete, Qianzhi compiled a History of Liang in ten scrolls, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 涼國盛事佛道，為論貶之，因稱佛是九流之一家。

translations.literal: The Liang state greatly favored Buddhism; in his treatise he criticized this, and accordingly called Buddhism one school among the Nine Schools.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Liang had greatly favored Buddhism; in his treatise he criticized this and accordingly called Buddhism one school among the Nine Schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 當世名士，競以佛理來難，謙之還以佛義對之，竟不能屈。

translations.literal: Famous scholars of the age competed to challenge him with Buddhist doctrine; Qianzhi answered with Buddhist reasoning in return, and in the end they could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Famous scholars of the age competed to challenge him with Buddhist doctrine; Qianzhi answered with Buddhist reasoning, and in the end none could defeat him.

sentences.zh: 以時所行歷，多未盡善，乃更改元修撰，為一家之法，雖未行於世，議者歎其多能。

translations.literal: Because the calendar then in use was in many respects not yet good, he revised the era designation and compiled a method of his own school; though it was not put into use in the world, commentators admired his many talents.
translations.idiomatic: Because the calendar then in use was in many respects still imperfect, he revised the era designation and compiled a calendrical system of his own; though it was never adopted, commentators admired his many talents.

sentences.zh: 於時朝議鑄錢，以謙之為鑄錢都將長史。

translations.literal: At the time the court deliberated casting coin, and Qianzhi was made Chief Clerk to the Director of Coinage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court debated minting coin, and Qianzhi was appointed Chief Clerk to the Director of Coinage.

sentences.zh: 乃上表求鑄三銖錢曰：

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial requesting the casting of three-zhu coin, saying,
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial requesting that three-zhu coins be cast, saying,

sentences.zh: 蓋錢貨之立，本以通有無，便交易。

translations.literal: In general, the establishment of money and goods was originally to pass between those who have and those who lack and to facilitate exchange.
translations.idiomatic: In general, money was originally instituted to pass goods between those who have and those who lack and to facilitate exchange.

sentences.zh: 故錢之輕重，世代不同。

translations.literal: Therefore the weight of coin has differed from age to age.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the weight of coin has differed from one age to the next.

sentences.zh: 太公為周置九府圜法，至景王時更鑄大錢。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke established the Nine Treasuries round-coin standard for Zhou; by the time of King Jing large coin was recast.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke established the Nine Treasuries round-coin standard for Zhou; by the time of King Jing of Zhou, large coins were recast.

sentences.zh: 秦兼海內，錢重半兩。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm within the seas, coin weighed half a liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm, coin weighed half a liang.

sentences.zh: 漢興，以秦錢重，改鑄榆莢錢。

translations.literal: When Han arose, because Qin coin was heavy, elm-seed coin was recast.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, because Qin coin was too heavy, elm-seed coin was recast.

sentences.zh: 至文帝五年，復為四銖。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Emperor Wen it was again made four zhu.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth year of Emperor Wen it was again made four zhu.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，悉復銷壞，更鑄三銖，至元狩中，變為五銖。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time all was melted down and destroyed, and three-zhu coin was recast; by the middle of Yuanshou it was changed to five zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu all existing coin was melted down and recast as three-zhu coin; by the middle of the Yuanshou era it was changed to five zhu.

sentences.zh: 又造赤仄之錢，以一當五。

translations.literal: Red-edge coin was also made, counting one as five.
translations.idiomatic: Red-edge coin was also minted, with one counting as five.

sentences.zh: 王莽攝政，錢有六等，大錢重十二銖，次九銖，次七銖，次五銖，次三銖，次一銖。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang held regency, coin had six grades: large coin weighing twelve zhu, then nine zhu, then seven zhu, then five zhu, then three zhu, then one zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang held regency, coin had six denominations: large coin weighing twelve zhu, then nine zhu, then seven zhu, then five zhu, then three zhu, then one zhu.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝罷五銖錢，至明帝復立。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei abolished five-zhu coin; by Emperor Ming it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei abolished five-zhu coin; under Emperor Ming it was restored.

sentences.zh: 孫權江左，鑄大錢，一當五百。

translations.literal: Sun Quan in the lands south of the Yangzi cast large coin, one counting as five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan in the lands south of the Yangzi cast large coins, one counting as five hundred.

sentences.zh: 權赤烏年，復鑄大錢，一當千。

translations.literal: In Sun Quan's Chiwu era, large coin was again cast, one counting as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Quan's Chiwu era, large coins were again cast, one counting as a thousand.

sentences.zh: 輕重大小，莫不隨時而變。

translations.literal: Light and heavy, large and small — none failed to change with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Light and heavy, large and small — all changed with the times.

sentences.zh: 竊以食貨之要，八政為首；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that in the essentials of food and goods, the eight policies take first place;
translations.idiomatic: I consider that among the essentials of food and goods, the eight policies of governance take first place;

sentences.zh: 聚財之貴，詒訓典文。

translations.literal: in the value of gathering wealth, handed-down instruction and canonical text.
translations.idiomatic: and in the value of gathering wealth, the instructions handed down in canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 是以昔之帝王，乘天地之饒，御海內之富，莫不腐紅粟於太倉，藏朽貫於泉府，儲畜既盈，民無困敝，可以寧謐四極，如身使臂者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperors and kings of old, riding the abundance of Heaven and Earth and controlling the wealth within the seas, all rotted red grain in the Grand Granary and stored decaying strings of cash in the treasury; once stores were full, the people were without hardship or exhaustion, and they could bring quiet to the four quarters as though the arm obeyed the body.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperors and kings of old, possessing the abundance of Heaven and Earth and the wealth of the realm, all filled the Grand Granary until grain rotted and the treasury until strings of cash decayed; once stores were full the people knew no hardship, and they could bring peace to the four quarters as though the arm obeyed the body.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之孝武，地廣財豐，外事四戎，遂虛國用。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's Emperor Wu, with broad territory and rich wealth, undertook external affairs with the four barbarians and thus emptied the state's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han, with broad territory and rich treasury, undertook foreign campaigns against the four barbarian frontiers and thus emptied the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 於是草萊之臣，出財助國；

translations.literal: Thereupon men from the grass and wilds came forth with wealth to assist the state;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon humble men from the countryside came forth with wealth to assist the state;

sentences.zh: 興利之計，納稅廟堂。

translations.literal: plans for increasing profit were admitted in the imperial hall.
translations.idiomatic: and schemes for increasing revenue were admitted in the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 市列榷酒之官，邑有告緡之令。

translations.literal: Markets had offices for monopolizing wine; districts had orders for reporting concealed wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Markets had offices for the wine monopoly; districts had orders for reporting concealed wealth.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵既興，錢幣屢改，少府遂豐，上林饒積。

translations.literal: Once the salt and iron [monopolies] were established and coin was repeatedly changed, the Privy Treasury grew rich and the Upper Park's stores multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Once the salt and iron monopolies were established and coin was repeatedly changed, the Privy Treasury grew rich and the Upper Park's stores multiplied.

sentences.zh: 外闢百蠻，內不增賦者，皆計利之由也。

translations.literal: Opening the hundred barbarians without and not increasing levies within — all came from calculating profit.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against barbarians abroad without increasing taxes at home — all of this came from calculating profit.

sentences.zh: 今羣妖未息，四郊多壘，徵稅既煩，千金日費，資儲漸耗，財用將竭，誠楊氏獻說之秋，桑、兒言利之日。

translations.literal: Now the many rebels have not ceased; on the four outskirts ramparts are many; levies and taxes are already burdensome, a thousand gold is spent daily; stores gradually dwindle and resources are nearly exhausted — truly this is the season for Yang's offering of counsel and the day for Sang and Er to speak of profit.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebellion has not ceased; on every frontier ramparts multiply; levies and taxes are already burdensome and a thousand gold is spent each day; stores gradually dwindle and the treasury is nearly exhausted — truly this is the season when men like Yang offer counsel and the day when men like Sang and Er speak of profit.

sentences.zh: 夫以西京之盛，錢猶屢改，並行小大，子母相權，況今寇難未除，州郡淪敗，民物凋零，軍國用少，別鑄小錢，可以富益，何損於政，何妨於人也？

translations.literal: When even the flourishing Western Capital changed coin repeatedly, large and small circulated together and mother and child coins balanced each other — how much more now, when bandit trouble is not yet cleared, prefectures and commanderies have fallen, people and goods are withered, and military and state use is scant, to cast separate small coin can enrich and increase stores — what harm to government, what injury to the people?
translations.idiomatic: When even the flourishing Western Capital changed coin repeatedly, large and small circulated together and mother and child coins balanced each other — how much more now, when banditry is not yet suppressed, prefectures and commanderies have fallen, people and goods are wasted, and military and state expenditure is scarce: to cast separate small coin can enrich the treasury — what harm to government, what injury to the people?

sentences.zh: 且政興不以錢大，政衰不以錢小，惟貴公私得所，政化無虧，既行之於古，亦宜效之於今矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, government does not rise because coin is large, nor decline because coin is small — what matters is only that public and private each get what is fitting and government and transformation suffer no loss; since it was practiced in antiquity, it should also be followed in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, good government does not depend on large coin, nor does bad government come from small coin — what matters is only that public and private interests are properly balanced and governance suffers no harm; since this was practiced in antiquity, it should also be followed today.

sentences.zh: 昔禹遭大水，以歷山之金鑄錢，救民之困。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yu encountered great flood and used gold from Lishan Mountain to cast coin, saving the people from distress.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Yu encountered the great flood, he used gold from Lishan Mountain to cast coin and relieve the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 湯遭大旱，以莊山之金鑄錢，贖民之賣子者。

translations.literal: Tang encountered great drought and used gold from Zhuangshan to cast coin, redeeming people who had sold their children.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang encountered great drought, he used gold from Zhuangshan to cast coin and redeem people who had sold their children.

sentences.zh: 今百姓窮悴，甚於曩日，欽明之主豈得垂拱而觀之哉？

translations.literal: Now the common people are impoverished and worn, more than in former days — can a reverent and enlightened sovereign merely fold his arms and look on?
translations.idiomatic: Today the common people are destitute and exhausted, more so than in former times — how can a reverent and enlightened sovereign simply stand aside and watch?

sentences.zh: 臣今此鑄，以濟交乏，五銖之錢，任使並用，行之無損，國得其益，穆公之言於斯驗矣。

translations.literal: Your servant now casts this coin to relieve want in trade; the five-zhu coin — let both be used as one sees fit; in practice there is no harm and the state obtains benefit — Duke Mu's words are here verified.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant now proposes this coinage to relieve shortages in commerce; the five-zhu coin may be used freely alongside it — in practice there is no harm and the state will benefit. Duke Mu's words are here proved true.

sentences.zh: 臣雖術愧計然，識非心算，暫充錢官，頗覩其理。

translations.literal: Though your servant's skill falls short of Ji Ran, and my knowledge is not heart-calculation, serving temporarily as coin officer I have seen much of the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Though your servant's skill cannot compare with Ji Ran's, and my knowledge falls short of mental reckoning, in serving temporarily as coin officer I have seen much of how the system works.

sentences.zh: 苟有所益，不得不言。

translations.literal: If there is some benefit, I cannot but speak.
translations.idiomatic: If there is some benefit to be gained, I cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 脫以為疑，求下公卿博議。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds it doubtful, I request that it be submitted to the high ministers for broad deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty has doubts, I ask that the matter be referred to the chief ministers for full deliberation.

sentences.zh: 如謂為允，即乞施行。

translations.literal: If it is deemed acceptable, I beg that it be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: If it is judged acceptable, I beg that it be implemented at once.

sentences.zh: 詔將從之，事未就，會卒。

translations.literal: An edict was about to approve it, but the matter was not completed when he died.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was about to approve the proposal, but the matter was not finished when he died.

sentences.zh: 初，謙之弟道穆，正光中為御史，糾相州刺史李世哲事，大相挫辱，其家恒以為憾。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qianzhi's younger brother Daomu, in the Zhenguang era served as censor and impeached Xiangzhou Inspector Li Shizhe on various matters, greatly humiliating him; Li's family always resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qianzhi's younger brother Daomu had served as censor during the Zhenguang era and impeached Xiangzhou Inspector Li Shizhe on various charges, greatly humiliating him; Li's family had long resented this.

sentences.zh: 至是，世哲弟神軌為靈太后深所寵任，直謙之家僮訴良，神軌左右之，入諷尚書，判禁謙之於廷尉。

translations.literal: At this time Shizhe's younger brother Shen Gui was deeply favored and trusted by Empress Dowager Ling; straightway a servant of Qianzhi's household sued for free status, Shen Gui supported him, entered and hinted to the Department of State Affairs, and Qianzhi was sentenced to imprisonment in the Court of Imperial Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shizhe's younger brother Shen Gui was deeply favored and trusted by Empress Dowager Ling. He immediately had a servant of Qianzhi's household bring suit claiming free commoner status; Shen Gui backed the case, went to the Department of State Affairs to drop hints, and Qianzhi was sentenced to imprisonment in the Court of Imperial Justice.

sentences.zh: 時將赦，神軌乃啟靈太后發詔，於獄賜死，時年四十二。

translations.literal: Just as an amnesty was impending, Shen Gui memorialized Empress Dowager Ling to issue an edict granting death in prison; he was then forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Just as an amnesty was about to be proclaimed, Shen Gui memorialized Empress Dowager Ling to issue an edict ordering Qianzhi's death in prison; he was then forty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 朝士莫不哀之。

translations.literal: No court official failed to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Every court official mourned him.

sentences.zh: 所著文章百餘篇，別有集錄。

translations.literal: His literary compositions numbered over a hundred pieces; there is a separate collected record.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred essays, which were collected in a separate volume.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈征虜將軍、營州刺史，諡曰康，又除一子出身，以明冤屈。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously given General Who Subdues Barbarians and Inspector of Yingzhou, with posthumous title Kang; one son was also granted office-entry rank to clear the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously appointed General Who Subdues Barbarians and Inspector of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Kang; one son was also granted initial office rank to acknowledge the injustice done to him.

sentences.zh: 謙之妻中山張氏，明識婦人也。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's wife was Lady Zhang of Zhongshan, a woman of clear understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's wife was Lady Zhang of Zhongshan, a woman of keen intelligence.

sentences.zh: 教勸諸子，從師受業。

translations.literal: She taught and exhorted her sons to follow teachers and receive learning.
translations.idiomatic: She taught and encouraged her sons to study under teachers.

sentences.zh: 常誡之曰：「自我為汝家婦，未見汝父一日不讀書。

translations.literal: She often admonished them, saying: "Since I became your family's daughter-in-law, I have never seen your father go a day without reading.
translations.idiomatic: She often warned them, saying, "Since I became your family's daughter-in-law, I have never seen your father go a single day without reading.

sentences.zh: 汝等宜各修勤，勿替先業。」

translations.literal: You should each cultivate diligence and not abandon your ancestors' occupation."
translations.idiomatic: You should each work hard and not abandon your ancestors' way of life."

sentences.zh: 謙之長子子儒，字孝禮。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's eldest son Ziru, styled Xiaoli.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's eldest son Ziru, styled Xiaoli.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，其叔道穆從駕北巡，子儒後踰河至行宮，莊帝見之，具訪洛中事意，子儒備陳元顥敗在旦夕。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, his uncle Daomu accompanied the emperor north on tour; Ziru later crossed the river to the traveling palace. Emperor Zhuang saw him and questioned him fully about affairs in Luoyang; Ziru explained in detail that Yuan Hao's defeat was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, his uncle Daomu accompanied the emperor on the northern tour; Ziru later crossed the river to the traveling palace. Emperor Zhuang saw him and questioned him closely about conditions in Luoyang, and Ziru explained in detail that Yuan Hao's defeat was imminent.

sentences.zh: 帝謂道穆曰：「卿初來日，何故不與子儒俱行？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Daomu: "On the day you first came, why did you not come together with Ziru?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Daomu, "When you first arrived, why did you not come together with Ziru?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣家百口在洛，須其經營。

translations.literal: He replied: "A hundred mouths of my family are in Luoyang and need his management.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There are a hundred mouths in my family still in Luoyang, and they needed his care.

sentences.zh: 且欲其今日之來，知京師後事。」

translations.literal: And I wanted him to come today so that he would know subsequent affairs of the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I also wanted him to come today so that he could report on later developments in the capital."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「子儒非直合卿本懷，亦大慰朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ziru not only suits your original intent; he also greatly reassures my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ziru not only suits your original purpose; he also greatly reassures me."

sentences.zh: 仍授祕書郎中，轉通直郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Secretary Gentleman and transferred to Direct Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ziru was appointed Secretary Gentleman and later transferred to Direct Drafter.

sentences.zh: 後除安東將軍、光祿大夫、司徒中兵參軍、兼祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Central Army Staff Officer under the Minister Over the Masses, and concurrently Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Central Army Staff Officer under the Minister Over the Masses, and concurrently Libationer.

sentences.zh: 襲爵。

translations.literal: He inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 興和初，除兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe he was appointed Concurrent Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xinghe era he was appointed Concurrent Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 時四方多有流民，子儒為梁州、北豫、西兗三州檢戶使，所獲甚多。

translations.literal: At that time there were many displaced people in all directions; Ziru served as Household Inspector for Liang, North Yu, and West Yan — he obtained a great many.
translations.idiomatic: At that time displaced people were numerous throughout the realm; Ziru served as Household Inspector for Liang, North Yu, and West Yan, and registered a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 後以公事去官。

translations.literal: Later he left office over official business.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office because of official business.

sentences.zh: 武定六年卒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Wuding, at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 子儒弟緒，字叔宗，明悟好學。

translations.literal: Ziru's younger brother Xu, styled Shuzong, was bright and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru's younger brother Xu, styled Shuzong, was intelligent and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 謙之常謂人曰：「興吾門者，當是此兒。」

translations.literal: Qianzhi often told people: "The one who will raise our house should be this boy."
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi often told people, "The one who will raise up our house will be this boy."

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵書傳，好文詠。

translations.literal: When he grew up he read widely in books and records and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he read widely in books and records and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 司空行參軍，轉長流參軍。

translations.literal: Staff Officer in the Ministry of Works, transferred to Chief Circuit Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Staff Officer in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to Chief Circuit Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 除鎮遠將軍、冀州儀同府中兵參軍，為府主封隆之所賞。

translations.literal: Appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Central Army Staff Officer in the Ji Province Equerry Office; he was esteemed by his bureau chief Feng Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Central Army Staff Officer in the Ji Province Equerry Office, and was esteemed by his bureau chief Feng Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 隆之行梁州、濟州，引自隨，恒令總攝數郡。

translations.literal: When Longzhi went to Liang and Ji provinces, he brought Xu along and constantly had him oversee several commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Longzhi went to Liang and Ji provinces, he took Xu with him and regularly put him in charge of several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 武定三年卒，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding he died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Wuding, at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 緒弟孝貞，武定中，司徒士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Xu's younger brother Xiaozhen, in the Wuding era served as Staff Officer in the Records Section of the Minister Over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's younger brother Xiaozhen served as Staff Officer in the Records Section of the Minister Over the Masses during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 孝貞弟孝幹，司空東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: Xiaozhen's younger brother Xiaogan, Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhen's younger brother Xiaogan served as Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 謙之弟恭之，字道穆，行字於世。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's younger brother Gongzhi, styled Daomu; his courtesy name was used in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's younger brother Gongzhi, styled Daomu, was known by his courtesy name in public life.

sentences.zh: 學涉經史，非名流儁士，不與交結。

translations.literal: He studied classics and histories; unless they were famous and outstanding gentlemen he did not associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics and histories, and would not associate with anyone who was not a celebrated and outstanding gentleman.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事兄如父母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his elder brother as [he would] parents.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he served his elder brother as he would his parents.

sentences.zh: 每謂人曰：「人生厲心立行，貴於見知，當使夕脫羊裘，朝佩珠玉者。

translations.literal: He often told people: "In life one should steel the heart and establish conduct — what is prized is being recognized; one should be able to cast off a sheepskin coat at dusk and wear pearls and jade in the morning.
translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "In life one should toughen the heart and establish one's conduct — what matters is being recognized; one should be able to cast off a sheepskin coat at dusk and wear pearls and jade by morning.

sentences.zh: 若時不我知，便須退迹江海，自求其志。」

translations.literal: If the times do not know us, then one must withdraw to rivers and seas and seek one's own purpose."
translations.idiomatic: If the times do not recognize us, then one must withdraw to rivers and seas and pursue one's own purpose."

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡高選御史，道穆奏記於匡曰：「道穆生自蓬簷，長於陋巷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang was selecting censors with high standards; Daomu submitted a petition to Kuang, saying: "Daomu was born under a thatched eave and grew in a narrow lane.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuan Kuang was selecting censors with exacting standards; Daomu submitted a petition to Kuang, saying, "Daomu was born under a thatched roof and grew up in a narrow lane.

sentences.zh: 頗獵羣書，無純碩之德；

translations.literal: I have ranged widely through many books but lack pure and solid virtue;
translations.idiomatic: I have read widely among many books, but lack pure and solid virtue;

sentences.zh: 尚好章詠，乏彫掞之工。

translations.literal: I still love regulated verse but lack the skill of carved and polished [composition].
translations.idiomatic: I still love regulated verse, but lack skill in polished composition.

sentences.zh: 雖欲厠影髦徒，班名俊伍，其可得哉？

translations.literal: Though I wish to stand among those glorious youths and rank in the company of the outstanding — how can that be attained?
translations.idiomatic: Though I wish to stand among those glorious youths and rank with the outstanding — how could that be achieved?

sentences.zh: 然凝明獨斷之主，雄才不世之君，無藉朽株之資，求人屠釣之下，不牽闇投之誚，取士商歌之中。

translations.literal: Yet a clear-minded sovereign who decides alone, a ruler of unmatched heroic talent, does not rely on the merit of rotting stumps but seeks men among butchers and fishermen; he does not fear the reproach of casting blindly but selects scholars from among those singing merchant songs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a clear-minded sovereign who decides for himself, a ruler of unmatched heroic talent, does not rely on the credentials of withered stumps but seeks men among butchers and fishermen; he does not fear the reproach of blind selection but chooses scholars from among those singing in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 是以聞英風而慷慨，望雲路而低佪者，天下皆是也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who hear heroic wind and are stirred, who gaze at the cloudy path and hesitate — the whole world is full of them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who hear of heroic virtue and are stirred, who gaze at the lofty path and hesitate — such men fill the whole world.

sentences.zh: 若得身隸繡衣，名充直指，雖謝周生騎上之敏，實有茅氏就鑊之心。」

translations.literal: If I could attach myself to the embroidered robe and fill the post of Direct Pointer, though I fall short of Master Zhou's alertness on horseback, I truly have the Ma clan's spirit of going to the cauldron."
translations.idiomatic: If I could join the ranks of the censors and fill the post of Direct Pointer, though I fall short of Master Zhou's alertness on horseback, I truly have the Ma clan's willingness to go to the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 匡大喜曰：「吾久知其人，適欲召之。」

translations.literal: Kuang was greatly pleased and said: "I have long known this man and was just about to summon him."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was greatly pleased and said, "I have long known this man and was just about to summon him."

sentences.zh: 遂引為御史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Daomu was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 其所糾摘，不避權豪，臺中事物，多為匡所顧問。

translations.literal: In his impeachments he did not avoid powerful magnates; affairs within the censorate were often referred to him by Kuang for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In his impeachments he did not shrink from powerful magnates, and Kuang often consulted him on affairs within the censorate.

sentences.zh: 道穆曾進說於匡曰：「古人有言，罰一人當取千萬人懼，豺狼當道，不問狐狸。

translations.literal: Daomu once offered counsel to Kuang, saying: "The ancients had a saying: in punishing one man one should make ten thousand men fearful; when wolves and jackals block the road, one does not trouble about foxes.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu once offered counsel to Kuang, saying, "The ancients had a saying: when punishing one man, one should make ten thousand men fearful; when wolves and jackals block the road, one does not bother with foxes.

sentences.zh: 明公荷國重寄，宜使天下知法。」

translations.literal: Your Excellency bears the state's heavy trust; you should make all under Heaven know the law."
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency bears the state's heavy trust; you should make all under Heaven respect the law."

sentences.zh: 匡深然之。

translations.literal: Kuang deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang fully agreed.

sentences.zh: 正光中，出使相州。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era he went on mission to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era he went on mission to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史李世哲即尚書令崇之子，[9]貴盛一時，多有非法，逼買民宅，廣興屋宇，皆置鴟尾，又於馬埒堠上為木人執節。

translations.literal: Inspector Li Shizhe was the son of Minister Over the Masses Li Chong; [9] noble and flourishing for a time, he committed many illegal acts — forced purchase of commoners' dwellings, greatly building houses, all fitted with owl-tail roof ornaments; he also had wooden figures holding insignia placed on mounds beside his horse racing track.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Li Shizhe was the son of Minister Over the Masses Li Chong; [9] for a time he was noble and powerful and committed many illegal acts — forcing the purchase of commoners' dwellings, building houses on a grand scale, all fitted with owl-tail roof ornaments; he also had wooden figures holding insignia placed on mounds beside his horse-racing track.

sentences.zh: 道穆繩糾，悉毀去之，并發其贓貨，具以表聞。

translations.literal: Daomu bound him to the law, had all destroyed, and also exposed his corrupt goods, reporting everything in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu prosecuted him according to law, had all these things destroyed, and also exposed his ill-gotten goods, reporting everything in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 又尒朱榮討蠕蠕，道穆監其軍事，榮甚憚之。

translations.literal: Also when Erzhu Rong campaigned against the Rouran, Daomu supervised his military affairs; Rong feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against the Rouran, Daomu supervised his military affairs, and Rong greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 還，除奉朝請，俄除太尉鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Attendance at Court; soon after, Staff Officer in the Armor Section of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Attendance at Court, and soon after was made Staff Officer in the Armor Section of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤西征，以道穆為行臺郎中，軍機之事，多以委之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin marched west, Daomu was made Traveling-Palace Gentleman; military affairs were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin marched west, Daomu was appointed Traveling-Palace Gentleman, and military affairs were largely entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 大都督崔延伯敗後，賊勢轉強，屢請益兵，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: After Grand Commander Cui Yanbo was defeated, rebel strength grew; [Baoyin] repeatedly requested reinforcements but the court did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Commander Cui Yanbo was defeated, rebel strength increased; reinforcements were repeatedly requested, but the court did not approve.

sentences.zh: 寶夤謂道穆曰：「非卿一行，兵無益理。」

translations.literal: Baoyin said to Daomu: "Without your one journey, troops cannot usefully be managed."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin said to Daomu, "Without your making this journey, troops cannot be usefully deployed."

sentences.zh: 遂令乘傳赴洛。

translations.literal: He then had him travel by post relay to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him travel by post relay to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親問賊勢，道穆具以狀對。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally asked about rebel strength; Daomu answered in full according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally asked about rebel strength, and Daomu answered in full according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 太后怒曰：「比來使人皆言賊弱，卿何獨云其強也！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager angrily said: "Recently all envoys have said the rebels are weak — why do you alone say they are strong!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said angrily, "Recently every envoy has said the rebels are weak — why do you alone say they are strong!"

sentences.zh: 道穆曰：「前使不實者，當是冀陛下恩顏，望霑爵賞。

translations.literal: Daomu said: "Those earlier envoys who were untruthful must have hoped for Your Majesty's gracious countenance and looked to receive ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu said, "Those earlier envoys who were untruthful must have hoped for Your Majesty's gracious favor and looked to receive ranks and rewards.

sentences.zh: 臣既忝使人，不敢虛妄。

translations.literal: Your servant, having the honor to serve as envoy, dares not speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, having the honor to serve as envoy, dares not speak falsely.

sentences.zh: 願令近臣親檢，足知虛實。」

translations.literal: I wish that nearby officials be sent to inspect in person — the truth will be fully known."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that nearby officials be sent to inspect in person — then the truth will be fully known."

sentences.zh: 事訖當反，遇病不行。

translations.literal: When the business was finished and he was about to return, he fell ill and could not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the business was finished and he was about to return, he fell ill and could not make the journey.

sentences.zh: 後屬兄謙之被害，情不自安，遂託身於莊帝。

translations.literal: Later, when his elder brother Qianzhi was killed, he was unable to calm his mind and therefore entrusted himself to Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after his elder brother Qianzhi was killed, he could not rest easy and therefore placed himself under Emperor Zhuang's protection.

sentences.zh: 帝時為侍中，特相欽重，引居第中，深相保護。

translations.literal: The emperor was then Attendant-in-ordinary; he especially esteemed him, brought him to live in his residence, and deeply protected him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then Attendant-in-ordinary; he especially valued him, brought him to live in his residence, and protected him closely.

sentences.zh: 俄而，帝以兄事見出。

translations.literal: Soon after, the emperor was removed from office because of the matter with his elder brother [Yuan Zhao].
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the emperor was removed from office because of the affair involving his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 道穆懼禍，乃攜家趣濟陰，變易姓名，往來於東平畢氏，以避時難。

translations.literal: Daomu feared disaster, took his family and hastened to Jiyin, changed his name, and went back and forth among the Bi clan of Dongping to escape the troubles of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu feared disaster, took his family and fled to Jiyin, changed his name, and moved back and forth among the Bi clan of Dongping to escape the troubles of the time.

sentences.zh: 及元顥逼虎牢城，或勸帝赴關西者，帝以問道穆，道穆對曰：「關中今日殘荒，何由可往。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed toward Hulao, some urged the emperor to go to Guanxi; the emperor asked Daomu, who replied: "Guanzhong today is ravaged and deserted — how could one go there?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed toward Hulao, some urged the emperor to flee to Guanxi; the emperor asked Daomu, who replied, "Guanzhong today is ravaged and deserted — how could one go there?

sentences.zh: 臣謂元顥兵眾不多，乘虛深入者，由國家將帥征捍不得其人耳。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that Yuan Hao's troops are not numerous; that he was able to penetrate deep by seizing the opening is because the state's generals assigned to defend were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that Yuan Hao's troops are not numerous; that he was able to penetrate deep by exploiting an opening is because the state's generals charged with defense were not the right men.

sentences.zh: 陛下若親率宿衞，高募重賞，背城一戰，臣等竭其股肱之力，破顥孤軍，必不疑矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty personally leads the palace guard, offers high rewards for recruitment, and fights one battle with our backs to the city wall, we your servants will exhaust our arm-and-leg strength — shattering Yuan Hao's isolated army is beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty personally leads the palace guard, offers high rewards for recruitment, and fights one battle with our backs to the wall, we your servants will give our all — crushing Yuan Hao's isolated army is beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 如恐成敗難測，非萬乘所履，便宜車駕北渡，循河東下。

translations.literal: If you fear that success or failure is hard to foretell and that this is not a path for the Son of Heaven, then it is fitting that the imperial carriage cross north and follow the river eastward.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear that success or failure is hard to foretell and that this is not a course for the Son of Heaven, then it is best for the imperial carriage to cross north and follow the river eastward.

sentences.zh: 徵大將軍天穆合於滎陽，向虎牢；

translations.literal: Summon Grand General Tianmu to assemble at Xingyang and advance on Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: Summon Grand General Tianmu to assemble at Xingyang and advance on Hulao;

sentences.zh: 別徵尒朱王軍，令赴河內以掎角之。

translations.literal: separately summon Erzhu Wang's army and order it to proceed to Henei to pinch from the angle.
translations.idiomatic: separately summon Erzhu Wang's army and order it to proceed to Henei to attack from the flank.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，何往不克。

translations.literal: Within ten days or a month, what could fail to be taken?
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days or a month, what could fail to be taken?

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂萬全之計，不過於此。」

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that no plan more secure than this could exist."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately considers that no plan could be more secure than this."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「高舍人語是。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Councillor Gao speaks correctly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Councillor Gao speaks correctly."

sentences.zh: 其夜到河內郡北，未有城守可依，帝命道穆秉燭作詔書數十紙，布告遠近，於是四方知乘輿所在。

translations.literal: That night they reached north of Henei commandery where there was no city garrison to rely on; the emperor ordered Daomu, by candlelight, to draft dozens of sheets of edict, announcing far and near, and thus the four directions knew where the imperial carriage was.
translations.idiomatic: That night they reached the north of Henei commandery, where there was no walled city to rely on; the emperor ordered Daomu, by candlelight, to draft dozens of edicts and announce them far and near, so that the four directions knew where the imperial carriage was.

sentences.zh: 除中軍將軍、給事黃門侍郎、安喜縣開國公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Central Army, Supervisor in the Yellow Gate, Duke Who Founded the State of Anxi with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu was appointed General of the Central Army, Supervisor in the Yellow Gate, and Duke Who Founded the State of Anxi with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 於時尒朱榮欲回師待秋，道穆謂榮曰：「元顥以蕞爾輕兵，奄據京洛，使乘輿飄露，人神恨憤，主憂臣辱，良在於今。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Rong wished to withdraw his army and wait for autumn; Daomu said to Rong: "Yuan Hao with his puny light force suddenly seized the capital, leaving the imperial carriage exposed — gods and men burn with resentment, sovereign grieves and ministers are shamed; truly it is now.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Erzhu Rong wished to withdraw his army and wait for autumn; Daomu said to Rong, "Yuan Hao with his puny light force suddenly seized the capital, leaving the imperial carriage exposed — gods and men burn with resentment, the sovereign grieves and ministers are shamed; truly the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 大王擁百萬之眾，輔天子而令諸侯，自可分兵河畔，縛筏造船，處處遣渡，徑擒羣賊，復主宮闕，此桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: Your Lordship commands a million men, assists the Son of Heaven and gives orders to the feudal lords — you might yourself divide troops along the riverbank, bind rafts and build boats, send crossings everywhere, go straight to capture the rebel band, and restore the Son of Heaven to the palace — the deed of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship commands a million men, assists the Son of Heaven and gives orders to the feudal lords — you could divide troops along the riverbank, bind rafts and build boats, send crossings everywhere, go straight to capture the rebel band, and restore the Son of Heaven to the palace — the deed of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 且一日縱敵，數世之患，今若還師，令顥重完守具，徵兵天下，所謂養虺成蛇，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to let the enemy go for one day brings calamity for generations; if you now withdraw, Yuan Hao will again complete his defenses and levy troops throughout the realm — that is the saying, "nurture a viper till it becomes a serpent" — and regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to let the enemy go for one day brings calamity for generations; if you now withdraw, Yuan Hao will again complete his defenses and levy troops throughout the realm — that is what is meant by "nurturing a viper until it becomes a serpent" — and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 榮深然之，曰：「楊黃門侃已陳此計，當更議決耳。」

translations.literal: Rong deeply agreed and said: "Councillor Yang Kan has already set forth this plan; we should discuss and decide further."
translations.idiomatic: Rong fully agreed and said, "Councillor Yang Kan has already set forth this plan; we should discuss and decide further."

sentences.zh: 及莊帝反政，因宴次謂尒朱榮曰：「前若不用高黃門計，則社稷不安。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang restored government, at a banquet he said to Erzhu Rong: "If we had not earlier used Councillor Gao's plan, the altars of state would not have been secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang restored power, at a banquet he said to Erzhu Rong, "If we had not earlier used Councillor Gao's plan, the altars of state would not have been secure.

sentences.zh: 可為朕勸其酒令醉。」

translations.literal: You may pour wine for me and get him drunk on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Pour wine for him on my behalf and get him drunk."

sentences.zh: 榮對曰：「臣本北征蠕蠕，高黃門與臣作監軍，臨事能決，實可任用。」

translations.literal: Rong replied: "Your servant was originally campaigning north against the Rouran; Councillor Gao served as my army supervisor — he could decide affairs in action and is truly fit for use."
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "Your servant was originally campaigning north against the Rouran; Councillor Gao served as my army supervisor — he could decide affairs in the field and is truly fit for use."

sentences.zh: 除征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫、兼御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Subdues the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu was appointed General Who Subdues the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋即真，仍兼黃門。

translations.literal: Soon after he received full appointment and still held the Yellow Gate concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he received full appointment and still held the Yellow Gate concurrently.

sentences.zh: 道穆外秉直繩，內參機密，凡是益國利民之事，必以奏聞。

translations.literal: Outwardly Daomu held the straight line of law; inwardly he participated in secret matters — whatever benefited the state and the people he was sure to report.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Daomu upheld the law without favor; inwardly he participated in secret affairs — whatever benefited the state and the people he was sure to report.

sentences.zh: 諫諍極言，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: In remonstrance he spoke to the utmost without any regard for fear.
translations.idiomatic: In remonstrance he spoke bluntly to the utmost, without any regard for fear.

sentences.zh: 選用御史，皆當世名輩，李希宗、李繪、陽休之、陽斐、封君義、邢子明、蘇淑、宋世良等四十人。

translations.literal: In selecting and appointing censors, all were famous men of the age — Li Xizong, Li Hui, Yang Xiuzhi, Yang Fei, Feng Junyi, Xing Ziming, Su Shu, Song Shiliang, and forty others in all.
translations.idiomatic: He selected and appointed censors, all famous men of the age — Li Xizong, Li Hui, Yang Xiuzhi, Yang Fei, Feng Junyi, Xing Ziming, Su Shu, Song Shiliang, and forty others in all.

sentences.zh: 於時用錢稍薄，道穆表曰：「四民之業，錢貨為本，救弊改鑄，王政所先。

translations.literal: At that time the coin in circulation had grown rather thin. Daomu memorialized: "The four classes of people — their livelihood rests on coin and goods; rescuing abuse and recasting coin is what royal government must put first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the coin in circulation had grown rather thin. Daomu memorialized, "The livelihood of the four classes of people rests on coin and goods; rescuing abuse and recasting coin is what royal government must put first.

sentences.zh: 自頃以私鑄薄濫，官司糾繩，挂網非一。

translations.literal: Recently, because of private casting of thin, debased coin, the offices have pursued correction, and the net has caught many.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because of private casting of thin, debased coin, the authorities have pursued offenders, and many have been caught in the net.

sentences.zh: 在市銅價，八十一文得銅一斤，私造薄錢，斤餘二百。

translations.literal: On the market, copper cost eighty-one cash for one jin of copper; in private manufacture of thin coin, one jin yielded more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On the market, one jin of copper cost eighty-one cash; in private manufacture of thin coin, one jin yielded more than two hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 既示之以深利，又隨之以重刑，罹罪者雖多，姦鑄者彌眾。

translations.literal: Once deep profit was shown them and heavy punishment followed, though offenders were many, illicit casters grew all the more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Once deep profit was held out to them and heavy punishment followed, though offenders were many, illicit casters grew all the more numerous.

sentences.zh: 今錢徒有五銖之文，而無二銖之實，薄甚榆莢，上貫便破，置之水上，殆欲不沉。

translations.literal: Today the coin bears only the inscription of five zhu yet lacks the substance of even two zhu — thin as elm seedpods, pierced at the top it breaks at once; placed on water it barely sinks.
translations.idiomatic: Today the coin bears only the inscription of five zhu yet lacks the substance of even two zhu — thin as elm seedpods, pierced at the top it breaks at once; placed on water it barely sinks.

sentences.zh: 此乃因循有漸，科防不切，朝廷之愆，彼復何罪。

translations.literal: This is gradual indulgence and inattentive regulation — a fault of the court; what crime is theirs?
translations.idiomatic: This is the result of gradual indulgence and lax enforcement — a fault of the court; what crime is theirs?

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝以五分錢小，改鑄四銖，至武帝復改三銖為半兩。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han, finding the five-fen coin too small, recast it as four zhu; by Emperor Wu's time three zhu was again changed to half-liang.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han, finding the five-fen coin too small, recast it as four zhu; by Emperor Wu's time three zhu was again changed to half-liang.

sentences.zh: 此皆以大易小，以重代輕也。

translations.literal: In each case large was exchanged for small, heavy replaced by light.
translations.idiomatic: In each case large was exchanged for small, heavy replaced by light.

sentences.zh: 論今據古，宜改鑄大錢，文載年號，以記其始，則一斤所成止七十六文。

translations.literal: Applying antiquity to the present, it is fitting to recast large coin, inscribing the reign era to mark its inception — then one jin would yield only seventy-six pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Applying antiquity to the present, it is fitting to recast large coin, inscribing the reign era to mark its inception — then one jin would yield only seventy-six pieces.

sentences.zh: 銅價至賤五十有餘，其中人功、食料、錫炭、鉛沙，縱復私營，不能自潤。

translations.literal: Copper's price would fall to little more than fifty, and among its costs — labor, provisions, tin, charcoal, and lead — even were private enterprise attempted, one could not turn a profit.
translations.idiomatic: Copper's price would fall to little more than fifty, and among its costs — labor, provisions, tin, charcoal, and lead — even private enterprise could not turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 直置無利，自應息心，況復嚴刑廣設也。

translations.literal: With no profit in it, offenders would naturally cease; how much more if strict punishment were widely set in place.
translations.idiomatic: With no profit in it, offenders would naturally cease; how much more if strict punishment were widely enforced.

sentences.zh: 以臣測之，必當錢貨永通，公私獲允。」

translations.literal: By my reckoning, coin and goods would surely flow forever, and public and private alike would be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, coin and goods would surely circulate freely, and public and private interests alike would be satisfied."

sentences.zh: 後遂用楊侃計，鑄永安五銖錢。

translations.literal: Subsequently Yang Kan's plan was adopted, and the Yong'an five-zhu coin was cast.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently Yang Kan's plan was adopted, and the Yong'an five-zhu coin was cast.

sentences.zh: 僕射尒朱世隆當朝權盛，因內見衣冠失儀，道穆便即彈糾。

translations.literal: Vice Director Erzhu Shilong's power in court was great; on entering for an audience his ritual dress was improper, and Daomu immediately impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Erzhu Shilong's power at court was great; when he entered for an audience his ritual dress was improper, and Daomu immediately impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝姊壽陽公主行犯清路，執赤棒卒呵之不止，道穆令卒棒破其車。

translations.literal: The emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Shouyang, violated the cleared road; the soldiers with red staves who seized her did not stop when shouted at, and Daomu ordered the staves to smash her carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Shouyang, violated the cleared road; the soldiers with red staves who seized her did not stop when shouted at, and Daomu ordered them to smash her carriage with their staves.

sentences.zh: 公主深以為恨，泣以訴帝。

translations.literal: The princess deeply resented this and wept as she appealed to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The princess deeply resented this and wept as she appealed to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝謂公主曰：「高中尉清直之人，彼所行者公事，豈可私恨責之也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the princess, "Supervisor Gao is a man upright and fair; what he did was public business — how can you resent him from private feeling?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the princess, "Supervisor Gao is an upright and fair man; what he did was public business — how can you resent him from private feeling?"

sentences.zh: 道穆後見帝，帝曰：「一日家姊行路相犯，極以為愧。」

translations.literal: When Daomu later saw the emperor, the emperor said, "One day my elder sister violated the road — I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daomu later saw the emperor, the emperor said, "One day my elder sister violated the road — I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 道穆免冠謝曰：「臣蒙陛下恩，守陛下法，不敢獨於公主虧朝廷典章，以此負陛下。」
