translations.literal: Daomu removed his cap and apologized: "Your servant receives Your Majesty's grace and upholds Your Majesty's law; I dared not alone relax the court's statutes for the princess's sake — for this I fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Daomu removed his cap and apologized, "Your servant receives Your Majesty's grace and upholds Your Majesty's law; I dared not alone relax the court's statutes for the princess's sake — for this I fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以愧卿，卿反謝朕。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I am ashamed before you, yet you apologize to me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am ashamed before you, yet you apologize to me?"

sentences.zh: 尋敕監儀注。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to supervise ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「祕書圖籍所在，內典□書，又加繕寫，緗素委積，蓋有年載。

translations.literal: Another edict read: "The place of the secretariat's maps and registers, the internal canon and [damaged] books — copying has also been added, and the silk and hemp rolls have piled up for years.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read, "The secretariat's maps and registers, the internal canon and [damaged] texts — copying has also been added, and the silk and hemp rolls have piled up for years.

sentences.zh: 出內繁蕪，多致零落。

translations.literal: When taken out, the proliferation inside leads often to loss and scattering.
translations.idiomatic: When taken out, the internal clutter often leads to loss and scattering.

sentences.zh: 可令御史中尉、兼給事黃門侍郎道穆總集帳目，并牒儒學之士，編比次第。」

translations.literal: Daomu, Censor-in-Chief and Concurrent Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, may be ordered to collect the ledgers in total and, together with memorials to men learned in the classics, arrange them in order."
translations.idiomatic: Daomu, Censor-in-Chief and Concurrent Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, is ordered to collect all ledgers and, together with memorials to scholars of the classics, arrange them in order."

sentences.zh: 道穆又上疏曰：「臣聞舜命臯陶，姦宄是託；

translations.literal: Daomu again submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that Shun appointed Gao Yao and entrusted to him wickedness and wrongdoing;
translations.idiomatic: Daomu again submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that Shun appointed Gao Yao and entrusted to him the punishment of wickedness and wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 禹泣罪人，堯心為念。

translations.literal: Yu wept over guilty men, and Yao's heart was moved with concern.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wept over guilty men, and Yao's heart was moved with concern.

sentences.zh: 所以舉直措枉，事切曩賢；

translations.literal: Therefore to raise the upright and set aside the crooked is a matter dear to sages of old;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to raise the upright and set aside the crooked is a matter dear to sages of old;

sentences.zh: 明德慎罰，議存先典。

translations.literal: to make virtue bright and punishments cautious is a principle preserved in former canons.
translations.idiomatic: to make virtue bright and punishments cautious is a principle preserved in former canons.

sentences.zh: 高祖太和之初，置廷尉司直，論刑辟是非，雖事非古始，交濟時要。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's Taihe reign the Court of Imperial Justice Direct Examiner was established to review the right and wrong of criminal penalties — though the office was not ancient, it met the needs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's Taihe reign the Court of Imperial Justice Direct Examiner was established to review the right and wrong of criminal penalties — though the office was not ancient, it met the needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 所謂禮樂互興，不相沿襲者矣。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by rites and music rising in turn, not following one another blindly.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by rites and music rising in turn, not following one another blindly.

sentences.zh: 臣以無庸，忝當今任，所思報效，未忘寢興。

translations.literal: Your servant, though without talent, unworthily holds the present charge; the service I ponder offering keeps me from rest day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, though without talent, unworthily holds the present charge; the service I ponder offering keeps me from rest day and night.

sentences.zh: 但識謝知今，業慚稽古，未能進一言以利國，說一策以興邦，索米長安，豈不知愧。

translations.literal: Yet my understanding falls short beside knowledge of the present, and my learning shames comparison with investigation of antiquity — I cannot advance one word to benefit the state or offer one stratagem to raise the realm; seeking rice in Chang'an, how could I not know shame?
translations.idiomatic: Yet my understanding falls short beside knowledge of the present, and my learning shames comparison with investigation of antiquity — I cannot advance one word to benefit the state or offer one stratagem to raise the realm; seeking rice in Chang'an, how could I not know shame?

sentences.zh: 至於職司其憂，猶望僶俛。

translations.literal: Yet as to the cares of my office, I still hope to exert myself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as to the cares of my office, I still hope to exert myself to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 竊見御史出使，悉受風聞，雖時獲罪人，亦不無枉濫。

translations.literal: I observe that when censors go out on mission they wholly accept hearsay; though at times culprits are caught, wrongful excess is not absent.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that when censors go out on mission they wholly accept hearsay; though at times culprits are caught, wrongful excess is not absent.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 得堯之罰，不能不怨。

translations.literal: Those who receive Yao's punishment cannot but resent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who receive punishment cannot but resent.

sentences.zh: 守令為政，容有愛憎。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates in government may harbor favor and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates in government may harbor favor and hatred.

sentences.zh: 姦猾之徒，恒思報惡，多有妄造無名，共相誣謗。

translations.literal: Crafty and wicked men always think to repay evil; many falsely invent anonymous charges and mutually slander.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and wicked men always think to repay evil; many falsely invent anonymous charges and mutually slander.

sentences.zh: 御史一經檢究，耻於不成，杖木之下，以虛為實，無罪不能自雪者，豈可勝道哉。

translations.literal: Once a censor launches investigation, ashamed if he does not succeed — under the rods of torture, false becomes true; the innocent who cannot clear themselves — can they be numbered?
translations.idiomatic: Once a censor launches investigation, ashamed if he does not succeed — under the rods of torture, false becomes true; the innocent who cannot clear themselves — can they be numbered?

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚短，守不假器，繡衣所指，冀以清肅。

translations.literal: Your servant, though dull and brief, in office would not borrow another's vessel; where the embroidered cloak points, I hope for cleansing and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, though dull and brief, in office would not borrow another's vessel; where the embroidered cloak points, I hope for cleansing and discipline.

sentences.zh: 若仍踵前失，或傷善人，則尸祿之責，無所逃罪。

translations.literal: If we still follow former errors and harm good men, then the charge of eating salary without work admits no escape from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If we still follow former errors and harm good men, then the charge of eating salary without work admits no escape from guilt.

sentences.zh: 所以夙夜為憂，思有悛革。

translations.literal: Therefore day and night I worry, thinking to reform and change.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore day and night I worry, thinking to reform and change.

sentences.zh: 如臣鄙見，請依太和故事，還置司直十人，名隸廷尉，秩以五品，選歷官有稱，心平性正者為之。

translations.literal: In my humble view, I ask that following the Taihe precedent the Direct Examiner be restored — ten men, nominally under the Court of Imperial Justice, rank of fifth grade, chosen from officials with reputation whose hearts are level and natures upright.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, I ask that following the Taihe precedent the Direct Examiner be restored — ten men, nominally under the Court of Imperial Justice, rank of fifth grade, chosen from officials with reputation whose hearts are level and natures upright.

sentences.zh: 御史若出糾劾，即移廷尉，令知人數。

translations.literal: If a censor goes out to impeach, the case should be transferred to the Court of Imperial Justice, which assigns the number of men.
translations.idiomatic: If a censor goes out to impeach, the case should be transferred to the Court of Imperial Justice, which assigns the number of men.

sentences.zh: 廷尉遣司直與御史俱發，所到州郡，分居別館。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Justice dispatches Direct Examiners to depart with the censor; arriving at each province and commandery, they lodge in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Justice dispatches Direct Examiners to depart with the censor; arriving at each province and commandery, they lodge in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 御史檢了，移付司直覆問，事訖與御史俱還。

translations.literal: When the censor finishes investigation, the file is transferred to the Direct Examiner for review; when the matter is done, both return together.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor finishes investigation, the file is transferred to the Direct Examiner for review; when the matter is done, both return together.

sentences.zh: 中尉彈聞，廷尉科按，一如舊式。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief reports; the Court of Imperial Justice applies the law — all as in the old form.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief reports; the Court of Imperial Justice applies the law — all as in the old form.

sentences.zh: 庶使獄成罪定，無復稽寬；

translations.literal: Thus cases would be settled and guilt fixed, with no further lenient delay;
translations.idiomatic: Thus cases would be settled and guilt fixed, with no further lenient delay;

sentences.zh: 為惡取敗，不得稱枉。

translations.literal: those who do evil and meet ruin could not call themselves wronged.
translations.idiomatic: those who do evil and meet ruin could not call themselves wronged.

sentences.zh: 若御史、司直糾劾失實，悉依所斷獄罪之。

translations.literal: If censor or Direct Examiner impeaches wrongly, each is punished according to the crime of the case judged.
translations.idiomatic: If censor or Direct Examiner impeaches wrongly, each is punished according to the crime of the case judged.

sentences.zh: 聽以所檢，迭相糾發。

translations.literal: They may use what each investigated to impeach the other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They may use what each investigated to impeach the other in turn.

sentences.zh: 如二使阿曲，有不盡理，聽罪家詣門下通訴，別加按檢。

translations.literal: If the two envoys show partiality and do not exhaust reason, the guilty family may go to the Gate Department to petition; separate review shall be added.
translations.idiomatic: If the two envoys show partiality and do not exhaust reason, the guilty family may go to the Gate Department to petition; separate review shall be added.

sentences.zh: 如此，則肺石之傍，怨訟可息；

translations.literal: In this way, beside the Lung-stone, complaints and litigation may cease;
translations.idiomatic: In this way, beside the Lung-stone, complaints and litigation may cease;

sentences.zh: 叢棘之下，受罪吞聲者矣。」

translations.literal: beneath the thorny clump, those who receive punishment will swallow their voices."
translations.idiomatic: beneath the thorny clump, those who receive punishment will swallow their voices."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，復置司直。

translations.literal: An edict approved it, and the Direct Examiner was restored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it, and the Direct Examiner was restored.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮之死也，帝召道穆付赦書，令宣於外。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, the emperor summoned Daomu, handed him the amnesty edict, and ordered him to proclaim it abroad.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, the emperor summoned Daomu, handed him the amnesty edict, and ordered him to proclaim it abroad.

sentences.zh: 因謂之曰：「自今日後，當得精選御史矣。」

translations.literal: He also said to him, "From today onward, censors can truly be carefully selected."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to him, "From today onward, censors can truly be carefully selected."

sentences.zh: 先是，榮等常欲以其親黨為御史，故有此詔。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rong and the others had often wished to appoint their own kinsmen and partisans as censors — hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rong and the others had often wished to appoint their own kinsmen and partisans as censors — hence this edict.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱世隆等率其部類戰於大夏門北，道穆受詔督戰，又贊成太府卿李苗斷橋之計，世隆等於是北遁。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Shilong and the others led their troops to battle north of the Daxia Gate, Daomu received orders to supervise the fighting; he also supported Minister of the Grand Storehouse Li Miao's plan to break the bridge, and Shilong and the others thereupon fled north.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong and the others led their troops to battle north of the Daxia Gate, Daomu received orders to supervise the fighting; he also supported Minister of the Grand Storehouse Li Miao's plan to break the bridge, and Shilong and the others thereupon fled north.

sentences.zh: 加衞將軍、假車騎將軍、大都督、兼尚書右僕射、南道大行臺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Guard, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Commander, Concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Agent of the Southern Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Guard, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Commander, Concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Agent of the Southern Route.

sentences.zh: 又除車騎將軍，餘官如故。

translations.literal: He was also appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry; his other posts remained as before.

sentences.zh: 時雖外託征蠻，而帝恐北軍不利，欲為南巡之計。

translations.literal: Though outwardly the campaign was against the barbarians in the south, the emperor feared the northern army would fail and contemplated a plan to tour south.
translations.idiomatic: Though outwardly the campaign was against the barbarians in the south, the emperor feared the northern army would fail and contemplated a plan to tour south.

sentences.zh: 未發，會尒朱兆入洛，道穆慮禍及己，託病去官。

translations.literal: Before setting out, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Daomu, fearing disaster would reach him, pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Daomu, fearing disaster would reach him, pleaded illness and left office.

sentences.zh: 世隆以道穆忠於前朝，遂害之，時年四十二。

translations.literal: Shilong, because Daomu had been loyal to the former court, then killed him — at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, because Daomu had been loyal to the former court, then killed him — at age forty-two.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，贈使持節、都督雍秦二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Yong and Qin provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Third Rank Equivalent to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Yong and Qin provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Third Rank Equivalent to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 子士鏡，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shi Jing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Jing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Northern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Northern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高仲密擁入關。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi rose in arms and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongmi rose in arms and entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 道穆弟謹之，繼沮渠氏後。

translations.literal: Daomu's younger brother Jinzhi succeeded to the Juqu clan line.
translations.idiomatic: Daomu's younger brother Jinzhi succeeded to the Juqu clan line.

sentences.zh: 卒於滄州平東府主簿，年三十五。

translations.literal: He died as secretary of the Pingdong office in Cangzhou — age thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died as secretary of the Pingdong office in Cangzhou — age thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈通直郎。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted General of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 謹之弟慎之，字道密。

translations.literal: Jinzhi's younger brother Shenzhi, courtesy name Daomi.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhi's younger brother Shenzhi, courtesy name Daomi.

sentences.zh: 好學，有諸兄風。

translations.literal: Fond of study, he had the character of his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of study, he had the character of his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，卒，無子，以兄謙之第二子緒繼焉。

translations.literal: At age twenty-three he died, having no sons; the second son of his elder brother Qianzhi, Xu, succeeded to him.
translations.idiomatic: At age twenty-three he died, having no sons; the second son of his elder brother Qianzhi, Xu, succeeded to him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：宋翻剛鯁自立，猛而斷務。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Song Fan stood firm and upright on his own, fierce and resolute in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Song Fan stood firm and upright on his own, fierce and resolute in affairs.

sentences.zh: 辛雄以吏能歷職，任智效官。

translations.literal: Xin Xiong advanced through office by administrative ability, employing wisdom in service.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong advanced through office by administrative ability, employing wisdom in service.

sentences.zh: 羊深以才幹從事，聲迹可紀。

translations.literal: Yang Shen served with talent and capacity; his repute and deeds are worth record.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen served with talent and capacity; his repute and deeds are worth record.

sentences.zh: 楊機清斷在公。

translations.literal: Yang Ji was clear and decisive in public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji was clear and decisive in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 高崇明濟為用。

translations.literal: Gao Chongming was appointed for practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongming was appointed for practical use.

sentences.zh: 謙之兄弟，咸政事之敏，飾學有聞，列于朝廷，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: The brothers Qianzhi were all sharp in government affairs and famed for cultivating learning; to stand arrayed in court — was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Qianzhi were all sharp in government affairs and famed for cultivating learning; to stand arrayed in court — was it for nothing?

sentences.zh: 深失之晚節，至於顛覆，惜乎！

translations.literal: Shen lost his footing in his later years and came to ruin — a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Shen lost his footing in his later years and came to ruin — a pity!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 北溝求救 按「北溝」不見記載。

translations.literal: "Northern Ditch seeks rescue": Commentary: "Northern Ditch" appears in no other record.
translations.idiomatic: "Northern Ditch seeks rescue": Note: "Northern Ditch" appears in no other record.

sentences.zh: 卷九肅宗紀孝昌元年十二月詔稱「北淯懸危，南陽告急」，即此傳所敍事。

translations.literal: Suzong annals juan 9, decree of the twelfth month, Xiaochang year 1 reads "Northern Yu hangs in peril, Nanyang cries urgent" — that is the affair this biography narrates.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong annals juan 9, decree of the twelfth month, Xiaochang year 1 reads "Northern Yu hangs in peril, Nanyang cries urgent" — that is the affair this biography narrates.

sentences.zh: 「北溝」當是「北淯」之訛。

translations.literal: "Northern Ditch" is likely a corruption of "Northern Yu."
translations.idiomatic: "Northern Ditch" is likely a corruption of "Northern Yu."

sentences.zh: 卷一０六下地形志下荊州有「北清郡」，錢氏考異卷三０據上引肅宗紀及卷七三楊大眼傳以為「清」當作「淯」。

translations.literal: Geography Treatise juan 106B, Jing Province section, lists "Northern Qing Commandery"; Qian's Textual Variants juan 30, citing the Suzong annals above and juan 73 Yang Dayan's biography, holds qing should be yu.
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise juan 106B, Jing Province section, lists "Northern Qing Commandery"; Qian's Textual Variants juan 30, citing the Suzong annals above and juan 73 Yang Dayan's biography, holds qing should be yu.

sentences.zh: 其地在今河南南陽市之北，此傳上文說「裴衍西通鵶路」的第一鵶也即在其地，可證。

translations.literal: The place lies north of present-day Nanyang in Henan; earlier in this biography "Pei Yan opened the E road westward" — the first E was also there, which confirms it.
translations.idiomatic: The place lies north of present-day Nanyang in Henan; earlier in this biography "Pei Yan opened the E road westward" — the first E was also there, which confirms it.

sentences.zh: 若不除煩收疾 冊府卷六五五

translations.literal: "If one does not remove troubles and gather sickness": Cefu juan 655
translations.idiomatic: "If one does not remove troubles and gather sickness": Cefu juan 655

sentences.zh: 〈七八四六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 7846〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈folio 7846〉

sentences.zh: 「收」作「救」，疑是。

translations.literal: "shou" (gather) is written as "jiu" (save/rescue); suspected correct.
translations.idiomatic: shou (gather) appears as jiu (save/rescue); jiu is likely right.

sentences.zh: 東軍不守 冊府卷四一七

translations.literal: "Eastern army does not hold": Cefu juan 417
translations.idiomatic: "Eastern army does not hold": Cefu juan 417

sentences.zh: 〈四九七五頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4975〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈folio 4975〉

translations.literal: "jun" (army) is written as "zhong" (central).
translations.idiomatic: jun (army) appears as zhong (central).

sentences.zh: 按上文稱永安二年元顥攻城，尒朱世隆狼狽退還云云，據卷七五世隆傳稱：「元顥逼大梁，詔假儀同三司、前軍都督，鎮虎牢。」

translations.literal: Commentary: Above it says in Yong'an year 2 Yuan Hao besieged the city and Erzhu Shilong fled in disarray, etc. According to juan 75 Shilong's biography: "Yuan Hao pressed Daliang; [Shilong] was ordered Acting Third Rank Equivalent, Forward Army Commander-in-Chief, to guard Hulao."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Above it says in Yong'an year 2 Yuan Hao besieged the city and Erzhu Shilong fled in disarray, etc. According to juan 75 Shilong's biography: "Yuan Hao pressed Daliang; [Shilong] was ordered Acting Third Rank Equivalent, Forward Army Commander-in-Chief, to guard Hulao."

sentences.zh: 下文又說纂「還鎮虎牢」，知辛纂所守之城即虎牢。

translations.literal: Below it again says Zuan "returned to garrison Hulao" — knowing the city that Xin Zuan defended was Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Below it again says Zuan "returned to garrison Hulao" — knowing the city that Xin Zuan defended was Hulao.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六地形志中北豫州條，云太和十九年於虎牢置「東中府」。

translations.literal: Geography Treatise juan 106, Northern Yuzhou entry, states that in Taihe year 19 the "Eastern Central Prefecture" was established at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise juan 106, Northern Yuzhou entry, states that in Taihe year 19 the "Eastern Central Prefecture" was established at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 這裏「軍」當是「中」之訛。

translations.literal: Here jun (army) is likely a corruption of zhong (central).
translations.idiomatic: Here jun (army) is likely a corruption of zhong (central).

sentences.zh: 又上記辛纂官「平東將軍、中郎將」，「中郎將」上亦當有「東」字。

translations.literal: Again, above Xin Zuan's titles are "General Who Pacifies the East, Leader of Cadet Gentlemen" — before zhonglangjiang (Leader of Cadet Gentlemen) there should also be the character dong (east).
translations.idiomatic: Again, above Xin Zuan's titles are "General Who Pacifies the East, Leader of Cadet Gentlemen" — before zhonglangjiang (Leader of Cadet Gentlemen) there should also be the character dong (east).

sentences.zh: 父敬宗 北史卷五０辛雄傳附辛琛作「祖敬宗，父樹寶」。

translations.literal: Father Jingzong. In the Xin Xiong biography appended in Beishi 50, Xin Chen reads "grandfather Jingzong, father Shubao."
translations.idiomatic: Father Jingzong. In the appended Xin Xiong biography in Beishi, vol. 50, Xin Chen has "grandfather Jingzong, father Shubao."

sentences.zh: 按元和姓纂輯本卷三辛氏稱「敬宗曾孫術」，術即琛子，又唐書卷七三上宰相世系表也是敬宗、樹寶、琛分列三代，當是此傳脫去「樹寶」，「父敬宗」亦當作「祖敬宗」。

translations.literal: According to the collated Yuanhe xingzuan, vol. 3, Xin clan, it says "Jingzong's great-grandson Shu"; Shu was Chen's son. The Tang shu, vol. 73A, Tables of Chancellor Lineages, likewise lists Jingzong, Shubao, and Chen across three generations. This biography must have dropped "Shubao," and "father Jingzong" should read "grandfather Jingzong."
translations.idiomatic: The collated Yuanhe xingzuan, vol. 3 (Xin clan), calls Shu "Jingzong's great-grandson"; Shu was Chen's son. The Tang shu tables of chancellor lineages (73A) likewise arrange Jingzong, Shubao, and Chen in three generations. This passage has evidently dropped Shubao, and "father Jingzong" should be "grandfather Jingzong."

sentences.zh: 子懿 北史卷五０辛雄傳末「懿」作「慤」。

translations.literal: Son Yi. At the end of the Xin Xiong biography in Beishi 50, "Yi" reads "Que."
translations.idiomatic: Son Yi. At the end of the Xin Xiong biography in Beishi, vol. 50, "Yi" appears as "Que."

sentences.zh: 按辛慤見北齊書卷四三源彪傳、元和姓纂輯本卷三、唐書卷七三上宰相世系表。

translations.literal: Xin Que appears in Beiqishu 43 (biography of Yuan Biao appended), Yuanhe xingzuan collated vol. 3, and Tang shu 73A.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Que is attested in Beiqishu 43 (Yuan Biao biography), the collated Yuanhe xingzuan, vol. 3, and Tang shu 73A.

sentences.zh: 據姓纂，懿乃慤六世祖，不應同名。

translations.literal: According to the xingzuan, Yi was Que's sixth-generation ancestor; they should not share the same name.
translations.idiomatic: According to the lineage compendium, Yi was Que's sixth-generation ancestor; the same name is impossible.

sentences.zh: 這裏「懿」當是「慤」之訛。

translations.literal: Here "Yi" must be a corruption for "Que."
translations.idiomatic: Here "Yi" is surely a scribal error for "Que."

sentences.zh: 太山平陽人 殿本考證云：「按北史羊祉傳

translations.literal: A native of Pingyang in Taishan. The Dianben kaozheng says: "According to the Yang Zhi biography in Beishi
translations.idiomatic: "Native of Pingyang, Taishan." The Dianben kaozheng notes: "According to the Yang Zhi biography in Beishi

sentences.zh: 〈卷三九〉
祉太山鉅平人。

translations.literal: Zhi was a native of Juping in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was from Juping in Taishan.

sentences.zh: 本書地形志

translations.literal: The Geography Treatise in this book
translations.idiomatic: The Geography Treatise of this work

sentences.zh: 〈卷一０六中〉

translations.literal: 〈vol. 106, middle〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈vol. 106, middle〉

sentences.zh: 泰山郡有鉅平，若平陽則屬高平郡，又有陽平，則屬魯郡，當以鉅平為是。」

translations.literal: Taishan commandery had Juping; if Pingyang, it would belong to Gaoping commandery, and if Yangping, to Lu commandery—Juping must be correct."
translations.idiomatic: Taishan commandery included Juping; Pingyang would belong to Gaoping, and Yangping to Lu—Juping is correct."

sentences.zh: 按本書卷八八良吏羊敦傳、卷八九酷吏羊祉傳並云「太山鉅平人」。

translations.literal: According to this book 88 (good official Yang Dun) and 89 (harsh official Yang Zhi), both say "native of Juping, Taishan."
translations.idiomatic: This book's biographies of the good official Yang Dun (88) and the harsh official Yang Zhi (89) both read "native of Juping, Taishan."

sentences.zh: 羊氏本泰山南城人，羊祜封鉅平侯，後人或稱鉅平，或稱梁父，這裏「平陽」當誤。

translations.literal: The Yang clan were originally from Nancheng in Taishan; Yang Hu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Juping, and later people sometimes said Juping, sometimes Liangfu—here "Pingyang" must be an error.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang were originally from Nancheng in Taishan; Yang Hu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Juping, and descendants used either Juping or Liangfu—"Pingyang" here is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 正平薛鳳賢等聚眾作逆 諸本「正」作「王」，北史卷三九羊祉附羊深傳大德本作「正」，百衲本從他本改「王」。

translations.literal: Xue Fengxian of Zhengping and others gathered a crowd in rebellion. In various editions "Zheng" reads "Wang"; in the Yang Shen biography appended to Yang Zhi in Beishi 39 the Dade edition has "Zheng," while the Baipu edition follows other texts in changing it to "Wang."
translations.idiomatic: "Xue Fengxian of Zhengping and others raised a rebel band." Various editions read "Wang" for "Zheng"; in Beishi 39 (Yang Shen appended to Yang Zhi) the Dade text has "Zheng," but the Baipu edition follows others in emending to "Wang."

sentences.zh: 按通志卷一四九羊深傳也作「正」，知北史本是「正」字。

translations.literal: According to Tongzhi 149 (Yang Shen biography), it also reads "Zheng," showing the Beishi text originally had "Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 149 likewise has "Zheng," confirming the Beishi reading.

sentences.zh: 本書卷一０六上地形志上東雍州有正平郡。

translations.literal: Geography Treatise 106A lists Zhengping commandery under Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise 106A places Zhengping commandery under Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 薛鳳賢於正平起事，見本書卷二五、北史卷二二長孫道生附長孫稚傳。

translations.literal: Xue Fengxian's uprising at Zhengping appears in this book 25 and Beishi 22 (Changsun Daosheng, appended Changsun Zhi biography).
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengxian's revolt at Zhengping is recorded in this book, vol. 25, and Beishi 22 (Changsun Zhi, appended to Changsun Daosheng).

sentences.zh: 〈北史避唐諱「稚」作「幼」。〉

translations.literal: 〈Beishi avoids the Tang taboo on "Zhi" by writing "You."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Beishi avoids the Tang taboo on Zhi by writing You.〉

sentences.zh: 「王」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "Wang" is corrupt; emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang" is a corruption; the text is emended to "Zheng."

sentences.zh: 憚比刑書 北史卷五０高道穆附高謙之傳「比」作「此」，疑是。

translations.literal: Feared comparison with the penal code. In Beishi 50 (Gao Daomu, appended Gao Qianzhi), "comparison" reads "this"—possibly correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Feared comparison with the penal code." In Beishi 50 (Gao Qianzhi appended to Gao Daomu), bi ("comparison") appears as ci ("this")—possibly the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 刺史李世哲即尚書令崇之子 北史卷五０高道穆傳「刺史」上有「前」字。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Li Shizhe was the son of Director Li Chong. In Beishi 50 (Gao Daomu biography), "provincial governor" is preceded by "former."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Li Shizhe was the son of Director Li Chong. Beishi 50 (Gao Daomu) has "former" before "provincial governor."

sentences.zh: 按卷六六李崇附李世哲傳，世哲此時已徵為兼太常卿，疑此傳脫「前」字。

translations.literal: According to 66 (Li Chong, appended Li Shizhe), Shizhe had by then been summoned as concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; this biography may have dropped "former."
translations.idiomatic: Per vol. 66 (Li Shizhe appended to Li Chong), Shizhe had already been recalled as concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; "former" may have dropped from this passage.

sentences.zh: 與薛曇尚書使晉陽 按薛曇尚，附卷四四薛野䐗傳，這時他以司徒左長史兼吏部尚書出使晉陽，授尒朱榮官。

translations.literal: With Xue Tanshang, Director, as envoy to Jinyang. Xue Tanshang is treated in 44 (Xue Yegou appended); at this time he went to Jinyang as chief steward of the left in the Secretariat and concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs to confer offices on Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: "With Xue Tanshang, Director, as envoy to Jinyang." Xue Tanshang appears in vol. 44 (appended to Xue Yegou); he was then chief steward of the left and concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs, sent to Jinyang to invest Erzhu Rong with office.

sentences.zh: 疑「書」字衍。

translations.literal: The character "Director" (shu) may be redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The character shu ("Director") may be superfluous.

sentences.zh: 但「曇尚」也可單稱「曇」，「尚書」作官名連讀，亦可通，今仍之。

translations.literal: But "Tanshang" can be abbreviated as "Tan," and reading "Director" as an official title also works—the text is retained as is.
translations.idiomatic: Yet "Tanshang" may be shortened to "Tan," and reading shangshu as the office title is also possible—the text is left unchanged.
